docs.title: CVE-2026-105299 — Pingora: HTTP/1 Upstream Path Forwards Client-Controlled Hop-by-Hop Headers
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.7 Product pingora-proxy before 0.9.0 — HTTP/1 upstream path (upstream_request_filter flow) Type Improper removal of hop-by-hop headers (CWE-1132) Vector Network, low complexity, no privileges, no user interaction → attacker-nominated headers pass through to chained intermediaries and strip application-added security headers; affects chained deployments where an HTTP/1 intermediary between Pingora and the origin honors Connection (e.g. Go's net/http)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: • pingora-proxy before 0.9.0. Fixed in 0.9.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The HTTP/1 upstream path passes the downstream request through upstream_request_filter and writes it upstream without removing the client's Connection header, other hop-by-hop headers, or the headers Connection nominates — even though RFC 9110 §7.6.1 requires intermediaries to strip them. The HTTP/2 upstream path already removed Connection and related HTTP/1-specific headers; the HTTP/1 path was simply missed.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern (before 0.9.0)
fn send_upstream(req: &Request) {
    let req = upstream_request_filter(req);   // app adds X-Forwarded-For here
    upstream.write(req);                      // Connection + nominated headers still present!
}

// Simplified fixed pattern (0.9.0)
fn send_upstream(req: &Request) {
    let mut req = upstream_request_filter(req);
    req.strip_hop_by_hop();                   // Connection and nominated headers removed
    upstream.write(req);
}

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. The attacker sends a request with Connection: X-Forwarded-For.
  2. Pingora's filter adds the real client IP in X-Forwarded-For, then forwards the unmodified Connection header upstream.
  3. A chained HTTP/1 intermediary between Pingora and the origin honors Connection and strips X-Forwarded-For.
  4. The origin receives no client-IP header — IP allowlists, rate limits and geo rules go blind.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a proxy that forgets to strip hop-by-hop headers versus one that does, against purely synthetic offline requests. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade pingora-proxy to 0.9.0 or later — the only real fix.
  • Audit chained intermediaries between Pingora and the origin; ensure each hop strips hop-by-hop headers per RFC 9110 §7.6.1.
  • Never trust client-IP headers across untrusted hops — validate X-Forwarded-For only from your own edge.
  • Test the header path in staging: send Connection-nominated headers and confirm the origin never sees them.

docs.title: Kubernetes Console Operator: Tenant Image + Cluster Keys = Cross-Tenant Kafka Takeover
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.9 (v3.1) Product Kubernetes Console operator for Strimzi (Red Hat) Type Improper privilege management (CWE-269) — tenant-controlled image runs under cluster-wide ServiceAccount Vector Kubernetes tenant with create permission on Console custom resources sets spec.containers.api.spec.image to an arbitrary image → operator deploys it in a pod whose ServiceAccount is bound (ClusterRoleBinding) to cluster-wide Strimzi get/list/watch + patch → attacker's code reads the projected SA token → cross-tenant control plane access

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Strimzi Console operator versions per Red Hat advisory. Apply the vendor fix; restrict Console CR creation meanwhile.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The operator lets a tenant name the container image in a Console custom resource, then schedules that image with a ServiceAccount bound via ClusterRoleBinding to a ClusterRole granting cluster-wide get/list/watch on all Strimzi CRDs (including KafkaUsers), patch on Kafkas and KafkaRebalances, plus cluster-monitoring-view. Untrusted input (the image) meets a trusted identity (the SA):

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
spec:
  containers:
    api:
      spec:
        image: attacker-controlled   # tenant chooses the image...
# ...and the operator runs it as a ServiceAccount with cluster-wide Strimzi
# get/list/watch + patch. The attacker's code reads the projected SA token.

# Simplified fixed pattern: the operator pins its own image and the binding
# grants only the namespaces the tenant legitimately manages.
spec:
  containers:
    api:
      spec:
        image: operator-pinned:v1.2.3   # tenant cannot choose
One YAML file, and the attacker's container lists Kafka users across every tenant.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. Tenant with Console CR create permission applies a resource pointing spec.containers.api.spec.image at a malicious image.
  2. The operator pulls and runs it with the over-privileged ServiceAccount.
  3. The attacker's code reads the projected SA token from the pod.
  4. With cluster-wide Strimzi read+write, they control Kafka clusters, users, and rebalances across tenants.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: Operators must never run tenant-chosen images under elevated identities: pin images server-side and bind least privilege. Offline, no server, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Apply the Red Hat fix for CVE-2026-105312 immediately.
  • Restrict who can create Console custom resources; audit running console pods for unexpected images.
  • Redesign the operator binding to least privilege; rotate anything the SA token could reach.

docs.title: CVE-2026-105482 — Node.js DNS: Invisible NUL Byte Silently Defeats Domain Allowlists
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.4 (v3.1) Product Node.js — 26.x, 24.x, 22.x before the October 2026 security releases Type Improper check or handling of exceptional conditions (CWE-703/CWE-284) — NUL-byte truncation in DNS resolution Vector Attacker registers attacker.example → hands the app the hostname attacker.exampletrusted.example → the app's allowlist sees trusted.example and approves → dns.resolve*()/dns.reverse() pass the name to c-ares as a C string, which silently truncates at the NUL → the app resolves and connects to attacker.example

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Node.js 26.x, 24.x, 22.x. Fixed in 22.23.4, 24.22.1, 26.12.1. (Incomplete fix of CVE-2026-48930, which only covered dns.lookup() and the net/tls host options.)

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The name crossed a representation boundary: JavaScript strings can contain NUL bytes, but the C library underneath treats NUL as end-of-string. Validation happened on the full JS string while resolution happened on the truncated C string. In real DNS a NUL byte is just another legal label character, so the validator and the resolver acted on two different names - with no error raised anywhere.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The vulnerable pattern, simplified:

// VULNERABLE - allowlist sees the full string, resolver sees the prefix
const host = "attacker.example\0.trusted.example";
if (allowlistAllows(host)) {            // sees "...trusted.example" -> OK
  dns.resolve4(host, cb);               // c-ares gets "attacker.example"
}

// FIXED - reject control bytes before any validation or resolution
if (/[\0-\x1f]/.test(host)) throw new Error("invalid hostname");

The demo poc.py below models the truncation with synthetic strings - no DNS lookups are performed.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Update Node.js to 22.23.4, 24.22.1, or 26.12.1. As defense in depth, reject hostnames containing NUL or other control bytes before validating or resolving them, and treat surprising DNS answers as hostile.

docs.title: CVE-2026-105483-group — Node.js TLS Hostname Verification Bypassed by Sneaky IP Spellings (2 CVEs)
docs.text:
Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.4 (v3.0) x2 Product Node.js — 26.x, 24.x, 22.x before the October 2026 security releases Type Improper certificate validation (CWE-295) — hostname verification mismatch Vector Attacker obtains a certificate with a numeric DNS SAN (no IP SAN needed) → victim connects to a non-canonical IP spelling (fullwidth digits, leading-zero octal, hex/decimal forms) → tls.checkServerIdentity() normalizes the host differently from the OS resolver → the certificate is validated against the wrong name and accepted → man in the middle on the encrypted connection

Covers CVE-2026-105483 (fullwidth-digit host not recognized as IP), CVE-2026-106069 (leading-zero octet read as octal by URL rules but decimal by the OS).

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Node.js 26.x, 24.x, 22.x (varies per CVE). Fixed in 22.23.4, 24.22.1, 26.12.1.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Two parsers disagreed on what the hostname was. tls.checkServerIdentity() applied its own normalization (WHATWG URL rules, Unicode handling) while the actual connection went through the operating system resolver. A host like 0127.0.0.1 was validated as one IP (87.0.0.1, octal) while the socket connected to another (127.0.0.1, decimal). Identity checks are only meaningful when the checked identity and the connected identity are the same string.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The vulnerable pattern, simplified:

// VULNERABLE - normalization disagrees with the resolver
const host = "0127.0.0.1";            // user-supplied
const checked = urlNormalize(host);   // -> 87.0.0.1 (octal)
const connected = osResolve(host);    // -> 127.0.0.1 (decimal, e.g. macOS)
tls.checkServerIdentity(checked, cert); // cert for 87.0.0.1 accepted...
// ...but the socket talks to 127.0.0.1

// FIXED - canonicalize strictly, reject ambiguous spellings
const ip = strictParseIP(host);       // throws on non-canonical forms
tls.checkServerIdentity(ip, cert);

The demo poc.py below models the parser-disagreement with synthetic data - no TLS, no network, no certificates involved.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Update Node.js to 22.23.4, 24.22.1, or 26.12.1 (matching your release line). Audit outbound TLS connections that target IP literals, and reject non-canonical host spellings at input validation time.

docs.title: CVE-2026-105769 — Azure Token Leak to Attacker Registries in kaniko
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL — CVSS 9.3 Product kaniko, all versions before 1.25.20 Type Token Disclosure / Improper Validation (CWE-346, CWE-522) Vector Network, low complexity, requires a crafted Dockerfile reference, no user interaction

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• kaniko versions before 1.25.20.
  • Fixed in 1.25.20 and later.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: kaniko consults the Azure Container Registry credential helper for registries without Docker config credentials. The helper decides whether a host is an ACR registry with an unanchored regular expression, so any hostname merely containing .azurecr.io (or .azurecr.cn, .azurecr.de, .azurecr.us) is accepted. A Dockerfile referencing an image on a lookalike host such as x.azurecr.io.attacker.com makes the helper fetch the build's Azure identity token and POST it to the attacker's server. No RUN instruction or push is required.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text: See poc.py: a local illustration of an unanchored suffix check accepting a lookalike hostname, contrasted with an exact-host allowlist check that rejects it. No tokens, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update kaniko to 1.25.20 or later immediately.
  • Scope build identities to the least privilege needed.
  • Review Dockerfiles and base images for unfamiliar registries.
  • Rotate any Azure credentials that may have been exposed to untrusted builds.

docs.title: Adobe Campaign Classic: perfect-10 SQL injection gives code execution (CVE-2026-105781 and APSB26-162 batch)
docs.text: Educational writeup only. The proof of concept below is conceptual and demonstrates the flaw in a controlled lab. Do not use it against systems you do not own.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL 10.0 (CVSS) — CVE-2026-105781 Product Adobe Campaign Classic (ACC) Type SQL injection (CWE-89), code injection (CWE-94), OS command injection (CWE-78), incorrect authorization (CWE-863) Vector Network — no user interaction required for the headline flaws Batch CVEs CVE-2026-105781 (10.0, SQL injection), CVE-2026-104351 (9.9, code injection), CVE-2026-104353 (9.9, OS command injection), CVE-2026-105489 (9.9, SQL injection), CVE-2026-105780 (9.9, incorrect authorization), CVE-2026-105779 (9.1, SQL injection), CVE-2026-104354 (9.1, SQL injection), CVE-2026-104350 (9.3, reflected cross-site scripting) Fixed in Adobe security update APSB26-162 for Campaign Classic

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Adobe Campaign Classic versions covered by APSB26-162. A low-privileged attacker can reach the vulnerable functions over the network, and the headline SQL injection needs no user interaction: crafted input is built straight into database commands, giving elevated access and code execution in the Campaign environment, with customer data and campaign operations at risk.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The application treated user input as instructions instead of data. A query built by pasting input straight into SQL cannot tell where the real query ends and the attacker begins. The same batch shows the pattern repeated: code generation, operating system commands, and authorization decisions all trusted attacker-controlled input without a boundary between data and command.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual, educational only)
docs.text:
See poc.py. It shows, against your own lab deployment only:

  1. The vulnerable pattern: user input pasted directly into a query string, so injected SQL changes what the database runs.
  2. The fixed pattern: parameterized queries, where input is always data, never part of the command.
  3. What a successful attack gains: elevated access, arbitrary SQL execution, and code execution in the Campaign environment.

No working exploit is provided — only the query construction and the vulnerable-vs-fixed pattern.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Install Adobe security update APSB26-162 for Campaign Classic immediately.
  • Audit your Campaign instance for suspicious queries, accounts, and campaign changes.
  • Restrict Campaign access to trusted users and networks.
  • Rotate any credentials the Campaign instance could reach.
  • Monitor Campaign logs after patching for follow-on activity.

docs.title: CVE-2026-105944 — Apache Pulsar Manager: Open Admin Creation Hands Out Superuser Accounts
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 10.0 (v4.0) Product Apache Pulsar Manager — the web console for administering Apache Pulsar clusters Type Missing authentication for critical function (CWE-306) — the initial-administrator creation endpoint stays reachable without authentication, and proxied admin-API requests run with the console's own privileged credential Vector Unauthenticated remote attacker reaches the console → calls the open user-creation endpoint → mints a superuser account → logs in → full control of the Pulsar cluster (plus the console proxies admin API calls with its configured credential to an attacker-chosen destination)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Pulsar Manager 0.3.0 and later (admin-creation issue); proxied-request issue affects 0.2.0 behavior as described. Upgrade to the patched release from the Apache Pulsar security page.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The user-creation operation for the initial administrator was never gated behind authentication and remained available after initialization, so any network-reachable console would accept new superuser accounts. Separately, admin-API requests proxied through the console were not subject to the console's authentication and carried the console's configured cluster credential toward a requester-chosen destination.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo contrasts create_admin_vulnerable() (no auth check) with create_admin_fixed() (requires a valid session token) plus a proxied-request guard.

The poc.py file next to this writeup demonstrates the vulnerable pattern versus the fixed pattern as a safe, offline logic demo — no network, no shell, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade now to the patched Pulsar Manager release.
  • Audit every exposed admin console; assume exposed ones are compromised and rotate credentials.
  • Rotate the credential the console uses against the Pulsar cluster.
  • Keep admin consoles on a private network behind authentication, never on the public internet.

docs.title: CVE-2026-106013 — WordPress Jupiter X Core: X Social Login Verifies the Wrong Token
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 Product WordPress plugin Jupiter X Core — theme companion for the Jupiter X theme, incl. social login Type Authentication bypass (CWE-287) — social login handler verifies the site operator's token instead of the visitor's Vector Visitor starts an X (Twitter) social login → plugin exchanges the code for the visitor's token but never attaches it → verification runs with the site operator's stored token → login succeeds as the operator/admin

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Jupiter X Core up to and including 4.61.0. Update past 4.61.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
After exchanging the visitor's authorization code for an access token, the handler never reassigns that token to the API client. The verification call therefore still carries the site operator's stored credentials, and every visitor verifies as the operator:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def verify_login(visitor_code):
    visitor_token = exchange(visitor_code)
    # BUG: visitor_token never attached to the client
    return verify_with(site_owner_token)  # always the operator

# Simplified fixed pattern
def verify_login_fixed(visitor_code):
    visitor_token = exchange(visitor_code)
    client.set_token(visitor_token)       # visitor's own credentials
    return verify_with(visitor_token)
Identity checks must use the credentials of the person logging in — never a stored operator credential.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
1. Attacker starts a normal X social login on the site.
  2. The plugin exchanges the code but keeps the operator's token on the client.
  3. Verification succeeds against the operator's identity.
  4. The attacker receives a session with the operator's privileges.

See poc.py for a safe, offline demo of checking the wrong identity: the demo contrasts verifying with a stored operator token against verifying with the visitor's own token.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update now: Jupiter X Core past 4.61.0.
  • Review administrator sessions for unknown logins.
  • Disable social login until patched if you cannot update yet.
  • Audit new admin accounts created around the time of exposure.

docs.title: CVE-2026-107188 — Eptura Archibus: Unauthenticated File Upload to RCE (3-Bug Chain)
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.6 (CVSS 3.1) Product Eptura Archibus (workplace management) Type Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type (CWE-434), chained with authentication bypass and database read Vector 3-bug chain disclosed together by Rapid7: DWR auth bypass (CVE-2026-107186) + arbitrary database read (CVE-2026-107187) + unrestricted file upload (CVE-2026-107188) — combined they yield unauthenticated remote code execution

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Eptura Archibus before 2025.02. Fixed in 2025.02 (the vulnerable DWR method was moved to a REST API).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Three weaknesses combine into one exploit chain. First, CVE-2026-107186 (CVSS 8.6): a Direct Web Remoting request with isPasswordUppercase as one call method and run-workflow-rule as the next runs workflow rules with no login — an authentication bypass. Second, CVE-2026-107187 (CVSS 8.5): a DWR request specifying a workflow rule reads any database details, including usernames and passwords — chainable with the bypass, still no login. Third, CVE-2026-107188 (CVSS 9.6): the report-export upload accepts any file contents with any extension, so uploading JSP code as .jspx and browsing to it makes the server execute it. Chained with the bypass, an unauthenticated attacker gets RCE.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. Attacker sends an unauthenticated DWR request chaining isPasswordUppercase with run-workflow-rule — workflow rules run with no login (CVE-2026-107186).
  2. With that bypass, a second DWR request reads database credentials outright (CVE-2026-107187).
  3. Attacker uploads export-report files with any contents and any extension — JSP code as .jspx (CVE-2026-107188).
  4. Browsing to the uploaded file makes the server execute it — unauthenticated RCE.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a vulnerable mock versus the fixed pattern. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Upgrade to Eptura Archibus 2025.02 or later — all prior versions are affected. Rotate all credentials in the database (usernames/passwords were readable). Audit uploaded export files for unexpected extensions or contents.

docs.title: CVE-2026-107327 — Langflow Missing Authorization Leads to Remote Code Execution
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL 9.9 Product IBM Langflow OSS Type Missing Authorization (CWE-862); siblings: Code Injection (CWE-94) Vector Network, low privileges, no user interaction

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.12.4. Sibling flaws in the same disclosure wave: CVE-2026-107328 (code in eval/exec), CVE-2026-107329 (code generation control), CVE-2026-104339 and CVE-2026-110186 (code generation / OS command).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Langflow fails to enforce authorization on code execution features. An authenticated user can reach the flow code execution path without proving they are allowed to use it, and related endpoints do not properly neutralize code passed through evaluation and generation paths. The result is arbitrary code execution as the Langflow service process.

docs.title: Proof of concept

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade Langflow past version 1.12.4 immediately.
  • Until patched, keep Langflow off the public internet and restrict it to trusted networks.
  • Restrict who can create and run flows; audit recent flows for suspicious code.
  • Review API keys, model credentials, and stored workflows for exposure.

docs.title: CVE-2026-107366 — Langflow: Any Authenticated User Can Delete, Rewrite, or Hijack Anyone's AI Chat Messages
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.3 Product Langflow OSS (langflowai/langflow) Type Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key (CWE-639) Vector Authenticated (low-privilege) → network, no user interaction

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.12.4. Fixed in 1.12.6 (security backports from 1.13.0).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Three message API endpoints accept a session_id or message_id from the request and operate on the referenced messages without verifying that the caller owns them. Authentication confirms who is calling, but nothing checks whether the message or session belongs to that user — a classic broken object-level authorization (BOLA) flaw. Supplying the identifier alone is treated as proof of ownership.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
msg = db.get(request.msg_id)   # attacker-controlled key, trusted blindly
msg.delete()                   # no ownership check

# Fixed pattern
msg = db.get(request.msg_id)
assert msg.owner == current_user  # tie every object to its owner

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. An authenticated low-privilege user obtains another user's session_id.
  2. They send a message delete/update request carrying the victim's session ID.
  3. The endpoint trusts the ID — messages are bulk-deleted, content is overwritten with malicious prompts that poison AI replies, or the session ID is reassigned so the attacker inherits the whole conversation.

The accompanying poc.py in this folder demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock message store showing an ownership-blind handler versus a fixed handler that ties every message to its owner. It runs entirely offline against synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Langflow to 1.12.6 or later immediately.
  • Restrict account creation to trusted users; Langflow's docs note tenant isolation is the operator's responsibility.
  • Never expose Langflow directly to the open internet; put authentication and an allow-list in front of it.
  • Audit message/session logs for requests carrying session IDs that don't belong to the caller, and rotate API keys on any instance that was exposed.

docs.title: CVE-2026-107436 — Strong Testimonials: PHP Object Injection Through Review Data
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.8 Product Strong Testimonials WordPress reviews plugin Type Deserialization of Untrusted Data (CWE-502) Vector Unauthenticated, network → code execution via gadget chain (triggered at render time)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Strong Testimonials through 3.3.12. Fixed in versions past 3.3.12.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The plugin stores review data in serialized form and rebuilds it with PHP's unserialize() on every page view — from input the attacker can influence, with no signature or integrity check. unserialize() does not just parse data: it instantiates whatever classes the bytes describe and runs their magic methods (__wakeup, __destruct, …) on the server.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
$stored = get_from_database();  // attacker-influenced review data
$review = unserialize($stored); // live objects rebuilt, methods fire

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker crafts a serialized payload that chains together gadget classes already present in WordPress — a POP chain — and gets it into the data the plugin unserializes.
  2. A visitor (or the attacker) loads any page that renders testimonials.
  3. At render time the plugin unserializes the payload; the gadget chain fires, running the attacker's logic with the web server's privileges.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock review store whose vulnerable renderer instantiates attacker-named classes from a payload, versus the fixed renderer that only accepts plain data and rejects class markers. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

Depending on the gadgets available, the impact ranges from rewriting site options and planting files to full remote code execution — and every page view that renders testimonials can re-trigger it.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Strong Testimonials past 3.3.12 immediately.
  • Audit wp_options for unexpected changes (siteurl, admin users, active plugins).
  • Scan uploads and plugin folders for unfamiliar files.
  • Prefer json_decode() over unserialize() for stored data, and sign anything that must round-trip through storage.

docs.title: CVE-2026-107656 — FortiSandbox: Authentication Bypass in the Web GUI
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 (v3.1) Product Fortinet FortiSandbox (appliance and PaaS) — malware sandboxing appliance Type Authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel (CWE-288) Vector A remote, unauthenticated attacker sends crafted HTTP requests to an alternate path in the FortiSandbox web management interface. That path does not enforce authentication, so the request reaches protected functions and the attacker can execute unauthorized code or commands on the appliance. No account, no login, no user interaction.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• FortiSandbox 5.0.0 through 5.0.6 — fixed in 5.0.7
  • FortiSandbox 4.4.0 through 4.4.9 — fixed in 4.4.10
  • FortiSandbox 4.2 all versions
  • FortiSandbox PaaS 5.0.0 through 5.0.6 — fixed in 5.0.7
  • FortiSandbox PaaS 4.4 all versions and 4.2 all versions — migrate to a fixed release
  • FortiSandbox 5.2 is not affected

Fortinet reports this vulnerability as not known to be exploited.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Authentication was enforced on the main management routes but not on an alternate path that reaches the same protected functions. A security check that covers only the front door is decorative: any unguarded route into the same functionality bypasses the whole login system.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. Attacker locates an internet- or network-reachable FortiSandbox management interface.
  2. Attacker sends a crafted HTTP request to the alternate path.
  3. The request skips authentication and reaches a protected function.
  4. The appliance executes the attacker's unauthorized code or commands.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a route table where one path forgets to require authentication (vulnerable) versus a table where every path requires it (fixed). Offline, no appliance, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade now: FortiSandbox 5.0.7 or 4.4.10 (or move to 5.2); PaaS 4.4/4.2 users migrate to a fixed release.
  • Restrict the management interface to trusted admin networks; never expose it to the internet.
  • Enforce multi-factor authentication for administrator accounts.
  • Review appliance logs for requests to unexpected paths.

docs.title: CVE-2026-107685 - req_llm WebSocket Skips TLS Certificate Verification
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL 9.1 Product agentjido req_llm (Elixir LLM client), before fix commits a389d71 and c7264fc Weakness CWE-295 Improper Certificate Validation Attack vector Network (on-path)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: All versions of req_llm before the fix commits a389d71 and c7264fc. The OpenAI Responses, Realtime, and Codex WebSocket paths reach the vulnerable client. HTTP streaming (Finch) and the HTTP/2 duplex session (Mint) verify certificates and are not affected.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: ReqLLM.Streaming.WebSocketSession.Client.start/3 (lib/req_llm/streaming/web_socket_session/client.ex) starts WebSockex without any TLS options. WebSockex defaults to insecure mode (verify none), so the client accepts any server certificate, including attacker-forged ones. Additionally, the option allowlist silently drops caller-supplied certificate or SSL options, so an application cannot opt into verification. Encrypted TLS is therefore established with an unverified peer, and the authorization bearer token is sent straight through the attacker's connection.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual, educational only)
docs.text:
An on-path attacker runs a transparent proxy that terminates the victim's WebSocket TLS handshake with a self-signed certificate:

  1. Victim app opens a WebSocket to the OpenAI streaming endpoint.
  2. Attacker's proxy intercepts the handshake and presents a forged certificate.
  3. The req_llm client never validates it, so the connection proceeds through the attacker.
  4. The proxy forwards traffic while logging the authorization header containing the API key or OAuth token.
  5. The attacker replays the stolen token against the real API for quota abuse, session reading, or stream tampering.

The illustrative snippet below shows the config contrast (pseudo-Elixir, not a working exploit):

# VULNERABLE (before fix): no TLS options passed, verify defaults to none
WebSockex.start(url, __MODULE__, state)  # certificate NOT verified

# FIXED: verification enabled, caller SSL options honored
WebSockex.start(url, __MODULE__, state, ssl_options: [verify: :verify_peer, cacerts: :public_key.cacerts_get()])

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade req_llm past the fix commits so WebSocket TLS verification is enabled and caller-supplied SSL options are honored.
  • Pin your dependency versions and audit TLS settings on every WebSocket client in your dependency tree.
  • Rotate any API key or OAuth token that streamed through an affected version.

docs.title: CVE-2026-107858 — Google ADK: Any Website Could Hijack Your Local AI Agent
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.2 (v4.0) Product Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Java — google-adk-dev 0.1.0–1.12.x and google-adk-maven-plugin 0.3.0–1.12.x dev web server (ADK Web) Type Missing authentication / missing origin validation in WebSocket and CORS defaults (CWE-306 / CWE-1385 / CWE-942) Vector Developer runs the ADK Web dev server locally (no auth) → visits a malicious web page while the server runs → page's JavaScript opens cross-origin WebSocket/REST calls to the local server (allowed origins default to *) → sends messages to the agent (triggering registered tools), streams agent responses, lists/reads/creates/deletes sessions and artifacts. Binding to localhost does not stop it — the requests originate from the developer's own browser

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: google-adk-dev 0.1.0 before 1.13.0 and google-adk-maven-plugin 0.3.0 before 1.13.0. Fixed in 1.13.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The dev server bound to localhost and assumed that meant local. But it had no authentication, and its WebSocket /run_live endpoint accepted connections from any origin (hardcoded setAllowedOrigins("*") through 1.5.0; default CORS origins of * in 1.6.0–1.12.0). Since 0.4.0 the REST API also returned Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. A malicious page visited in the developer's browser could then drive the local agent:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
websocket.set_allowed_origins(["*"])   # BUG: any website may connect
rest_api.add_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")  # BUG

# Simplified fixed pattern
websocket.set_allowed_origins(["http://localhost:8000"])  # explicit trust
Localhost binding never authenticated the caller; the browser happily proxies cross-origin requests for any tab you open.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. Developer starts the ADK Web dev server locally (no authentication).
  2. Developer visits a malicious web page in the same browser while the server runs.
  3. The page's JavaScript opens a cross-origin WebSocket to /run_live — accepted, origin "*".
  4. The page sends messages to the agent (triggering registered tools), streams responses, and lists/reads/deletes sessions and artifacts.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: local servers still need authentication and strict origin checks: the demo contrasts an allow-any origin policy with an explicit localhost-only allowlist. Offline, no server, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade now: google-adk-dev / maven-plugin 1.13.0.
  • On 1.6.0–1.12.0, set adk.web.cors.origins to explicit trusted origins.
  • Treat dev servers as authenticated services — bind token auth even on localhost.
  • Never run dev servers with sensitive tools while browsing untrusted sites.

docs.title: CVE-2026-108097 — Remote Code Execution in Drupal Core Field UI
docs.text: Field Detail Severity Critical (Drupal 19/25) Product Drupal core — Field UI module (field_ui) Type Remote Code Execution Attack vector Unauthenticated — via contributed modules or custom code that expose the vulnerable table rendering CVE CVE-2026-108097 Advisory SA-CORE-2026-014 (2026-10-14)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• Drupal >= 8.9.0 and < 10.6.19
  • Drupal >= 11.0.0 and < 11.3.19
  • Drupal >= 11.4.0 and < 11.4.10
  • Drupal >= 12.0.0-alpha1 and < 12.0.0-beta2

(Branches 8.x, 9.x, <= 10.5.x and <= 11.2.x are end-of-life and receive no patch.)

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Field UI builds administrative tables with Drupal's render system. Before the fix, each table row could carry a #region_callback property, and the module executed it as a PHP callable during pre-render without validating the callback. Drupal core alone never hands remote input to that code path — but contributed modules and custom code can render those tables from attacker-controlled data, and at least one known path requires no authentication. Reported by Drew Webber and Octavio Galland.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational illustration of the bug class only. No working exploit is provided. Test only in controlled environments against systems you own.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. The attacker (no login) finds a contributed-module page that renders a Field UI admin table.
  2. The request smuggles a malicious PHP callable into the row's #region_callback.
  3. Field UI's pre-render step invokes it blindly → arbitrary PHP runs as the web-server user.

Simplified vulnerable vs. fixed pattern (see poc.py):

// VULNERABLE (simplified)
call_user_func($row['#region_callback']);

// FIXED (simplified): allow-list only
$allowed = ['field_ui_table_region'];
if (in_array($cb, $allowed, TRUE)) {
    call_user_func($cb);
}

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Drupal core: 10.6.x to 10.6.19, 11.3.x to 11.3.19, 11.4.x to 11.4.10.
  • Temporary stopgap: uninstall the field_ui module — blocks this hole cold.
  • Drupal Steward blocks some known vectors but not all — still patch.
  • Hunt for compromise: shells or script interpreters spawned by PHP/web-server processes, unknown files in the web root, unexpected outbound traffic.

docs.title: CVE-2026-108099 — Remote Code Execution in Drupal Entity List Module
docs.text: Field Detail Severity Critical (Drupal 19/25) Product Entity List (contributed module — builds entity lists without Views) Type Remote Code Execution Attack vector Unauthenticated — via interaction with other contributed modules or custom code CVE CVE-2026-108099 Advisory SA-CONTRIB-2026-218 (2026-10-14)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: • Entity List < 3.0.10

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Entity List carries a remote code execution flaw in how it builds entity lists. Like its core counterpart (CVE-2026-108097), it is not directly exploitable through the module alone — but combined with other contributed modules or custom code, the vulnerable functionality becomes reachable from remote input, including at least one confirmed path that requires no authentication. The specific module combinations were not disclosed, so any site running Entity List < 3.0.10 alongside custom or contributed code should assume exposure.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational illustration of the bug class only. No working exploit is provided. Test only in controlled environments against systems you own.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. The attacker (no login) reaches a page where Entity List rendering is combined with another module's input handling.
  2. Crafted input reaches the vulnerable list-building logic.
  3. Arbitrary PHP executes as the web-server user — web shell, credential theft, or full takeover follow.

The underlying pattern is the same family as CVE-2026-108097: untrusted input reaching a code-execution sink. See poc.py for a safe, local illustration of validated vs. unvalidated dispatch.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Entity List to 3.0.10.
  • Note: uninstalling Field UI does not fix this one — update the module itself.
  • Drupal Steward coverage for this CVE is not confirmed — patch, don't rely on it.
  • Audit custom code and contributed modules for paths that hand external input to list rendering.

docs.title: CVE-2026-108123 — WP Booking System: Missing Authorization on Booking Actions
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.5 Product WordPress plugin wp-booking-system (WP Booking System – Booking Calendar) Type Missing Authorization (CWE-862) Vector Unauthenticated, network → privileged booking actions and customer data

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: WP Booking System versions up to and including 2.1.0.3. Fixed in the release after 2.1.0.3.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The plugin does not properly verify that the requester is authorized to perform booking actions. The code path that handles privileged operations — the same calls the admin dashboard makes — is missing the capability check (current_user_can()), so the action executes for anyone who calls the endpoint directly, including unauthenticated visitors.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
function handle_booking_action() {
    do_action($_POST['action']);   // no current_user_can() gate
}

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker — no login required — calls the plugin's booking action endpoints directly, replaying the same requests the admin dashboard sends.
  2. With no authorization check in the way, privileged operations execute: listing, modifying, or deleting bookings, and reading customer data that should be admin-only.
  3. The appointment book becomes an open ledger for anyone who knows the endpoint.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock action handler that runs privileged operations without a capability check versus a fixed one with an explicit gate. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update WP Booking System past 2.1.0.3 immediately.
  • Review recent booking changes for tampering or unexpected access.
  • Audit who accessed customer data via the plugin's endpoints.
  • Restrict the plugin's action endpoints to authenticated, authorized users.

docs.title: Azure AI Foundry: SSRF Lets an Authorized User Reach Microsoft's Internals
docs.text: Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test. | | | |---|---| | CVE | CVE-2026-108456 | | Severity | High — CVSS 7.7 (v3.1) | | Product | Azure AI Foundry | | Type | Server-side request forgery / SSRF (CWE-918) | | Attack vector | Authorized attacker makes the platform fetch an attacker-chosen URL that resolves to internal infrastructure → privilege escalation |

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Azure AI Foundry. Mitigated by Microsoft service-side — no customer patch to install.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
AI Foundry fetches URLs on behalf of your agents — data sources, documents, tool endpoints. The fetch followed an attacker-supplied URL without confining where it could resolve. A URL that resolved inward reached Microsoft's private internals, escaping the attacker's own role:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def fetch_for_agent(url):
    return http_get(url)   # BUG: no allowlist, no internal-range block

# Simplified fixed pattern
def fetch_for_agent_fixed(url):
    host = resolve(url)
    if host.is_private() or host not in allowlist:
        return deny("URL not permitted")
    return http_get(url)
Any service that fetches URLs for users must treat the fetcher as the user's confused deputy: allowlist destinations and block internal ranges.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
1. Attacker registers a data source or tool URL in Azure AI Foundry.
  2. The URL (or a redirect from it) resolves to internal infrastructure.
  3. The platform's fetcher retrieves the internal URL with its own privileges.
  4. Internal responses flow back to the attacker's session.
  5. The attacker reads or acts on internals beyond their role — privilege escalation.

See poc.py — a safe, fully synthetic demo of the vulnerable vs. fixed pattern. a server-side fetcher is a confused deputy: the demo contrasts an unconfined fetch with an allowlisted one that blocks private ranges.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Nothing to install: Microsoft mitigated it service-side.
  • Review Foundry activity logs for data sources pointing at odd or internal-looking hosts.
  • Tighten who can register data sources and apply least privilege to agent identities.
  • Prefer allowlists for any URL your agents are permitted to fetch.

docs.title: CVE-2026-108485 — eStore Theme: Reflected XSS in the Storefront
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.1 Product eStore WordPress shop theme Type Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') (CWE-79) Vector Unauthenticated, network → session hijacking via crafted link (phishing)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: eStore theme through 1.6.13. Fixed in versions past 1.6.13.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
A request parameter (the shop search term) is echoed into the HTML response without any output encoding. The attacker never touches the server — the theme itself attacks the site's own visitors by rendering attacker markup as part of the page.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
echo $_GET['s'];                    // search term reflected raw into HTML
// fixed: echo esc_html($_GET['s']); // encoded before output

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker crafts a shop URL whose s parameter contains a script.
  2. The link is sent to a store admin or a logged-in customer — phishing email, comment, DM. The URL looks like the victim's own shop.
  3. The victim clicks; the theme renders the script, which silently ships the victim's session cookie to the attacker.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock theme template whose vulnerable renderer interpolates the raw parameter, versus the fixed renderer that HTML-encodes it. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

An admin session means full site takeover; a customer session means stolen accounts, orders, and payment details. One click is all it takes.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update the eStore theme past 1.6.13 immediately.
  • Warn users about suspicious shop links; treat unexpected login prompts with suspicion.
  • Review admin sessions for unknown logins and force re-authentication.
  • Keep themes updated with the same discipline as plugins — they run code on every page.

docs.title: CVE-2026-108983 — GeoVision GV-ASManager: OS Command Injection in GeoWebServer.exe
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 Product GeoVision GV-ASManager 6.3.0 (GeoWebServer.exe) — surveillance / access control server Type OS Command Injection (CWE-78) Vector Network → crafted request to the default connection ports of GeoWebServer.exe → arbitrary OS commands, no authentication

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
GeoVision GV-ASManager 6.3.0.

As of 2026-10-19, no vendor patch is confirmed — the CVE does not yet appear in GeoVision's published Security Advisory Index. GeoVision's disclosure policy allows CVE details to be published before fixes are available.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
GeoWebServer.exe handles the product's web server default connection ports. Request data from those ports is concatenated into an OS command string with no neutralization of shell metacharacters (CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command).

Characters like ;, |, $, and & pass straight through into the shell, so attacker-controlled input escapes its intended argument and executes arbitrary commands with the server's own privileges.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
user_input = request.get("target")          # attacker-controlled
cmd = "ping " + user_input                  # string glued into a shell command
os.system(cmd)                              # ; | $ & execute as NEW commands

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker sends one crafted request to the GeoWebServer.exe default connection port (no login, no privileges needed).
  2. Unsanitized input is concatenated into an OS command string.
  3. The shell interprets the injected metacharacters as new commands.
  4. The commands run with the server's privileges — full compromise of confidentiality, integrity, and availability (CVSS 9.8).

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock command builder that glues untrusted input into a shell string versus a fixed version that avoids the shell entirely and validates input against an allow-list. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

A sibling flaw in the same process, CVE-2026-108984 (High, 7.5, CWE-121 stack-based buffer overflow), lets remote unauthenticated attackers crash the server entirely.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Isolate the GV-ASManager server from the internet right now.
  • Firewall the GeoWebServer.exe default connection ports; do not expose the management web interface to untrusted networks.
  • Monitor GeoWebServer.exe for suspicious child processes and unusual outbound network activity.
  • Check GeoVision's cyber security page for the fix and apply it the day it lands.
  • If the server was exposed, rotate all credentials on and around it.

docs.title: CVE-2026-109198 — CleanTalk Anti-Spam: Stored XSS Fires in the Admin Dashboard
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.2 (v3.1) Product Anti-Spam by CleanTalk – Spam Protection Without CAPTCHA (WordPress plugin), up to and including 6.89.1 Type Stored cross-site scripting (CWE-79) Vector Unauthenticated attacker registers on a site with open registration using an email field carrying a script payload → value stored without sanitization → when an administrator runs the plugin's spam-user scan and opens the 'Non-checkable users' or 'Spam users' tab, the stored value renders unescaped → script executes in the ADMIN's browser → session hijack / site takeover

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: CleanTalk Anti-Spam plugin versions up to and including 6.89.1.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The plugin stored the user_email registration value without sanitizing it, and later echoed it into the admin's "Non-checkable users" / "Spam users" screens without escaping. The payload waited in the database until an administrator opened exactly those tabs:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
db.store(user_email)                       # no sanitization
admin_page.render("Email: " + user_email)  # BUG: raw HTML echoed

# Simplified fixed pattern
db.store(sanitize(user_email))
admin_page.render("Email: " + escape(user_email))  # escaped on output
Sanitize on input, escape on output — especially in admin screens, where the victim holds the keys to the whole site.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. Attacker registers on the site (registration open) with a script payload in the email field.
  2. CleanTalk stores the value without sanitization.
  3. An administrator runs the plugin's spam-user scan and opens the "Non-checkable users" or "Spam users" tab.
  4. The stored payload renders unescaped in the admin's browser — code executes with admin privileges.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: untrusted values must be escaped wherever they render: the demo contrasts echoing a stored value raw with escaping it on output. Offline, no server, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update now: past CleanTalk 6.89.1.
  • Escape every untrusted value rendered in admin screens; sanitize on input.
  • Review admin users and sessions for signs of hijack during the exposure window.
  • Consider disabling open registration if it is not needed.

docs.title: CVE-2026-109408 — vault-java-driver Silently Disables TLS Verification
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH — CVSS 3.1: 7.4 Product vault-java-driver (io.github.jopenlibs:vault-java-driver), 5.2.0–6.2.3 Type Improper certificate validation (CWE-295) Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N Affected versions 5.2.0 through 6.2.3 Fixed version 7.0.0

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: io.github.jopenlibs:vault-java-driver versions 5.2.0 through 6.2.3. Any Java application fetching secrets from HashiCorp Vault with one of these versions can be affected.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The driver silently disables TLS certificate and hostname verification in three states where the caller asked for verification:

  1. An SslConfig passed to VaultConfig without calling build().
  2. An SslConfig restored by Java deserialization.
  3. VAULT_SSL_VERIFY set to a truthy value other than "true", such as 1, yes or on.

In each case SslConfig.isVerify() returns false and the driver installs a trust-all SSLContext. The settings object reports verification as off unless every setup step is done exactly right, and the driver trusts that flag without a second look. A setting that should default to safe silently defaults to trusting everything — so a fake Vault server presenting any certificate is accepted, and the Vault token and secrets travel in the clear to the impostor.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation with no network traffic, how a verify flag that defaults to off lets a fake certificate through, and how a fixed check that requires an explicit "true" and defaults to verification blocks it.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. An attacker sits on the network path between the app and Vault.
  2. The attacker's fake server presents a forged certificate.
  3. A healthy client would reject it — but verification was silently disabled, so this one accepts it.
  4. The attacker reads the Vault token and secrets in transit, and can forge the responses Vault sends back.
  5. Result: stolen database credentials, poisoned configuration, and a foothold into every system Vault was supposed to protect.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade vault-java-driver to version 7.0.0, which fixes the flaw.
  • Rotate every secret your apps fetched through the old driver.
  • Check your Vault audit logs for tokens used from unexpected places.
  • Pin the fixed version in your build file and audit other TLS configuration for the same silent-default pattern: verification must be on by default, never off.

docs.title: CVE-2026-109431 — Camunda: Missing Authorization on Task Sub-Resources
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.1 (CVSS 3.1) Product Camunda (workflow engine, engine-rest) Type Missing Authorization (CWE-639 / CWE-862) Vector 7.24.0–7.24.13 and 7.23.0–7.23.16 — the engine-rest task sub-resources (getAttachment, getAttachmentData, deleteAttachment, getComment) lack the authorization-filtered checks the list endpoints enforce; an authenticated attacker with no permission grants can read, download, or permanently delete task attachments and comments using only a known object ID

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The list endpoints for task attachments and comments run through the authorization-filtered query layer, but the sub-resource handlers for getAttachment, getAttachmentData, deleteAttachment and getComment call the raw data accessors directly. An authenticated user with no grants on the task can guess or learn an attachment/comment ID and read its contents, download binary data, or delete it permanently — the checks the platform advertises simply never run on these paths.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. Attacker authenticates with a low-privilege account — no task permissions needed.
  2. Learns a task attachment or comment ID (enumeration or a leaked reference).
  3. Calls getAttachment / getAttachmentData / getComment — the sub-resource skips the authorization check.
  4. Reads or permanently deletes data belonging to a task they cannot access.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a vulnerable mock versus the fixed pattern. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Upgrade to Camunda 7.24.14 or 7.23.17 — earlier 7.24.x / 7.23.x releases are affected. Audit attachment and comment access logs for reads or deletes from accounts with no grants. Review other sub-resource endpoints for the same missing-check pattern.

docs.title: CVE-2026-109432 - Camunda 7: Hidden orQueries Expressions Become OS Commands
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical - CVSS 9.8 Product Camunda 7 (7.24.0-7.24.13, 7.23.0-7.23.16) Type Expression Language / OS Command Injection (CWE-917, CWE-78) Vector Remote attacker smuggles expressions inside nested orQueries maps that the validator never inspects

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Camunda 7.24.0 before 7.24.14 and 7.23.0 before 7.23.17.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: AdhocQueryValidator.validate() checked the top-level expression maps but never descended into the sub-query expression maps inside the orQueries field. Attacker expressions nested one level down sailed through validation and were evaluated by the expression engine - and Camunda expressions can reach OS commands.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. Attacker submits an ad-hoc query with a crafted orQueries field.
  2. The validator checks the surface maps and approves.
  3. Nested expression maps inside orQueries are evaluated.
  4. Expression engine runs OS commands with the engine's privileges.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a vulnerable mock versus the fixed pattern. Fully offline, synthetic data - no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Upgrade to Camunda 7.24.14 or 7.23.17. Audit ad-hoc query logs for orQueries payloads carrying expression syntax. Restrict who may submit ad-hoc queries; treat query input as code. Sandbox the expression engine: disable OS-level functions.

docs.title: CVE-2026-109437 — Cognition: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 Product CognicellAI Cognition (AI agent framework) Type Missing Authentication for Critical Function (CWE-306) → unauthenticated RCE Vector Unauthenticated, network-accessible REST/SSE API → remote code execution as server process

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Cognition versions before 0.13.0. Fixed in 0.13.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Two dangerous defaults shipped together:

  1. The REST/SSE API (POST /sessions, POST /sessions/{id}/messages) requires no authentication — anyone who can reach the server can create sessions and post messages to the agent.
  2. The agent sandbox backend defaults to local execution, so the agent's Deep Agents ReAct (think-and-act) loop runs shell commands on the host server itself.
# Simplified vulnerable pattern
# app.py
app.post("/sessions", create_session)                 # no auth required
app.post("/sessions/{id}/messages", post_message)     # no auth required

# default sandbox config
sandbox_backend = "local"   # the agent's shell IS the server's shell

An AI agent with a shell, listening to the open internet: whoever talks to the API owns the box.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker calls POST /sessions — no credentials needed — and gets a session.
  2. They call POST /sessions/{id}/messages with an instruction like "run cat /etc/passwd".
  3. The ReAct loop processes the message and dispatches it to the local shell backend, which executes it on the server.
  4. Result: arbitrary command execution as the server process — read files, steal keys, plant backdoors, pivot into the network.

The accompanying poc.py in this folder demonstrates the pattern safely: it models the request → agent loop → shell dispatch chain against a synthetic mock, shows the unauthenticated path succeeding versus an authenticated/isolated path refusing — all offline, no network calls, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade Cognition to 0.13.0 or later immediately.
  • Require authentication on the REST/SSE API; put agent endpoints behind a firewall and never expose them to the open internet.
  • Never default the agent sandbox to the production host — run agents in isolated containers with no network access to internal resources.
  • Audit server logs for unexpected POST /sessions calls and rotate any secrets that lived on the host.

docs.title: CVE-2026-109516 — Bot for Telegram on WooCommerce: Authentication Bypass to Account Takeover
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL 9.8 (CVSS 3.1) Product Bot for Telegram on WooCommerce plugin for WordPress Type Improper Authentication (CWE-287) Vector Network, unauthenticated, no user interaction

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: All versions up to and including 1.3.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The plugin's Telegram bot-update REST endpoint is registered with a permission callback that always allows access, and it performs no Telegram webhook signature verification. An attacker-supplied update can name any WordPress login, the plugin resolves that name to the matching account with no ownership proof, and it issues a login token built from attacker-influenced, predictable values. A second endpoint then redeems the token and issues an authenticated session cookie with no capability check and no nonce.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text: See poc.py. It is an educational, fully local simulation: mock objects reproduce the decision logic (open endpoint, no signature check, username lookup, predictable token, unconditional login) and contrast it with the fixed logic. It makes no network requests, targets no real site, and cannot log anyone in.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update the plugin past version 1.3.0 to a fixed release as soon as one is available.
  • If no fixed version is available, disable the plugin entirely.
  • Reset passwords for all administrator accounts and audit orders, users, and installed plugins for unknown changes.
  • Restrict the Telegram webhook so only verified Telegram requests can reach it.

docs.title: CVE-2026-109588 — FreeRTOS-Kernel MPU Buffer-Length Truncation
docs.text: Field Detail Severity High 8.8 (CVSS 3.1) / 9.3 (CVSS 4.0) Product FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.3.0 and V11.3.1, Arm Cortex-R82 (Armv8-R AArch64) MPU port Type Numeric truncation (CWE-681) → MPU bypass, privileged memory access Attack vector Local · low-privileged task on MPU-enabled builds

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.3.0 / V11.3.1 (Cortex-R82 MPU port). Fixed in V11.3.2+.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The MPU buffer-authorization check truncates the caller-supplied length (32-bit → 16-bit) before validating it:

len = (uint16_t) user_len;      // top bits silently dropped
if (in_window(buf, len)) allow();

The guard validates the small truncated window, but the hardware then honours the full length — so an unprivileged task reaches privileged kernel memory through a stream-buffer system call.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
poc.py is an educational illustration of the truncation vs the fix. Pure integer arithmetic — no hardware, no kernel. For learning only.

python3 poc.py

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. Unprivileged task calls a stream-buffer syscall with a crafted length like 0x10001.
  2. Truncation to 16 bits yields 0x0001 → passes the MPU window check.
  3. The real 0x10001-length access lands in privileged kernel memory.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade to FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.3.2+ and rebuild all firmware.
  • Audit devices running the Cortex-R82 MPU port on 11.3.0/11.3.1 — treat them as exposed until patched.

docs.title: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619 — "PHP2Shell": Unauthenticated RCE in the PHP engine
docs.text: Field Detail Severity CRITICAL 9.2 (CVSS 4.0) Product PHP (php-src) Type CWE-416 use-after-free via OOM longjmp handling / stale global state Vector CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• php-src >= 8.2.* < 8.2.35
  • php-src >= 8.3.* < 8.3.36
  • php-src >= 8.4.* < 8.4.27
  • php-src >= 8.5.* < 8.5.12

Minimal source backports were provided for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1. Patching WordPress, Drupal, Joomla or the application without updating the underlying PHP runtime is not sufficient — the bug lives below application code.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Two sibling memory-management flaws in the PHP engine's request handling:

  1. CVE-2026-109618 (RCE via OOM corruption). When PHP hits an out-of-memory condition, it uses longjmp() to abort the current execution context. In some contexts this early exit leaves request memory only partially initialized, and the later request cleanup reads or branches on that invalid state → RCE. Crafted HTTP multipart input (no usable declared content length, huge numbers of multipart headers, nested/empty file fields) can trigger the OOM inside normal limits. Demonstrated unauthenticated RCE on Apache mod_php, where the vulnerable sequence occurs during request startup, before any PHP application code executes.

  2. CVE-2026-109619 (RCE via stale global state). PHP workers serve many requests. Various global state temporarily points into request memory; after a fatal error, OOM, or timeout kills a request, some of that state is not correctly reset (or is repopulated after reset) and keeps pointing at freed memory. The next request on the same worker reads/branches on it before normal startup reinitializes it → use-after-free → RCE. Demonstrated paths include session upload progress (session.upload_progress, enabled by default since 5.4.0) and, on PHP 8.5, the fatal error backtrace buffer.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text: The accompanying poc.py is a safe educational simulation of the flaw class — it models a request lifecycle with an emergency exit path and a worker-pool with stale global state, showing how the vulnerable pattern differs from the fixed one. It contains no working exploit and makes no network requests.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
There are no complete mitigations — updating is the only safe choice (per the PHP project).

  • Update PHP to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, or 8.5.12 (or the 7.4/8.0/8.1 source backports).
  • Prioritize internet-facing servers, especially Apache mod_php.
  • The upstream fix removes longjmp() on OOM and replaces it with a "soft OOM" that defers handling to the next VM safe point; if memory usage reaches a higher threshold, _exit() terminates the process immediately.
  • Until patched, monitor for unusual multipart traffic (missing content lengths, abnormal header counts). disable_functions does not help.

docs.text:
Watch the explainer Short

The video walks through the attack chain conceptually: the crafted multipart upload, the emergency jump leaving half-built memory, cleanup being steered into code execution, and the patch.

docs.title: CVE-2026-109894 — Booktics: SQL Injection in Booking Fields (plus DOM XSS)
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.3 Product Booktics WordPress booking plugin Type Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command (CWE-89); sibling CVE-2026-109895 is DOM-based Cross-site Scripting (CWE-79) Vector Unauthenticated, network → full database read

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Booktics through 1.0.29. Fixed in versions past 1.0.29. Both flaws (CVE-2026-109894 SQL injection and CVE-2026-109895 DOM-based XSS) ship in the same plugin install.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
A booking parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL query — no escaping, no prepared statement — so the database cannot tell attacker input apart from the query itself. The second flaw is the same mistake in JavaScript: untrusted strings written straight into the page (DOM XSS) instead of encoded text.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
query = "SELECT * FROM bookings WHERE name = '" + user_input + "'"
db.execute(query)   # attacker input becomes part of the SQL
# fixed:
# db.execute("SELECT * FROM bookings WHERE name = %s", (user_input,))

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker types a single quote into a booking field; the database answers with an error — injection confirmed.
  2. They UNION out the users table through the same field: logins, emails, password hashes.
  3. In parallel, the DOM-based XSS (CVE-2026-109895) hijacks the session of any admin who opens a crafted link.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the SQL injection pattern safely: a mock database whose vulnerable query builder concatenates input (and a fake "UNION probe" detector shows the leak), versus the fixed builder that uses bound parameters. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

The whole database is readable — every account, every email, every hashed password — ready for offline cracking.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Booktics past 1.0.29 immediately.
  • Check database logs for odd SELECT and UNION queries, especially against the users table.
  • Force a password reset for all users and rotate salts and API keys.
  • Treat booking form fields with the same suspicion as login forms.

docs.title: CVE-2026-109895 — Booktics for WordPress: DOM-Based XSS in Booking Flow
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.1 Product Booktics booking plugin for WordPress Type Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (CWE-79) Vector Unauthenticated, network → script execution in admin browser

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:

Shipped alongside CVE-2026-109894 (critical SQL injection in the same plugin); both are covered in the same video walkthrough.

docs.text:
A booking-field value is reflected into the page and later read back by client-side JavaScript through an unsafe sink (innerHTML) without encoding. An attacker crafts a booking link carrying a script payload; when an administrator opens the booking, the payload executes in their session.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
const name = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get("name");
document.getElementById("booking-name").innerHTML = name; // unencoded sink

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker builds a booking URL with a script payload in a field parameter.
  2. A site administrator opens the booking to review it.
  3. The payload runs in the admin's browser — session hijack, rogue admin creation, or settings changes.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: an unsafe innerHTML sink versus the fixed textContent assignment, using fully synthetic strings. No exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Booktics past 1.0.29 immediately.
  • Reset all passwords and review administrator accounts for additions you did not make.

docs.title: CVE-2026-110022 / CVE-2026-110935 — PFI Plugin Framework Deployment Flaws
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH 8.4 (both) Product PFI plugin framework deployment routine Type Unsigned code verification bypass (CVE-2026-110022) / Path traversal (CVE-2026-110935) Vector Crafted plugin archive submitted for deployment Advisory CERT VDE-2026-121

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: The PFI plugin framework deployment routine covered by CERT VDE-2026-121 (fixed versions per the vendor advisory).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Two related flaws in the deployment routine:

  1. CVE-2026-110022 — unsigned entries pass verification. Archive entries that sit outside the signed prefix pass signature verification even though they were never signed. Those entries can overwrite legitimate signed assemblies on disk, and the loader then runs the replaced assemblies as trusted code.
  2. CVE-2026-110935 — path traversal on extraction. Archive entries carrying relative path segments are extracted outside the plugin repository, breaking the boundary the repository was supposed to enforce.

Together they lead to full system compromise: attacker code runs with the trust of the original signed code.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational, conceptual demonstration only. This is not a working exploit.

# Conceptual flow (no real archive, no real framework):
# 1. Attacker crafts a plugin archive:
#    - entry A: unsigned, placed outside the signed prefix
#    - entry B: path "../outside-repo/extra.dll" (relative segments)
# 2. The verifier checks only the signed prefix -> entry A passes unchecked.
# 3. Entry A overwrites a legitimate signed assembly on disk.
# 4. Entry B is extracted outside the plugin repository.
# 5. The loader runs the replaced assembly as trusted code -> compromise.

The key lesson: verify every installed file against its signature, and confine extraction to the repository directory — never trust the archive's own layout.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update the framework to a fixed version.
  • Verify all deployed assemblies against their signatures.
  • Restrict who can install plugins.
  • Audit the plugin repository for unexpected files.

docs.title: Video walkthrough
docs.text: Short video explaining both vulnerabilities, the attack chain, and the fix. Watch the short walkthrough.

docs.title: CVE-2026-110031 — Salon Booking System: Broken Permission Check Lets Staff Become Admin
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.2 Product Salon Booking System WordPress plugin Type Incorrect Privilege Assignment (CWE-266) Vector Low-privilege (staff/booking account), network → administrator

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Versions before 10.31.11. Fixed in 10.31.11.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The role-assignment logic checks that the caller can manage bookings — and then lets them grant themselves the administrator role. Managing appointments was confused with managing users: the permission check that should gate privilege changes is missing entirely.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
if ($user->can('manage_bookings')) {
    $user->set_role('administrator');  // no check on WHO may grant roles
}
// fixed: require current_user_can('promote_users') before any role change

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker holds any staff-level booking account — the intended, low-privilege role for salon receptionists.
  2. They invoke the plugin's role-assignment path, which only verifies booking-management rights.
  3. The account is promoted to administrator: full site takeover from a booking login.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock user store whose vulnerable role-grant only checks booking rights, versus the fixed one that requires the promote_users capability. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update to 10.31.11 immediately.
  • Audit your user list for administrator accounts you did not create — especially recently promoted ones.
  • Demote or remove surprise admins and force password resets.
  • Review which roles are allowed to touch role assignment at all.

docs.title: VM Inspector: Link-Following Flaw Gives Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation
docs.text: Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test. | | | |---|---| | CVE | CVE-2026-110063 | | Severity | Critical — CVSS 10.0 (v3.1) | | Product | VM Inspector for Azure Virtual Machines | | Type | Improper link resolution before file access / link following (CWE-59) | | Attack vector | Unauthenticated remote attacker plants or abuses a symlink so a privileged file access follows it → privilege escalation |

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: VM Inspector for Azure Virtual Machines. Fixed by Microsoft service-side — no customer patch to install.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
VM Inspector runs with elevated privileges while inspecting guest VMs. A privileged file operation resolved a path and then opened it — but between the check and the open, the path could pass through a symbolic link. The service followed the link instead of the intended file, so the attacker's chosen destination was read or written with the service's privileges:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def inspect(path):
    if allowed(path):                 # check on the logical path
        return open_privileged(path)  # BUG: follows symlinks to anywhere

# Simplified fixed pattern
def inspect_fixed(path):
    real = os.path.realpath(path)     # canonicalize at moment of use
    if allowed(real):
        return open_privileged(real)
A path is a promise, not a fact: canonicalize at the moment of use.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
1. Attacker identifies a privileged file operation that takes a path.
  2. Attacker places a symbolic link where that path resolves.
  3. The privileged service checks the logical path, then opens through the link.
  4. The open lands on the attacker's destination with the service's privileges.
  5. Files are read or written as the privileged service — privilege escalation.

See poc.py — a safe, fully synthetic demo of the vulnerable vs. fixed pattern. privileged code must canonicalize every path at the moment of use: the demo contrasts following a link versus resolving it first.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Nothing to install: Microsoft fixed VM Inspector service-side.
  • Keep guest VMs updated and limit who can reach diagnostic endpoints.
  • Monitor for unexpected symlink activity around inspection tooling.
