docs.title: CVE-2026-122299 — Dulwich Commit Parser Tree Header Misinterpretation
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH — CVSS 3.1: 8.8 Product Dulwich (Python Git library), via Poetry 2.5.1 Type Incorrect behavior order / parser differential (CWE-115) Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Affected versions Dulwich before 1.2.20 Fixed version 1.2.20

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Dulwich before 1.2.20. Poetry 2.5.1 ships this version and uses Dulwich by default for Git dependency installation.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The commit object read path in _parse_commit resolves a duplicate tree header to the last occurrence instead of the first, diverging from core Git's resolution behavior. A commit object can therefore carry two tree headers: reviewers and CI using Git see the benign tree, while a Dulwich-based checkout resolves to a different, attacker-controlled tree. The disagreement between the two parsers is the whole vulnerability — what was reviewed is not what gets installed.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation, how a parser that takes the last duplicate header resolves a crafted commit to a different tree than a parser that takes the first, and how the fixed version (first occurrence wins, matching Git) breaks the chain.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. An attacker crafts a commit object with two tree headers: a benign tree first, a malicious tree second.
  2. Reviewers and CI using core Git resolve the first tree and approve the benign code.
  3. Poetry, using Dulwich, installs the dependency and resolves the second tree instead.
  4. The attacker-controlled tree contains malicious build scripts, which execute on the install or build host.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Dulwich to 1.2.20 or later now, and move past Poetry 2.5.1, which ships the vulnerable version.
  • Pin dependencies and verify lockfiles against reviewed sources.
  • Audit recent installs from Git dependencies for unexpected build scripts.
  • Treat parser differentials as a review gap: the code that was checked must be byte-identical to the code that was installed.

docs.title: CVE-2026-122311-group — Namespace Escape and Cluster Takeover in Kyverno before 1.19.2
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL — CVSS 3.1: 9.9 (lead CVE-2026-122311; batch includes 9.9, 9.8, 9.1 and HIGH 7.5–8.5) Product Kyverno before 1.19.2 Type Authorization Bypass / Namespace Isolation Failure (CWE-22, CWE-269, CWE-862, CWE-863 and others) Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H (lead CVE-2026-122311) Affected versions Kyverno before 1.19.2 (some flaws from 1.11.0, 1.16.0, 1.17.0, 1.18.0 or 1.19.1) Fixed version Kyverno 1.19.2

docs.title: The batch
docs.text:
One release, 1.19.2, closes more than twenty flaws. The most severe share one story: a tenant who can create a namespaced policy can reach outside their namespace because a check fails or a privileged controller trusts tenant-supplied content. Headline members:

  • CVE-2026-122311 (9.9) — Path traversal in the resource argument of resource.get() / resource.post() in namespaced CEL policies: .. segments reach arbitrary cluster objects with the admission controller's ServiceAccount.
  • CVE-2026-122303 (9.9) — NamespacedMutatingPolicy mutate-existing accepts a CEL map literal fabricating a target with an attacker-chosen namespace, overwriting Secrets, Deployments or policies cluster-wide.
  • CVE-2026-122304 (9.9) — CleanupPolicy context loader built with a nil policy lets namespace admins read cross-namespace Secrets and modify validating webhook configurations.
  • CVE-2026-122310 (9.9) — Policy apiCall urlPath validated after cleaning but executed raw, so # / ? hide .. segments and reach cluster-scoped endpoints as cluster admin.
  • CVE-2026-122313 (9.9) — NamespacedMutatingPolicy CEL output lacks namespace checks, so tenants mutate other namespaces' RoleBindings, NetworkPolicies and ConfigMaps.
  • CVE-2026-122302 (9.8) — Generate-rule admission checks verify the controller's permissions, not the author's, so namespace admins clone resources cluster-wide.
  • CVE-2026-122321 (9.1) — verifyImages cache keyed by image reference string instead of digest, so a moved tag skips signature checks.
  • Plus HIGH flaws: label spoofing of the generation handler (122308), mutate-existing cross-namespace writes (122316), generate-clone reads (122320), image verification bypasses (122318), and denial-of-service flaws in variable substitution, CEL evaluation, wildcard matching and decompression (122305, 122306, 122309, 122314, 122315, 122319, 122322, 122323).

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Kyverno before 1.19.2. The exact floor varies per flaw (1.11.0, 1.16.0, 1.17.0, 1.18.0 or 1.19.1); treat every release before 1.19.2 as affected.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Kyverno's controllers hold cluster-wide power and act on policy content that namespace tenants can write. Several validation paths trusted that content: path segments were not normalized before authorization, CEL expressions could fabricate target objects without a namespace check, and one context loader ran with no policy at all. The tenant's request therefore executed with the controller's identity — a small account borrowing a giant one.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation, how a path check that never normalizes .. segments lets a namespaced policy address a cluster-scoped object, and how the fixed version (normalize first, then verify every segment stays inside the tenant's namespace) blocks it.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. Attacker holds a tenant account that can create a namespaced policy.
  2. Attacker hides an escape in the policy — a path that climbs out of the namespace, or a fabricated target naming another tenant.
  3. Kyverno's privileged controller trusts the request and executes it.
  4. The attacker reads other tenants' Secrets, overwrites policies and Deployments, or bypasses image verification.
  5. Result: cluster takeover from a single namespace.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade Kyverno to version 1.19.2 immediately — it closes the whole batch.
  • Until upgraded, restrict who can create namespaced policies (NamespacedValidatingPolicy, NamespacedMutatingPolicy, CleanupPolicy, generate rules) to trusted administrators.
  • Audit existing namespaced policies for unusual paths, .. segments, or targets outside the author's namespace.
  • Monitor for cross-namespace reads and writes by the Kyverno controllers' ServiceAccounts.
  • Apply least privilege to Kyverno's ServiceAccounts where the deployment allows it.

docs.title: CVE-2026-123018 / CVE-2026-123019 — DB-GPT Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Your AI Agent Server
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH — CVSS 3.1: 8.3 (CVE-2026-123018), 7.3 (CVE-2026-123019) Product eosphoros-ai DB-GPT, up to 0.8.2 Type Code injection (CWE-74) / Inclusion of functionality from untrusted control sphere (CWE-829) Vector CVE-2026-123018: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:L Vector CVE-2026-123019: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L Affected versions Up to 0.8.2 Fixed version No patch yet (project has not responded) — isolate the service

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: DB-GPT up to version 0.8.2, in its default deployment: the service binds 0.0.0.0:5670 with no real authentication. Both flaws were disclosed with public exploits on 2026-11-05, and the project had been informed earlier through issue reports without responding.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Two independent flaws, same outcome — remote code execution with no login:

CVE-2026-123018 (CodeAction code injection, CWE-74). The CodeEngineer agent's default action extracts code blocks from the language model's output and runs every Python, bash or shell block through execute_code(). The sandbox decision is broken by design inside the official Docker container: the code checks whether /.dockerenv exists, and that file always exists inside a container, so the check always takes the native execution branch — subprocess.run on the server itself — even with the Docker SDK installed. The permission review that should ask a human first unconditionally returns "approved". On top of that, the default deployment has no authentication: the auth layer returns role admin for any caller, and requests pass through when no API keys are configured. An attacker creates an agent app and gets the model to emit a code block through two unauthenticated API calls.

CVE-2026-123019 (HuggingFace trust_remote_code, CWE-829). The model loader trusts remote code by default: the deploy parameters and the adapter base class both default trust_remote_code to true, and the loader forwards it into from_pretrained, so transformers downloads the model repository and executes its Python code at import time. The model registration endpoint carries no authentication, so an unauthenticated attacker registers a malicious model themselves and triggers loading. The code runs at the import stage, before any weights are read — a later "load failed" error does not undo the execution.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation with no network traffic, how a code runner that trusts model output and always approves its own review executes attacker code on the "server", and how a fixed runner that sandboxes execution, requires human approval, and refuses untrusted remote code blocks it. It also simulates the model-loading flaw: a loader that defaults to trusting remote code executes the model's code at import, while a loader with trust disabled refuses to run it.

Conceptual attack chain (CVE-2026-123018):

  1. The attacker reaches the DB-GPT service on port 5670 — no login, no key.
  2. They create a single-agent app using CodeEngineer via an unauthenticated API call.
  3. They get the model to emit a code block via an unauthenticated chat request.
  4. CodeAction extracts the block and execute_code() runs it natively — the container probe makes the sandbox branch unreachable.
  5. The code runs inside the server process (verified 8/8 in the official Docker deployment by the researchers).

Conceptual attack chain (CVE-2026-123019):

  1. The attacker registers a malicious HuggingFace model via the unauthenticated model registration endpoint.
  2. Loading the model runs its code at import time, inside the server process.
  3. The load then fails for missing weights — but the code has already run.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Take DB-GPT off the public internet now and block port 5670 at the firewall. There is no patch yet — isolation is the fix today.
  • Set trust_remote_code to false everywhere; only load models from sources you trust, and never let an unauthenticated caller register a model.
  • Put real authentication on every endpoint — API keys enforced, no mock auth that returns admin for anyone.
  • Require human approval before any agent executes generated code, and run generated code only inside a real sandbox, never in the server process.
  • Watch for a patched release past 0.8.2 and upgrade as soon as it lands.
  • If you ran DB-GPT exposed to a network, treat the host as compromised: review server logs for unexpected code execution and rebuild if in doubt.

docs.title: CVE-2026-124060: TOTOLINK CA300-PoE Buffer Overflow via the UploadCustomModule File Parameter
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL (9.1) CVSS vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H Product TOTOLINK CA300-PoE ceiling access point, firmware 6.2c.884 Vulnerability type Buffer Overflow (CWE-119, CWE-120)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: TOTOLINK CA300-PoE firmware 6.2c.884.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The UploadCustomModule handler in /cgi-bin/cstecgi.cgi copies the File argument into a fixed-size memory buffer without checking its length. A file name longer than the buffer overflows it, overwriting adjacent memory and letting an attacker steer the device's execution flow. The attack is launched remotely over the network and requires high (admin) privileges. A public proof of concept exists.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo in poc.py models the safe pattern: a bounded copy that validates the file name length before copying, so an oversized name is rejected instead of overflowing the buffer. It runs locally.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• No firmware patch is available yet. Restrict the admin web interface to trusted networks only.
  • Disable remote management of the access point.
  • Isolate the device on a management VLAN or separate network segment.
  • Monitor TOTOLINK for a firmware update and apply it as soon as it is released.
  • Review logs for unusual upload requests to the device's web interface.

docs.title: CVE-2026-124501 — Privileged Job Escape in moto AWS Batch Emulation (5.2.0–5.2.4)
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH — CVSS 3.1: 7.3 Product Tidelift moto 5.2.0–5.2.4 Type Improper Privilege Management (CWE-266, CWE-269) Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L Affected versions moto 5.2.0, 5.2.1, 5.2.2, 5.2.3, 5.2.4 Fixed version None yet — vendor was contacted and did not respond

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: moto 5.2.0 through 5.2.4. The flaw is in the AWS Batch emulation (moto/batch/models.py): a job definition can request a privileged container and host volume mounts, and the mock server accepts those flags without validation.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: moto is a test library: it pretends to be AWS so code can be tested without touching real cloud services. Its mock Batch endpoint accepts job definitions from anyone who can reach it, and it passes the privileged flag and volumes (host path mounts) straight through to the container runtime. Privileged mode and host mounts are real container powers, not harmless test data — but the mock treated them as ordinary fields and never checked them. Anyone who can submit a job to the mock server therefore gets a container with host-level access on the machine running moto.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation, how a job definition carrying privileged: True and a host root mount is accepted unchecked by the vulnerable mock, and how the fixed version (reject privileged mode and host mounts, or require an explicit allow-list) blocks it.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. Attacker reaches a moto mock server (moto_server) exposed on the network — no login is required.
  2. Attacker submits an AWS Batch job definition asking for a privileged container with the host root folder mounted inside.
  3. The mock server accepts the job as requested and runs it.
  4. The container now sees the host filesystem: the attacker reads host files, reaches other services, and gains a foothold.
  5. Result: container escape from a test tool — host access from a job that was supposed to be fake.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Do not expose the moto mock server to untrusted networks. Bind it to localhost only (127.0.0.1) and never publish its port.
  • Run the mock server isolated from anything sensitive, and never as root — a privileged container escape is far less useful on a disposable, unprivileged host.
  • Restrict who can submit jobs to the mock endpoint (network ACLs, firewall rules) to your own test runners.
  • Watch for a fixed moto release and upgrade the moment it lands. Until then, treat any moto server reachable on the network as untrusted input.
  • Audit recent Batch job definitions for privileged flags or host volume mounts you did not expect.

docs.title: CVE-2026-125120 — Mongoose countDocuments() Skips sanitizeFilter (9.8 CRITICAL)
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL — CVSS 3.1: 9.8 Product Mongoose before 6.13.11 / 7.8.12 / 8.24.3 / 9.9.2 Type Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Query (CWE-943) Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Affected versions Mongoose < 6.13.11, < 7.8.12, < 8.24.3, < 9.9.2 Fixed version 6.13.11, 7.8.12, 8.24.3, 9.9.2

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Mongoose 6.x before 6.13.11, 7.x before 7.8.12, 8.x before 8.24.3, and 9.x before 9.9.2. Applications that enable sanitizeFilter and pass attacker-controlled values to countDocuments() are affected.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Mongoose offers sanitizeFilter, a defense that strips query operator objects (like $gt, $ne) out of user-supplied filters so they are treated as literal values. But countDocuments() never applies it: the sanitizer runs on other query paths and simply skips this one.

The result is a defense that reports itself enabled while one of the most-used methods leaves it off. An attacker-controlled filter value that is secretly an operator object is processed as a live operator, so the count includes documents that should never match — poisoning any authorization or application logic that trusts that count.

Sibling flaws in the same release window: CVE-2026-125119 (the connection-level sanitizeFilter setting is ignored by query casting) and CVE-2026-125117 (prototype pollution via inherited properties).

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation, how an operator object smuggled into a filter is executed by the vulnerable count path, and how the fixed version (sanitize before counting) strips it.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. Application enables sanitizeFilter and trusts it to clean filters.
  2. Attacker sends a filter value that is an operator object, for example a password field carrying $ne.
  3. countDocuments() skips the sanitizer and treats the object as a live operator.
  4. The count includes documents that should not match.
  5. Result: authorization or business logic that relies on the count makes the wrong decision — the defense was on everywhere except where it mattered.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Mongoose to 6.13.11, 7.8.12, 8.24.3, or 9.9.2 depending on your major version.
  • Never pass raw user input as a query filter object — validate every value and strip operator keys yourself as defense in depth.
  • Audit authorization and limit checks that rely on countDocuments() results.
  • Prefer global mongoose.set('sanitizeFilter') or per-query .sanitizeFilter(), which were not affected, and verify the sanitizer actually runs on every query path you use.

docs.title: CVE-2026-125396 — Ghostscript -dSAFER Bypass to Remote Code Execution (7.8 HIGH)
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH — CVSS 3.1: 7.8 Product Ghostscript before 10.08.0 Type Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast (CWE-648) Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Affected versions Ghostscript < 10.08.0 Fixed version 10.08.0

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Ghostscript before 10.08.0. Any service that renders untrusted PostScript or PDF documents with Ghostscript — printers, preview pipelines, document converters — is affected.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Ghostscript's -dSAFER sandbox is supposed to block dangerous operations while rendering untrusted documents. But the .putgstringcopy procedure in gs_fonts.ps calls the privileged .forceput operator without checking the types of its operands.

An attacker crafts a document that triggers a type error at exactly the right moment and catches it with a custom error handler, recovering .forceput for their own use. Combined with a use-after-free across save/restore, that recovered privilege escapes the sandbox and executes arbitrary code.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation, how a helper that hands out a privileged operation without a type check lets an error handler recover it, and how the fixed version (validate operands first) refuses.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. Attacker sends a crafted PostScript or PDF document to a service that renders it with Ghostscript.
  2. The document triggers a type error inside the font helper.
  3. A custom error handler catches the error and recovers the privileged .forceput operator.
  4. A use-after-free across save/restore corrupts memory.
  5. Result: the -dSAFER sandbox is escaped and arbitrary code runs with the privileges of the rendering service.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Ghostscript to 10.08.0 immediately.
  • Isolate document rendering: run converters in a sandboxed, unprivileged container with no network access.
  • Never let untrusted documents reach an old renderer — validate uploads and patch every converter, printer, and preview service.
  • Treat any document conversion service as an attacker-reachable boundary, not an internal tool.

docs.title: CVE-2026-125406-group — Seven Memory Flaws in Ettercap Dissectors (up to 8.8 HIGH)
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH — CVSS 3.1: up to 8.8 Product Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 Type Memory corruption: stack underwrite, use-after-free, heap overflow (CWE-124, CWE-416, CWE-122) Vector CVE-2026-125406: CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Affected versions Ettercap through 0.8.4.1 Fixed version Patched release past 0.8.4.1 (see PR #1330)

docs.title: Covered CVEs
docs.text: CVE Severity Flaw CVE-2026-125400 8.8 HIGH Use-after-free in func_pcre() (filter engine reads freed PCRE2 match data) CVE-2026-125401 8.1 HIGH Heap buffer overflow in gg_get_version() CVE-2026-125402 8.1 HIGH Heap out-of-bounds read in sslw_get_clienthello_sni() CVE-2026-125403 8.1 HIGH Out-of-bounds read + size_t underflow in sslw_remove_sts() CVE-2026-125404 7.5 HIGH Integer underflow in ccmp_decrypt() CVE-2026-125405 8.1 HIGH Out-of-bounds read in Parse_NTLM_Auth() CVE-2026-125406 8.8 HIGH Stack buffer underwrite in the telnet dissector (backspace without lower-bound check)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Ettercap through 0.8.4.1. Ettercap normally runs as root, so any of these flaws can mean code execution with the highest privileges.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Ettercap's packet dissectors parse attacker-controlled network data in memory-unsafe C and trust it to stay within bounds. The headline flaw is in the telnet dissector (src/dissectors/ec_telnet.c): every backspace character decrements the output pointer by one, with no check for the start of the buffer. Send more backspaces than preceding characters and the pointer walks below the buffer, writing over the stack.

The siblings share the same root cause in different dissectors: the filter engine reads PCRE2 match data after freeing it, the GG, SSL, and NTLM dissectors read past heap buffers, and the CCMP decryptor underflows an integer. One cluster, one pattern: unchecked parsing of hostile bytes.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation, how a backspace stream walks a write pointer below its buffer unchecked by the vulnerable dissector, and how the fixed version (lower-bound check) refuses.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. Attacker is network-adjacent to a machine running Ettercap.
  2. Attacker sends a telnet stream packed with backspace characters.
  3. Each backspace moves the output pointer one step back — no lower bound is ever checked.
  4. The pointer walks below the buffer and overwrites the stack of a process running as root.
  5. Result: memory corruption, and potentially code execution as root — from the very tool meant to watch the network.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Ettercap past 0.8.4.1 to the patched release.
  • Never run sniffers on untrusted networks longer than needed, and restrict who can reach the machine running them.
  • Run Ettercap with the least privilege the task allows, isolated from sensitive services.
  • Audit memory-unsafe parsers that handle hostile input, and fuzz dissectors with malformed streams before shipping.

docs.title: CVE-2026-126537 — Ninja Forms File Uploads arbitrary file deletion (path traversal)
docs.text: Severity Product Type Attack vector CRITICAL 9.1 Ninja Forms — File Uploads add-on for WordPress, up to and including 3.3.36 Path traversal / arbitrary file deletion (CWE-22) Network — unauthenticated, via a crafted public form submission

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• Ninja Forms File Uploads <= 3.3.36
  • Fixed in versions after 3.3.36 (update to the latest release)

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Two code paths combine into the flaw. In includes/fields/upload.php, NF_FU_Fields_Upload::process() returns early — leaving the client-supplied files[] array intact — whenever a public submission carries a nonempty extra.saveProgress. Separately, in includes/external/abstracts/service.php, NF_FU_External_Abstracts_Service::process_upload() only reloads the authoritative path when the client sends upload_id. By omitting upload_id, an attacker's data[file_path] survives into the Background Upload queue, where it is used both by upload_file_to_s3() (as SourceFile) and by the maybe_delete_server_file() unlink() call in includes/external/abstracts/backgroundupload.php.

There is no canonicalization and no upload-directory containment check on that path — the plugin's own is_path_within_upload_dir() helper is only applied on admin paths, never on public ones.

Deleting wp-config.php forces WordPress into its setup screen, enabling full site takeover. The same unchecked path can also be used to read files out through the S3/Dropbox/Google Drive exfiltration path.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Conceptual only — illustrates the pattern behind the bug, not a working exploit.

# A public form submission carries a visitor-supplied file path.
# The plugin trusts it because the containment check only runs
# on admin requests:
#
#     path = data["file_path"]        # attacker-controlled
#     if is_admin_request():
#         assert is_path_within_upload_dir(path)
#     background_queue.enqueue(path)  # public path: never checked
#     ...
#     unlink(path)                    # deletes ANY file on disk
#
# Point it at wp-config.php and WordPress drops into its setup
# screen — full site takeover with no login.

See poc.py for a safe, pure-Python simulation of the unchecked-path pattern vs. the fixed containment behavior.

Educational use only. Do not build or distribute working exploits for this vulnerability — patch your dependencies instead.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Ninja Forms File Uploads past 3.3.36 immediately.
  • Verify wp-config.php and other critical files are intact; if the config was deleted, restore it from backup and rotate your database credentials.
  • Review upload logs for submissions carrying suspicious file_path values (paths outside the uploads directory, ../ sequences).
  • For defense in depth, enforce server-side containment on every upload path — public and admin alike — and block path separators in client-supplied file fields.

docs.title: CVE-2026-15266 / CVE-2026-6715: IBM Concert OS Command Injection
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL (9.8) CVSS vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Product IBM Concert 1.0 through 3.0.1.1 Vulnerability type OS Command Injection (CWE-78)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: IBM Concert 1.0 through 3.0.1.1.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Concert contains components that incorporate attacker-supplied input into operating system commands without adequate validation or sanitization. A remote attacker can craft input that escapes the intended command and runs arbitrary system commands on the host with the privileges of the affected service. No authentication is required. The two CVEs describe the same root cause from two angles: unsafe command execution (CVE-2026-15266) and unsanitized input flowing into an OS command (CVE-2026-6715).

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo in poc.py shows the dangerous pattern (building a shell command by concatenating user input) next to the safe pattern (a fixed allowlist of commands executed without a shell, with user input passed only as a data argument). It runs locally.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade to IBM Concert Software 3.1.0 (Concert Protect 3.1.0 / Concert Platform 3.0.3), which IBM strongly recommends.
  • Never build OS commands by concatenating user input; use an allowlist of fixed commands and pass data as arguments, never through a shell.
  • Restrict network access to the Concert service to trusted hosts until patched.
  • Review logs for unexpected command executions or unusual input to Concert components.

docs.title: CVE-2026-15723 — GitLab: LDAP Account Takeover via OmniAuth SAML Identity Linking
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.2 (v3.1) Product GitLab CE/EE with OmniAuth SAML + LDAP auto-linking enabled Type Improper input sanitization (CWE-90) in the LDAP email lookup during identity linking Vector Authenticated attacker signs in via SAML, links to a victim's LDAP-backed account through a poorly sanitized email lookup — no interaction from the victim required

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: All versions from 10.1 before 19.3.6, 19.4 before 19.4.3, and 19.5 before 19.5.1. Fixed in 19.3.6, 19.4.3, 19.5.1.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
When both OmniAuth SAML and LDAP auto-linking were enabled, GitLab tried to match the incoming SAML identity to an existing LDAP user by email. The email value taken from the SAML assertion was not properly sanitized before being used in the LDAP lookup path, so an attacker could shape it to match someone else's LDAP account. GitLab then linked the attacker's session to the victim's account:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def link_identity(saml_email):
    ldap_user = ldap_lookup(saml_email)   # BUG: unsanitized attacker input
    if ldap_user:
        link(current_session, ldap_user)  # victim's account linked to attacker

# Simplified fixed pattern
def link_identity_fixed(saml_email):
    email = strict_normalize(saml_email)  # canonicalize + validate first
    ldap_user = ldap_lookup_exact(email)
    if ldap_user and verified_owner(email, current_user):
        link(current_session, ldap_user)

Identity linking must never trust an unsanitized claim.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. Target instance has OmniAuth SAML and LDAP auto-linking both enabled.
  2. Attacker authenticates with their own low-privilege SAML identity.
  3. During linking, the attacker supplies a crafted email value that the loose LDAP lookup resolves to the victim's LDAP-backed account.
  4. GitLab links the attacker's session to the victim's account — full takeover, zero victim interaction.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: loose vs. strict email matching when resolving an account for linking. Offline, no server, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade: 19.3.6 / 19.4.3 / 19.5.1.
  • Review identity links: audit identities for unexpected SAML↔LDAP linkages, especially around privileged accounts.
  • Disable auto-linking if the SAML and LDAP user populations are not strictly aligned.
  • Enforce exact, verified email matching between identity providers before linking.

docs.title: CVE-2026-15748 — Forminator MIME Blocklist Bypass → Unauthenticated PHP Shell Upload
docs.text: Field Detail Severity Critical 9.8 (CVSS 3.1) Product Forminator Forms (WordPress), ≤ 1.56.1 Type Unrestricted file upload via blocklist bypass (CWE-434) Attack vector Network · unauthenticated form submission with forged upload field

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: All versions up to and including 1.56.1. Fixed in 1.56.2.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: handle_file_upload validates uploads against a blocklist of dangerous MIME types using exact string-key matching. MIME types support pipe-separated alternatives, so declaring the file's type with a trailing pipe fails the exact match while the server still treats the payload as PHP. Separately, the upload field configuration is attacker-controlled through a forged Select field value, so the attacker dictates the allowed types for the submission.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Conceptual attack chain (educational only): 1. The attacker forges the Select field value to inject a custom upload field configuration. 2. The attacker submits a PHP shell declaring its MIME type with a trailing pipe character. 3. The blocklist's exact-match check misses → the file is accepted into the uploads directory. 4. The attacker requests the uploaded file → remote code execution, no login required.

The bundled poc.py demonstrates the exact-match versus normalized validation logic on synthetic inputs only — no server involved.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Forminator to 1.56.2 immediately.
  • Scan wp-content/uploads/ for unexpected .php or other executable files.
  • Prefer allowlists of known-safe types over blocklists of bad ones; normalize and validate the real file extension server-side.

docs.title: CVE-2026-16460 — bootc + ostree: Two Holes in the OS Image Trust Chain (Signature Bypass)
docs.text:
Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.4 (CVE-2026-16460), CVSS 8.1 (CVE-2026-16487) Product bootc + ostree — image-based Linux (RHEL image mode, Fedora Atomic) Type Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity (CWE-345) Vector Local (16460: staged deployments) / Network (16487: mutable-tag upgrades) → unsigned OS content becomes the host on reboot

This writeup covers two CVEs published together against the same product:

CVE Issue CVE-2026-16460 bootc and ostree finalize already-staged deployments without revalidating the container image against the current containers signature policy. Unsigned OS content staged under a prior permissive policy stays bootable after the policy is hardened to reject unsigned images. CVSS 7.4, AV:L/AC:H. CVE-2026-16487 bootc operating with the default containers signature policy: automatic or manual upgrades of a mutable image tag may apply unsigned content for registries that fall through to insecureAcceptAnything. An attacker who can update that tag gets arbitrary OS content executed as the host root filesystem on reboot. CVSS 8.1, AV:N/AC:H.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• CVE-2026-16460: bootc/ostree builds predating the upstream fix — staged deployments are finalized without policy revalidation. Track the fix via the Red Hat CVE page.
  • CVE-2026-16487: bootc builds honoring the default containers signature policy with insecureAcceptAnything fallthrough. Track the fix via the Red Hat CVE page.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
A signature-policy decision is made once, at pull time, and then trusted forever. Two code paths skip the check at the moments that matter:

  1. Finalize path (CVE-2026-16460): the policy is consulted when content is staged, never when the staged deployment is finalized or booted. Hardening the policy afterwards changes the rules for new pulls, but the staged deployment keeps its old, unvalidated trust — and it is still the one queued to boot.
  2. Upgrade path (CVE-2026-16487): registries with no explicit rule in the policy fall through to insecureAcceptAnything, so for those registries the signature check silently never runs — on automatic and manual upgrades of mutable tags.
# Simplified vulnerable pattern (containers policy + bootc finalize)
policy:
  default: signedBy(trusted-key)   # checked ONLY at pull/stage time
  # no rule for attacker.registry  ->  insecureAcceptAnything fallthrough

finalize(staged_deployment):
    boot(staged.image)             # <-- no policy re-check here

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
Path A (CVE-2026-16460):

  1. With the containers signature policy still permissive, unsigned OS content is staged on the machine (attacker needs local access).
  2. The admin hardens the policy to reject unsigned images. The staged deployment is untouched and stays queued to boot.
  3. On reboot, bootc finalizes the staged deployment — no revalidation — and the machine boots attacker-controlled content as the host OS. Full compromise of confidentiality, integrity and availability.

Path B (CVE-2026-16487):

  1. The machine tracks a mutable tag (e.g. registry/app:latest) on a registry with no explicit policy rule, falling through to insecureAcceptAnything.
  2. An attacker who can update that tag (registry compromise, weak credentials) points it at unsigned, malicious OS content.
  3. The next automatic or manual upgrade pulls it with no signature check; on reboot it becomes the host root filesystem.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a finalize step that skips revalidation versus one that re-checks the current policy, and a mutable tag that falls through to "accept anything" versus a pinned digest with an explicit signedBy rule. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update bootc and ostree to the patched releases (see the Red Hat CVE pages above for errata).
  • Pin images to immutable digests, not mutable tags, wherever the fleet allows it.
  • Close the policy hole: remove any insecureAcceptAnything fallthrough from your containers signature policy; give every registry an explicit signedBy rule.
  • Audit every staged deployment on the fleet after any policy change — clear unvalidated staged content before it boots.
  • Rotate any credentials/tokens that could have been exposed on a compromised host and audit boot logs for unexpected staged content.

docs.title: CVE-2026-16487 — bootc: Unsigned Mutable-Tag Upgrades via insecureAcceptAnything Fallthrough
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.1 Product bootc (image-based Linux) running under the default containers signature policy Type Insufficient verification of data authenticity (CWE-345): unsigned content accepted through the insecureAcceptAnything registry fallthrough Vector Network, high complexity, no privileges → whoever can update a mutable image tag lands arbitrary OS content that becomes the host root filesystem on reboot

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: • bootc builds predating the upstream fix (see the Red Hat advisory for the fixed package versions).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Under the default containers signature policy, any registry without an explicit policy entry falls through to insecureAcceptAnything. When bootc performs an automatic or manual upgrade of a mutable image tag (e.g. :latest), it may pull and apply unsigned content from such registries. Anyone able to update that tag — a compromised registry account, a tag-mutation attack — gets arbitrary OS content staged as the next boot target, running as the host root filesystem after reboot.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def policy_for(registry, policy):
    return policy.get(registry, "insecureAcceptAnything")  # unsigned accepted

# Simplified fixed pattern
def policy_for(registry, policy):
    return policy.get(registry, "reject")  # default-deny; pin digests

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. The target host runs bootc with the default policy; its registry has no explicit entry → insecureAcceptAnything.
  2. The attacker updates the mutable tag (:latest) the host tracks.
  3. The next bootc upgrade (automatic or manual) pulls the unsigned image and stages it.
  4. On reboot the attacker's image becomes the host OS — full root compromise.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a policy lookup with the insecure fallthrough versus default-deny plus digest pinning. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update bootc to the fixed build (Red Hat CVE-2026-16487 / bug 2503686).
  • Remove insecureAcceptAnything from policy.json; give every registry an explicit entry (signed or reject).
  • Pin image digests (image@sha256:...) instead of tracking mutable tags.
  • Restrict who can push to the tags your fleet tracks, and monitor tag mutations.

docs.title: CVE-2026-16762 — Qt QXmlStreamReader: Crafted XML Burns the CPU
docs.text: Field Value Severity Under analysis — NVD has not published a CVSS score yet; denial of service via CPU exhaustion Product Qt — QXmlStreamReader XML parsing component used across desktop and embedded applications Type Disproportionate resource consumption / algorithmic complexity (CWE-407) Vector Attacker supplies a crafted XML document to any application using QXmlStreamReader → parsing consumes disproportionate CPU → the application becomes unresponsive (denial of service)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Applications parsing attacker-influenced XML with vulnerable Qt builds. Check the Qt security advisory for the fixed versions.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Certain XML constructs trigger pathological behavior in the streaming parser: a small input causes the parser to do an outsized amount of work. No authentication, privileges, or user interaction are needed - ingesting the input is enough.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The vulnerable pattern, simplified:

// VULNERABLE - unbounded parse of untrusted input
QXmlStreamReader xml(untrustedBytes);
while (!xml.atEnd()) { xml.readNext(); }   // crafted input -> CPU at 100%

// FIXED - bound the work: size limits, timeouts, patched parser
if (untrustedBytes.size() > MAX_XML) { reject(); }
QXmlStreamReader xml(untrustedBytes);      // + parser with the upstream fix

Algorithmic-complexity DoS is cheap for attackers: bytes in, meltdown out. Defenses are input size caps, parse timeouts, and the patched library.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Update Qt to a build containing the QXmlStreamReader fix. As defense in depth, cap accepted XML sizes and enforce parse timeouts on any endpoint that ingests XML.

docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL (9.9) CVSS vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H Product IBM API Connect 10.0.8.0–10.0.8.12 and 12.1.0.0–12.1.1.2 Vulnerability type OS Command Injection (CWE-78), plus 206 sibling flaws in the same advisory

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: IBM API Connect 10.0.8.0 through 10.0.8.12 and 12.1.0.0 through 12.1.1.2.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: IBM published a single advisory, "Multiple Vulnerabilities in IBM API Connect", covering 207 flaws disclosed on 2026-11-07. The lead flaw, CVE-2026-17402, is OS command injection: user-supplied input is passed to the operating system without being neutralized, so a remote authenticated attacker can execute arbitrary commands on the gateway host. The same broken pattern repeats across the advisory: unvalidated input, server-side request forgery, SQL injection, missing authorization, and broken authentication let a low-privilege logged-in user read data, reach other tenants, and run code on the host.

docs.text:
The demo in poc.py models the safe pattern: user input is validated against an allowlist and passed to a fixed command through an argument array, never through a shell string. It runs locally.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: CVE-2026-17466: IBM Optim Path Traversal Information Disclosure
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL (9.1) CVSS vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:L Product IBM Optim 1.0.0, 1.1.0, and 1.2.0 Vulnerability type Path Traversal (CWE-22)

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: IBM Optim does not properly validate file paths supplied by a remote authenticated attacker. A crafted path containing directory-traversal sequences escapes the intended directory and lets the attacker read sensitive files elsewhere on the system. The impact extends beyond the vulnerable component (scope changed), so files outside the application's own data can be exposed.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo in poc.py shows the unsafe pattern (joining a user-supplied path straight onto a base directory) next to the safe pattern (resolving the path and rejecting anything that escapes the base directory). It runs locally on temporary files.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Move to IBM Optim Test Data Management 2.0.0, which validates file paths and resolves these vulnerabilities.
  • Never trust user-supplied file paths: resolve them and verify the result stays inside the intended base directory.
  • Restrict Optim access to authorized users and audit recent file-access logs for traversal attempts.
  • Apply the principle of least privilege to the Optim service account so it cannot read sensitive files outside its data directory.

docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH (7.5) CVSS vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N Product IBM App Connect Enterprise 13.0.1.0 through 13.0.8.2 Vulnerability type Incorrect Authorization (CWE-863)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: IBM App Connect Enterprise 13.0.1.0 through 13.0.8.2.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: IBM App Connect Enterprise has broken access control on its REST API: endpoints that should require authorization return sensitive information to a remote attacker with no login at all. The missing check turns the integration broker's API into an open window onto data that was meant to stay behind authentication.

docs.title: Proof of concept

The demo in poc.py models the fix: every API handler checks the caller's authorization before returning a resource, and unauthenticated requests are rejected. It runs locally.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update to IBM App Connect Enterprise 13.0.9.0 (APAR IT50196).
  • Restrict access to the REST API to trusted networks and authenticated clients only.
  • Rotate any credentials or sensitive data that may have been exposed through the API.
  • Audit every API endpoint for a missing authorization check; an endpoint without one is an endpoint anyone can call.

docs.title: CVE-2026-18450 — Supermicro BMC/IPMI: Unauthenticated Command Execution Cluster
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 (v3.1) Product Supermicro BMC / IPMI firmware — the baseboard management controller inside Supermicro servers Type Missing authentication for critical function (CWE-306) — IPMI commands accepted without integrity/encryption enforcement; cluster includes CWE-798, CWE-78, CWE-269, CWE-696 Vector Attacker reaching the BMC sends crafted IPMI packets that run commands on an active session because integrity and encryption requirements are not enforced. Sibling flaws in the same October 2026 advisory allow opening sessions via a broken RAKP+ handshake (CVE-2026-65219), escalating an account to administrator (CVE-2026-65220, 8.8), OS command injection in BMC functions (CVE-2026-16521), and authenticated file/memory access on the BMC (CVE-2026-65211).

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Supermicro BMC firmware covered by the vendor's October 2026 BMC/IPMI advisories (security_BMC_IPMI_Oct_2026_1 and _2). Apply the October 2026 firmware release for your board model.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The BMC is a second computer inside the server that answers management commands even while the host is off. This cluster breaks the checks that are supposed to gate those commands:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def handle_ipmi(packet, session):
    run_command(packet.command)  # BUG: integrity/encryption not enforced

# Simplified fixed pattern
def handle_ipmi_fixed(packet, session):
    if not session.authenticated or not packet.integrity_ok:
        return deny("unauthenticated or tampered command")
    return run_command(packet.command)
Sibling flaws compound it: a RAKP+ handshake flaw opens sessions, a logic flaw escalates accounts to administrator, and a BMC function passes input to the OS shell. Management-plane power with missing authentication checks means network packets become physical control.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. Attacker reaches a Supermicro BMC over the network.
  2. Attacker sends crafted IPMI packets that skip integrity/encryption enforcement and ride an active session.
  3. A RAKP+ handshake flaw can open a session, or a logic flaw escalates an account to administrator.
  4. The attacker controls power, console, and virtual media — below the OS, surviving reinstalls.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: management commands must be gated by verified session state and packet integrity: the demo contrasts running any packet against requiring an authenticated session with an integrity check. Offline, no server, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Apply the October 2026 Supermicro BMC firmware across the fleet.
  • Isolate every BMC on a private management network with no internet exposure.
  • Change default credentials and disable unused BMC services.
  • Audit BMC session logs for unknown sessions or privilege changes.

docs.title: CVE-2026-19677 — onPhase Forms: Public Registration Auth Bypass to Tenant Admin and RCE
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.3 (v4.0) Product onPhase Forms (frevvo) 11.0.14 — public registration form Type Missing authentication for critical function (CWE-306) — registration endpoint trusts tenant name + user identifier without verifying identity Vector Unauthenticated remote attacker submits the public registration form with a valid tenant name and an existing user identifier → server logs the attacker in as that tenant user → TenantAdmin and Designer privileges granted → arbitrary OS command execution via designer tooling

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: onPhase Forms (frevvo) 11.0.14. Fixed in the vendor's patched release (11.0.14 is vulnerable).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The public registration form exists so strangers can sign up. On the affected release, the registration handler accepted two parameters — a tenant name and a user identifier — and treated them as proof of identity instead of claims that need verification:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def register(params):
    tenant = params["tenant"]        # e.g. "acme"
    user   = params["user_id"]       # e.g. "admin"
    session = login_as(tenant, user) # BUG: no password, token, or signature checked
    return session

# Simplified fixed pattern
def register_fixed(params):
    tenant = params["tenant"]
    user   = params["user_id"]
    if not verify_identity(tenant, user, params["credential"]):
        raise AuthError("identity not proven")
    return login_as(tenant, user)

Anyone who knew a valid tenant name and an existing user identifier could become that user. TenantAdmin and Designer roles followed, and the Designer role's tooling runs arbitrary operating system commands.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. Attacker opens the public registration form (no login required).
  2. Attacker substitutes a valid tenant name and an existing user identifier in the request parameters.
  3. The server skips any credential check and establishes a session as that tenant user.
  4. The attacker now holds TenantAdmin and Designer privileges over the whole tenant.
  5. Via the Designer role's tooling, the attacker executes arbitrary OS commands.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: claiming an identity must not equal proving it: the demo contrasts trusting registration parameters with requiring a credential check. Offline, no server, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Patch now: update onPhase Forms to the vendor's fixed release — 11.0.14 is vulnerable.
  • Disable public registration if your tenants do not need it, or put it behind authentication.
  • Rotate tenant credentials and review every account created or elevated recently.
  • Hunt access logs for registration requests with mismatched or unusual tenant/user parameter pairs.

docs.title: CVE-2026-19678 — onPhase Forms: Unauthenticated SSRF Reaches Internal Apache Solr
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.7 (v4.0) Product onPhase Forms (frevvo) 11.0.14 — unauthenticated form service Type Server-side request forgery (CWE-918) — unauthenticated form service fetches attacker-controlled URL with no allowlist or internal-address check Vector Unauthenticated remote attacker submits a publicly accessible form with an attacker-controlled URL → the server fetches that URL server-side → URL points at the internal Apache Solr instance → Solr trusts the internal request and returns sensitive indexed data

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: onPhase Forms (frevvo) 11.0.14. Fixed in the vendor's patched release (11.0.14 is vulnerable).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The form service fetches user-supplied URLs — a normal feature for link previews and webhooks. The vulnerable release performed that fetch server-side with no boundary checks: no allowlist, no block on internal addresses, no response validation:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def handle_form(form):
    url = form["link"]            # attacker-controlled
    return fetch(url)             # BUG: server fetches ANY url, incl. internal

# Simplified fixed pattern
def handle_form_fixed(form):
    url = form["link"]
    if not allowlisted(url):
        raise ValueError("url not allowlisted")
    if resolves_to_internal(url):
        raise ValueError("internal addresses forbidden")
    return fetch(url)

Because the request originates from the server itself, internal services such as Apache Solr treat it as trusted — turning your server into the attacker's browser inside your own network.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. Attacker finds a public form that accepts a URL field.
  2. Attacker sets the URL to the internal Apache Solr endpoint (e.g. http://solr:8983/...).
  3. The server fetches the URL with no allowlist or internal-address check.
  4. Solr answers the request, which looks fully internal and trusted.
  5. The attacker reads sensitive indexed documents and metadata through the server's response.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: outbound fetches must be fenced: the demo contrasts fetching any URL with an allowlist plus internal-address block. Offline, no server, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Patch now: update onPhase Forms to the vendor's fixed release.
  • Allowlist outbound fetch domains — deny everything else by default.
  • Block internal IP ranges (RFC 1918, link-local, metadata endpoints) on every server-side fetch.
  • Isolate Solr on a network segment the web tier cannot browse directly.
  • Hunt form logs for submissions carrying internal or unusual URLs.

docs.title: CVE-2026-20043 — Snort 3 Memory-Safety Hardening Batch (October 2026)
docs.text:
Cluster writeup. This page is framed around CVE-2026-20043, the lead identifier (CVSS 9.0) of Cisco's October 2026 Snort 3 hardening batch. The same internal review produced a family of CVEs; all are listed under References below and fixed by the same hardening releases.

Field Value Severity CRITICAL 9.0 Product Open Source Snort 3 (Cisco-owned), Cisco Cyber Vision, Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD), Cisco Meraki MX (auto-patched), Cisco CDFW/CSA (auto-patched), UTD IPS engine on Cisco IOS XE Vulnerability type Out-of-bounds write (CWE-787); sibling identifiers cover missing authentication on the control channel socket (CWE-306), plus further memory-safety hardening classes Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• Open Source Snort 3: 3.1.x through 3.12.3.x releases prior to the fix (fixed in 3.12.4.0).
  • Cisco Cyber Vision 3.x through 5.8.x prior to the fix (fixed in 5.6.0 for the 5.6 line — see advisory fixed-release tables per line).
  • Secure FTD 7.0 through 7.7 / 10.x prior to the fixed trains (7.0.10, 7.2.12, 7.4.8, 7.6.6, 7.7.13, 10.0.2, 10.1.0).
  • UTD IPS engine on IOS XE prior to 17.12.8 / 17.15.6 / 17.18.5 / 26.1.2 / 26.2.1.
  • Meraki MX, CDFW, and CSA cloud instances were updated automatically as of October 21, 2026 — no customer action required.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The Snort 3 packet-parsing code computed a length incorrectly and then used it in a copy into a fixed-size buffer without verifying the bounds — a classic out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). Because the parser touches attacker-controlled packet bytes before any detection rule runs, a single crafted packet could corrupt neighboring memory. In the same batch, the control channel socket accepted local connections without any authentication (CVE-2026-76524, CWE-306), letting a low-privilege local user issue commands as the Snort process user and read/write its memory. Cisco found these during an internal review; no malicious exploitation is known.

docs.title: Proof of concept (educational only)
docs.text: poc.py is a safe, self-contained simulation of the concept — a bounded-buffer model in pure Python that shows how a miscalculated length would overrun a buffer in the vulnerable pattern, and how an explicit bounds check neutralizes it. It also models the control-socket lesson: a mock channel that demands caller authentication. It performs no memory corruption, opens no network sockets, touches no real Snort installation, and cannot be turned into a working exploit. Run with python3 poc.py.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade Open Source Snort 3 to 3.12.4.0.
  • Secure FTD: apply the fixed trains (7.0.10, 7.2.12, 7.4.8, 7.6.6, 7.7.13, 10.0.2, 10.1.0 as appropriate for your line).
  • IOS XE with UTD: upgrade to 17.12.8 / 17.15.6 / 17.18.5 / 26.1.2 / 26.2.1.
  • Cyber Vision: migrate to a fixed release per the advisory tables.
  • Meraki / CDFW / CSA: already auto-patched — verify your dashboard shows the updated Snort package.
  • There are no workarounds — upgrading is the only remediation.

docs.title: CVE-2026-28328 — SolarWinds Observability Self-Hosted: Broken Authorization Lets Low-Privilege Users Rewrite What Isn't Theirs
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.8 (v3.1) Product SolarWinds Observability Self-Hosted (Hybrid Cloud Observability, HCO) — on-prem monitoring platform for infrastructure, apps, and networks Type Broken authorization schema (CWE-863) — privilege boundary failure Vector Authenticated low-privileged user accesses and modifies data beyond their assigned permissions → integrity/confidentiality breach of the monitoring estate

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• SolarWinds Observability Self-Hosted prior to the patched release.
  • Fixed in HCO 2026.4 (see release notes).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The authorization schema — the mapping of users to what they may see and change — is broken: permission checks either miss resource types or trust role labels without enforcing them on the data path. The result is a privilege boundary that exists in the UI but not in the API:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def update_alert_rule(user, rule_id, changes):
    rule = get_rule(rule_id)
    # no check that rule belongs to user's scope
    rule.apply(changes)                        # low-priv user edits anything

# Simplified fixed pattern
def update_alert_rule_fixed(user, rule_id, changes):
    rule = get_rule(rule_id)
    if not user.can_write(rule.scope):         # enforced on every data path
        raise PermissionError("outside your assigned permissions")
    rule.apply(changes)

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. The attacker authenticates with a low-privilege account (e.g. read-only dashboard viewer).
  2. They call the management API directly for resources outside their assigned scope — alert rules, monitored nodes, credentials.
  3. The broken authorization schema grants the request: data is read and modified beyond the attacker's permissions.
  4. From there: silence alerts, alter monitoring data, or pivot with credentials the platform stores.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a scope-check model that compares a missing authorization check against an enforced one on synthetic user/resource objects — offline, no server, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update now: SolarWinds Observability Self-Hosted to HCO 2026.4 or later.
  • Review role assignments and audit logs for unauthorized modifications; apply least privilege and re-verify scopes after the upgrade.

docs.title: CVE-2026-3295 — IBM Cloud Pak System: Stored Cross-Site Scripting
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.4 Product IBM Cloud Pak System Type Stored Cross-Site Scripting (CWE-79, OWASP A7:2021 Injection) Vector Authenticated attacker → malicious script stored → executed in victims' browsers (scope changed)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: IBM Cloud Pak System 2.3.6.0 and 2.3.6.1. Apply IBM's security bulletin fix / upgrade beyond 2.3.6.1.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The web console accepts user-supplied input, stores it, and renders it later without sanitizing or HTML-encoding it first:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
save(input)          # stored raw in the app
...
render(input)        # rendered raw — script becomes part of the page!

Because user data and page instructions travel the same road, a script typed into a form becomes part of the console page itself. The browser trusts the console, and the console trusts the input.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. An authenticated attacker submits a crafted payload (e.g. <script>…</script>) into any console input field; the app stores it raw.
  2. Later, an administrator (or any victim) opens the affected page.
  3. The browser executes the stored script automatically — no clicks, no warnings — inside the trusted admin session.
  4. Consequences: session tokens stolen, console actions forged, cloud infrastructure reconfigured.

The accompanying poc.py in this folder demonstrates the pattern safely: it models the store-then-render pipeline with synthetic data and shows how raw rendering lets a payload survive into the page versus how output encoding neutralizes it — all offline, no browser, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Apply IBM's security bulletin fix — upgrade beyond 2.3.6.1; do not stay on 2.3.6.0/2.3.6.1.
  • Audit admin accounts and session logs for suspicious activity around console pages.
  • Treat all console inputs as hostile: sanitize on input, encode on output, and enforce Content Security Policy.
  • Review stored records that may already contain injected markup.

docs.title: CVE-2026-33923 — Signature Verification Bypass in Nozomi Guardian/CMC Updates
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH 7.2 Product Nozomi Networks Guardian, CMC Type Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature (CWE-347) Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Published 2026-10-29

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Guardian and CMC before 26.4.0. Fixed in 26.4.0 and later. Companion issue: CVE-2026-33924 (OS command injection in the same installer).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The update installation functionality validates the contents of an update bundle inconsistently. A crafted bundle can pass signature verification while still containing an unsigned script, which the installer then runs with root privileges. An attacker with administrative privileges on the appliance can supply such a bundle remotely.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only. The demo below is a local simulation of the validation logic — a bundle manifest check that verifies the outer signature but never re-checks the files inside — with no appliance, no firmware, and no network access.

See poc.py. Run it with python3 poc.py. It demonstrates:

  1. A bundle whose outer signature verifies but whose inner script is unsigned.
  2. A fixed installer that verifies every file before installing anything.
  3. Why "signed container" must never imply "every file inside is signed".

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade Guardian and CMC to 26.4.0 or later.
  • Use the internal firewall features to limit access to the web management interface.
  • Review all accounts with administrative privileges and delete unnecessary ones.
  • Install update bundles only from trusted Nozomi Networks sources.

docs.title: CVE-2026-33924 — OS Command Injection in Nozomi Guardian/CMC Updates
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH 7.2 Product Nozomi Networks Guardian, CMC Type OS Command Injection (CWE-78) Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Published 2026-10-29

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Guardian and CMC before 26.4.0. Fixed in 26.4.0 and later. Companion issue: CVE-2026-33923 (signature verification bypass in the same installer).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The update installation functionality does not sufficiently validate the contents of an update bundle. Fields from the bundle are used in operating system commands without neutralization, so a crafted bundle supplied by an attacker with administrative privileges causes arbitrary commands to execute with root privileges when the bundle is installed.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only. The demo below is a local simulation of the pattern — bundle fields interpolated into a shell command versus passed as data — with no appliance, no firmware, and no command actually executed.

See poc.py. Run it with python3 poc.py. It demonstrates:

  1. How an unvalidated bundle field can break out of a shell command string.
  2. How passing the same field as an argument keeps it harmless data.
  3. Why installer inputs must be treated as untrusted data, never as commands.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade Guardian and CMC to 26.4.0 or later.
  • Use the internal firewall features to limit access to the web management interface.
  • Review all accounts with administrative privileges and delete unnecessary ones.
  • Install update bundles only from trusted Nozomi Networks sources.

docs.title: CVE-2026-42922 — FUXA: Authorization Bypass to Remote Code Execution via Node-RED
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL 9.8 (CVSS 3.1) Product FUXA web-based HMI (frangoteam) Type Improper Authorization (CWE-285) Vector Network, unauthenticated, no user interaction

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The authorization callback guarding the /nodered routes verifies that a token is correctly signed, but it never checks the holder's permission level. Separately, the public /api/heartbeat route mints valid guest tokens for unauthenticated callers. Any guest token therefore passes the gate, giving unauthenticated users access to the Node-RED deployment, where deployed flows can execute arbitrary commands on the host.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text: See poc.py. It is an educational, fully local simulation: mock objects reproduce the decision logic (signature-only check, public guest-token minting, missing permission check) and contrast it with the fixed logic (guest tokens rejected, authenticated non-guest user or valid API key required). It makes no network requests and deploys no flows.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update FUXA to version 1.3.3, where the middleware rejects guest tokens and refresh tokens and requires an authenticated non-guest user or a valid API key.
  • Never expose a FUXA panel to the public internet; put it behind a VPN and firewall it to operator networks only.
  • Audit Node-RED flows for anything you did not deploy, and rotate credentials and API keys.

docs.title: CVE-2026-43850 (cluster CVE-2026-43849…43858) — Advantech ADAM-3600 EdgeLink: 10 Flaws, Root for the Taking
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.6 (headliners); batch includes 6.3–8.6 Product Advantech ADAM-3600 EdgeLink — wireless remote terminal unit (RTU) for industrial data acquisition and remote monitoring (manufacturing, utilities, energy) Type Command injection (CWE-78), stack/heap buffer overflows (CWE-121/122), path traversal (CWE-22), credential exposure (CWE-200), assertion DoS Vector Authenticated remote attacker (some bugs unauthenticated) → root-level code execution, arbitrary file read/write, crashes, credential theft

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• ADAM-3600 EdgeLink firmware prior to 2.8.5.0.
  • Fixed in firmware 2.8.5.0+ (patched by Advantech 2026-10-15).

docs.title: The batch
docs.text: CVE CVSS Bug CVE-2026-43850 8.6 Command injection → root-level code execution (authenticated) CVE-2026-43856 8.6 Stack buffer overflow in FileProcess::CheckDir — path longer than 1024 bytes → code execution CVE-2026-43857 8.6 Remote authenticated arbitrary code execution with service privileges CVE-2026-43858 8.6 Stack-based buffer overflow → remote authenticated code execution CVE-2026-43851 8.2 Path traversal → read arbitrary files (authenticated) CVE-2026-43852 8.2 Write files to arbitrary locations (authenticated) CVE-2026-43853 8.2 Crafted message triggers assertion fault → service crash (DoS) CVE-2026-43855 7.5 Heap-based buffer overflow → remote authenticated code execution CVE-2026-43849 6.9 Heap memory read → sensitive data exfiltration CVE-2026-43854 6.3 Encrypted project file yields administrator credentials for EdgeLink devices

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Management input flows straight into operating-system commands without sanitization, fixed-size stack buffers take unbounded paths, and traversal guards are missing in both directions — embedded-device code that would never survive a web-application review, guarding physical infrastructure:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def run_diagnostic(user_input):
    os.system(f"diag --target {user_input}")   # injection -> root shell

def check_dir(path):                            # FileProcess::CheckDir
    buf = bytearray(1024)
    buf[:len(path)] = path.encode()             # path > 1024 -> stack smash

# Simplified fixed pattern
def run_diagnostic_fixed(user_input):
    run(["diag", "--target"], args=[validated(user_input)])  # no shell

def check_dir_fixed(path):
    if len(path) > 1024: raise ValueError()     # bounds checked

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The headline attack chain (CVE-2026-43850) is:

  1. The attacker authenticates to the device's management interface.
  2. They submit crafted input through a management function.
  3. The device interpolates the input into an OS command unsanitized.
  4. The injected command runs — as root — giving full device control; from an owned RTU, the attacker pivots into the plant network.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: shell-string interpolation versus argument-vector execution, and a fixed-buffer copy versus a bounds-checked one — all synthetic, offline, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update now: ADAM-3600 EdgeLink firmware to 2.8.5.0 or later immediately.
  • Remove internet exposure of industrial devices; segment the control network (IT/OT separation); restrict administrative access.
  • Rotate credentials that may have lived in project files.

docs.title: CVE-2026-44179 — XWiki Remote Macros: Syntax Injection via Excerpt-Include Macro
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.9 Product XWiki Remote Macros (xwiki-pro-macros) — Confluence migration rendering macros Type Improper neutralization of input / code injection (CWE-95) — macro content executed with the macro's rights Vector User able to edit a page (no script or programming rights needed) plants macro syntax in a page title or excerpt → a page including that excerpt renders it → code executes with the macro's privileges

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: XWiki Remote Macros from 1.13 until 1.14.5. Fixed in 1.14.5.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The excerpt-include macro renders included content as wiki syntax instead of plain text, and does not escape the included page's title. User-supplied text therefore crosses the line from content to code:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def render_excerpt(title, excerpt):
    page = title + excerpt      # BUG: title not escaped
    return execute_macros(page)  # runs with macro rights

# Simplified fixed pattern
def render_excerpt_fixed(title, excerpt):
    page = escape(title) + escape(excerpt)
    return render_as_text(page)  # content stays content
Content and code must be kept apart: escape user text before rendering, and never execute included content with elevated rights.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
1. An editor (no script rights needed) plants macro syntax in a page title or excerpt.
  2. Another page includes that excerpt through the excerpt-include macro.
  3. The wiki renders the planted syntax and executes it with the macro's rights.
  4. The attacker reads restricted pages or escalates further.

See poc.py for a safe, offline demo of content rendered as code: the demo contrasts executing included text with escaping it and rendering it as plain text.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade now: XWiki Remote Macros 1.14.5 or later.
  • Audit recently edited pages for suspicious macro syntax in titles and excerpts.
  • Limit who can edit shared pages, and review macro usage on migrated content.

docs.title: CVE-2026-45049: OpenAM Cross-Domain SSO Session Token Leak
docs.text: Field Detail Severity High — CVSS 8.3 Product OpenAM (Open Identity Platform) — access management / single sign-on Type Exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor (CWE-201) — session token posted to an attacker-controlled URL Vector Attacker induces an authenticated victim to visit a crafted URL → CDSSO servlet posts the victim's raw session token to the attacker's server → session hijacking

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: OpenAM before 16.1.1 with Cross-Domain Single Sign-On (CDSSO) enabled and a non-default protective configuration absent. Fixed in 16.1.1.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The CDSSO servlet is designed to share a login session across trusted domains. When CDSSO is enabled and one protective setting is missing, the servlet does not strictly confine where the raw session token may be sent, so a crafted URL can make it post the token to an attacker-controlled address. A session token is a bearer credential: whoever holds it is treated as the user.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def cdsso_post(token, destination):
    # BUG: destination not confined to trusted domains
    return post(destination, {"token": token})

# Simplified fixed pattern
def cdsso_post_fixed(token, destination, trusted_domains):
    if destination not in trusted_domains:
        raise ValueError("untrusted destination")
    return post(destination, {"token": token})

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
1. Victim logs into an OpenAM deployment with CDSSO enabled.
  2. Attacker crafts a URL that triggers the CDSSO servlet.
  3. Victim visits the crafted URL while authenticated.
  4. The servlet posts the victim's raw session token to the attacker's server.
  5. Attacker replays the token and acts as the victim.

The educational demo in poc.py illustrates why a bearer token must only ever travel to allow-listed trusted domains.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade now: OpenAM 16.1.1 or later.
  • Disable CDSSO if your deployment does not need cross-domain login.
  • Allow-list only your own domains as token destinations.
  • Revoke active sessions after patching.

docs.title: CVE-2026-50053 — Zimbra: Forged Request Details Hijack Signed-In Sessions (8.7)
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.7 (v3.1) Product Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) Type Request attribute override (improper control of internal state) — unauthenticated Vector Unauthenticated requests to /h/* can populate servlet attributes intended for trusted internal dispatch: RestFilter copies URL parameters specifying an authentication token, target account, target item, and dispatch state into request attributes consumed by the Classic Web Client. Combined with a cross-site scripting flaw on ZCS 10.1.16, an attacker can supply their own valid token and document identifiers and execute JavaScript in another user signed-in browser session.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Zimbra Collaboration Suite — ZCS 10.1.17 blocks the combined scripting chain by changing the document renderer, but retains the request attribute override; apply the latest ZCS security patch.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Internal dispatch state was populated from untrusted URL parameters instead of being set only by trusted internal code. The boundary between "what the user asked for" and "what the server decided internally" was erased, so forged attributes flowed straight into the web client session handling.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The vulnerable pattern, simplified:

# VULNERABLE - internal attributes copied from URL parameters
# request.attrs["auth_token"] = params["token"]   # attacker-controlled
# FIXED - internal attributes set only by trusted code paths
# request.attrs["auth_token"] = session.token    # server-side only

The demo poc.py below contrasts a dispatcher that trusts URL parameters with one that only accepts server-side values.

The demo poc.py below illustrates the vulnerable pattern against the fixed pattern with purely synthetic, offline objects — no real product, no network, no exploit.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Apply the latest Zimbra security patch, and treat any Classic Web Client deployment as exposed until patched: audit /h/* access and review session handling.
