docs.title: CVE-2026-50240: OpenShift Pipelines-as-Code Runs Attacker Pipelines as Cluster Admin
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH (8.8) CVSS vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Product OpenShift Pipelines-as-Code Vulnerability type Missing Authorization (CWE-862)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: OpenShift Pipelines-as-Code (see the Red Hat advisory for affected and fixed releases)

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Pipelines-as-Code does not verify whether the creator of a Repository custom resource has permission to create PipelineRuns. A namespace user with only Repository and Secret create/delete permissions can cause Pipelines-as-Code to execute attacker-controlled PipelineRuns as the auto-provisioned pipeline ServiceAccount, which carries ClusterRole/edit by default. This results in namespace-scoped privilege escalation, enabling secret reads, resource creation/modification/deletion, and potential supply chain injection in CI/CD namespaces.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo in poc.py models the safe pattern: before executing a pipeline, the controller verifies that the Repository creator is authorized to create PipelineRuns in that namespace; unauthorized requests are refused. It runs locally.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Apply the fixed Pipelines-as-Code release from the Red Hat advisory.
  • Restrict who can create Repository custom resources in CI/CD namespaces.
  • Audit the auto-provisioned pipeline ServiceAccount roles and apply least privilege.
  • Review recent PipelineRuns for runs triggered by low-privilege users.

docs.title: CVE-2026-52848 — GLPI One-Time-Password Verification Bypass
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL — CVSS 4.0: 9.2 Product GLPI IT asset management software Type Authentication bypass by capture-replay / improper authentication (CWE-288) Vector Network, low complexity, unauthenticated during the login phase Affected versions 11.0.0 through 11.0.8 Fixed version 11.0.8

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: GLPI from 11.0.0 until 11.0.8. The flaw is in the login phase, where a crafted URL can skip one-time-password verification.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: During login, the one-time-password step is a separate phase of the flow rather than a gate that every login must pass. A crafted URL aimed at the login phase skips that step, so the second factor is never verified and the session is granted anyway. Two-factor authentication therefore protects the account on paper but not in practice for logins that take this shortcut.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation with no network traffic, how a login flow that lets a crafted request jump past the code step grants a session, and how a fixed flow that always requires the code breaks the chain.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. The attacker reaches the GLPI login flow.
  2. The attacker uses a crafted address aimed at the login phase.
  3. The one-time-password step is skipped and never verified.
  4. A session is granted, defeating the account's two-factor protection and exposing tickets, asset records, and internal details.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update GLPI to 11.0.8 now.
  • Review recent login history for sessions that lack a one-time-password verification, and treat them as suspect.
  • Reset passwords on accounts with unusual logins, and re-enrol two-factor authentication where you cannot confirm the session.
  • Alert on logins from unusual locations or at unusual hours.

docs.title: CVE-2026-53921 — odhcpd on OpenWrt: One Packet, Root on the Router (9.8)
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 (v3.1) Product odhcpd (DHCPv6/DHCPv4/router-advertisement server used by OpenWrt) — before 25.12 Type Stack-based buffer overflow — unauthenticated, network-reachable Vector odhcpd DHCPv6 IA response handler writes past the end of a fixed 512-byte stack buffer when a single DHCPv6 REQUEST carries enough IA options to nearly exhaust the reply space. Two independent overflow sites exist in the same call chain, both reachable from the network via a single unauthenticated UDP packet. odhcpd runs as root on OpenWrt, and embedded targets often lack stack canaries and ASLR.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: odhcpd before 25.12. Fixed in 25.12.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: A reply was built into a small fixed-size stack buffer without checking whether the accumulated options would fit. The overflow is reachable from an unauthenticated network packet, in a root service on devices with few exploit mitigations.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The vulnerable pattern, simplified:

/* VULNERABLE - fixed buffer, no length check */
char pdbuf[512];
/* append option after option... */
/* FIXED - check remaining space before every append */
if (len + optlen > sizeof(pdbuf)) return -1;  /* illustrative */

The demo poc.py below contrasts an unchecked append into a fixed buffer with a length-checked one.

The demo poc.py below illustrates the vulnerable pattern against the fixed pattern with purely synthetic, offline objects — no real product, no network, no exploit.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Update odhcpd to 25.12 on every OpenWrt device you manage, and limit network reach to the DHCP service until patched.

docs.title: CVE-2026-53942 — Conda Infrastructure: a Comment Hijacks the Build (9.9)
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.9 (v3.1) Product conda/infrastructure (Conda organization infrastructure) — before commit 9c0f238 Type GitHub Actions pwn request (code injection via untrusted input) — unauthenticated Vector The update workflow triggers on issue_comment events containing "@conda-bot render" or "@conda-bot recreate". For the render path it checks out the pull request head repository/branch using a privileged sync token, then runs an external template action that reads templates from the checked-out directory with an unsandboxed Jinja2 environment — so attacker-controlled template content becomes code execution in a privileged runner.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: conda/infrastructure before commit 9c0f238. Fixed by commit 9c0f238.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Two trust levels were mixed in one workflow: the trigger and the templates came from untrusted pull request authors, while the checkout token and runner privileges came from the project. An unsandboxed template renderer closed the gap, turning template text into live code.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The vulnerable pattern, simplified:

# VULNERABLE - untrusted template rendered with full template power
# render(template_from_pr, sandbox=False)   # illustrative
# FIXED - sandbox the renderer and never render untrusted templates
# render(template_from_pr, sandbox=True)    # illustrative

The demo poc.py below shows a template engine with and without sandboxing: the unsandboxed path lets template text reach dangerous operations, the sandboxed path blocks them.

The demo poc.py below illustrates the vulnerable pattern against the fixed pattern with purely synthetic, offline objects — no real product, no network, no exploit.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Apply commit 9c0f238. Never check out pull request code in a workflow that holds secrets, gate bot commands to trusted authors, sandbox every template renderer, and rotate any token that ran in an exposed workflow.

docs.title: CVE-2026-53995 - MLflow: Unauthenticated Path Traversal in FileStore Traces
docs.text: Field Value Severity High - CVSS 8.2 Product MLflow through 3.17.1 (ML experiment tracking) Type Path Traversal (CWE-22) Vector Unauthenticated POST to /api/3.0/mlflow/traces with crafted trace ID

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: MLflow through 3.17.1.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: FileStore.start_trace() used the caller-supplied trace ID directly as a filesystem path. An unauthenticated attacker could submit a trace ID containing ../ sequences to POST /api/3.0/mlflow/traces, causing the server to write trace_info.yaml, request_metadata, and tag files with attacker-controlled metadata outside the experiment trace directory. FileStore is the default tracking backend before MLflow 3.7.0.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. Attacker POSTs to /api/3.0/mlflow/traces with a trace ID like ....//....//evil.
  2. FileStore.start_trace() builds paths from the raw trace ID, no sanitization.
  3. trace_info.yaml and tag files land outside the trace directory.
  4. Attacker writes arbitrary files within the server process permissions.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a vulnerable mock versus the fixed pattern. Fully offline, synthetic data - no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Upgrade MLflow past the fixed release (see fix PR mlflow/mlflow#26842). Validate trace IDs server-side (allowlist of safe characters), run the tracking server behind authentication, and never expose an MLflow tracking server unauthenticated to a network. Audit the artifact store for unexpected files written outside experiment directories.

docs.title: CVE-2026-54349: Chartbrew SQL Injection via Dashboard URL Filters
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL (9.8) CVSS vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Product Chartbrew Vulnerability type SQL Injection (CWE-89)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Chartbrew before 5.2.1

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: SQL dashboard-variable substitution used attacker-controlled JavaScript replacement strings unsafely across SQL connectors, and separately failed to escape backslashes for MySQL and MariaDB quoted contexts. The vulnerable surface is public and embedded dashboard/chart requests that call the variable-substitution helper. An unauthenticated user sends crafted URL filter values to a public or embedded chart backed by a stored SQL query: replacement-string dollar sequences can alter the SQL independently of the database engine, while MySQL and MariaDB backslash handling provides a second quoted-string escape path. Injected SQL can read, modify, or delete data available to the configured database account.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo in poc.py models the safe pattern: dashboard filters are bound as query parameters against an allow-listed column, never pasted into the SQL text. It runs locally against an in-memory database.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Chartbrew to 5.2.1 immediately.
  • Audit every public and embedded chart that takes URL-controlled variables in a SQL query.
  • Give the configured database account only the minimum rights it needs (no write access where charts only read).
  • Prefer parameterized queries everywhere user input reaches SQL.

docs.title: CVE-2026-56065 — Doofinder for WooCommerce Sensitive Data Exposure
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH 7.5 Product Doofinder for WooCommerce Type Sensitive information in externally accessible file (CWE-538) Vector Unauthenticated direct request for a plugin-generated file

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Versions up to 2.17.2.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The plugin writes sensitive information into a file that is externally accessible. The generated file embeds sensitive data and is served by the web server without authentication, at a predictable path. Anyone who finds the file path can simply download it and read the embedded data — no login, no exploit, just a public link.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational, conceptual demonstration only. This is not a working exploit.

# Conceptual flow (no real requests, no real site):
# 1. Plugin generates a file embedding sensitive data.
# 2. The file is placed under the web root and served without authentication.
# 3. Attacker requests the predictable file path directly.
# 4. Server returns the file; attacker reads the embedded sensitive data.

The key lesson: sensitive data must never live in a file the web server can serve, and generated files must be stored outside the web root or protected.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update the plugin past version 2.17.2.
  • Delete or rotate any data that was exposed in the file.
  • Block direct access to plugin-generated files on your server.
  • Audit access logs for downloads of the file.

docs.title: PraisonAI Multi-Agent Authorization Flaws — 8 CVEs fixed in 4.6.59
docs.text:
Field Value Severity HIGH — CVSS up to 8.8 (lead: CVE-2026-56840) Product PraisonAI multi-agent teams framework, before 4.6.59 Vulnerability type Broken authorization / approval gates (XSS, improper auth, path traversal, command injection) Attack vector Network — varies per flaw (chat channels, webhooks, dashboard, streaming runner)

Covered CVEs: CVE-2026-56840 (8.8), CVE-2026-56832 (8.8), CVE-2026-56837 (8.6), CVE-2026-56835 (8.3), CVE-2026-56836 (8.2), CVE-2026-56838 (7.8), CVE-2026-56834 (7.5), CVE-2026-56833 (7.5).

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: PraisonAI before 4.6.59 (version windows vary per flaw; all fixed in 4.6.59).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
PraisonAI agents must ask a human to approve dangerous tool calls — but the approval gates themselves were broken in eight ways:

  1. CVE-2026-56840 (8.8, XSS): the HTTP approval dashboard rendered pending tool approval arguments directly into HTML. An attacker-controlled argument injected JavaScript that ran in the reviewer's browser when they opened the approval page.
  2. CVE-2026-56832 (8.8, insufficient verification): DiscordApproval approved a pending dangerous tool call on ANY later non-bot message in the channel classified as approval (e.g. "yes") — so any user who could post in the approval channel could approve high-risk calls.
  3. CVE-2026-56837 (8.6, improper auth): LinearBot bound a webhook listener to 0.0.0.0 and treated LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET as optional; without it, signature verification was skipped entirely.
  4. CVE-2026-56835 (8.3, missing authorization): the Slack bot enforced its allowed_users/allowed_channels policy in the normal message handler but not in the app_mention handler — mentioning the bot bypassed the allowlist.
  5. CVE-2026-56836 (8.2, improper auth): the deprecated Typer console entrypoint for praisonai recipe serve could start the recipe HTTP server path with weaker checks.
  6. CVE-2026-56838 (7.8, OS command injection): recipe.run() enforced the dangerous-tools policy, but the streaming path recipe.run_stream() skipped the policy check — streaming recipes could run default-denied tools.
  7. CVE-2026-56834 (7.5, path traversal): Dynamic Context Discovery artifact tools did not confine artifact_path under the configured artifact directory.
  8. CVE-2026-56833 (7.5, path traversal): Dynamic Context filesystem history/terminal-log tools joined caller-supplied run_id/agent_id into paths without validation.

The common lesson: an approval gate is only real when the reviewer, the channel, and the rendered page are ALL locked down.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational-only conceptual walkthrough — no working exploit.

  • Approval hijack (56832): attacker queues a risky tool call, then posts "yes" from any account in the configured Discord channel; the pending call is approved.
  • Forged webhook (56837): with no secret configured, an unauthenticated caller sends a crafted webhook event to the public listener; it is accepted without signature verification.
  • Dashboard XSS (56840): attacker hides JavaScript in a tool argument; when the human opens the approval URL to review the request, the script executes in the dashboard origin.
  • Policy skip (56838): a recipe that is blocked on the normal runner executes its dangerous tools when run through the streaming runner.

Illustrative vulnerable-vs-fixed pattern (Python, educational pseudocode):

# VULNERABLE: any channel message counts as approval
if classify(message.text) == "approval" and not message.is_bot:
    approve(pending_call)

# FIXED: only the designated reviewer, verified identity
if message.author.id == REVIEWER_ID and verify_signature(message):
    approve(pending_call)

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade to PraisonAI 4.6.59 (fixes all eight).
  • Lock approval channels to trusted reviewers only; never approve on unauthenticated chat messages.
  • Require webhook secrets everywhere; fail closed when absent.
  • Enforce allowlists on EVERY handler path, not just the main one.
  • Confine artifact/history paths under configured base directories.
  • Treat agent framework config as security-critical infrastructure.

docs.title: CVE-2026-57155 — OPNsense GeoIP Importer Path Traversal
docs.text: Field Detail Severity Critical 9.9 (CVSS 3.1) Product OPNsense Firewall — GeoIP importer Type Path traversal (CWE-22) → remote code execution as root Attack vector Network · low privileges (firewall alias edit rights)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: OPNsense versions prior to 26.1.11. Fixed in 26.1.11.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The GeoIP country importer takes the country_code value straight from the downloaded archive and concatenates it into a filesystem path — with no validation at all:

out = GEODIR + country + '-IPv4'
open(out, 'w')   # country is attacker-controlled

A value like ../../cron.d/evil walks out of the GeoIP directory. The importer runs as root, so the attacker's file lands anywhere on the system with root ownership.

The chain completes with a crafted log configuration plus an oversized log file, which tricks the hourly root cron job into executing the attacker's commands.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
poc.py is an educational illustration of the flawed pattern versus the fix. It runs safely — string-level only, no real filesystem writes.

python3 poc.py

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. Attacker hosts a malicious GeoIP archive on their own server.
  2. With firewall alias edit rights, they point the GeoIP source at it.
  3. The archive carries country_code = ../../cron.d/evil.
  4. The root importer writes the file outside the GeoIP folder.
  5. A crafted log config + oversized log makes the hourly root cron run it.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update to OPNsense 26.1.11 — the complete fix (input is validated before any path is built).
  • Until then: restrict who can edit firewall aliases, use only trusted GeoIP sources, and keep the management interface off the internet.

docs.text: Watch the explainer Short

docs.title: CVE-2026-57845 — Hugging Face Datasets: a Dataset File That Runs Code (8.8)
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.8 (v3.1) Product Hugging Face Datasets — through 5.1.0 Type Insecure deserialization (pickle) — victim must load a crafted dataset Vector The deprecated pandas dataset builder processes pickle-backed datasets via pandas.read_pickle() without validation, so when a victim calls load_dataset with the pandas builder on attacker-supplied data files, the embedded payload executes arbitrary Python code with the victim process privileges.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Hugging Face Datasets through 5.1.0. Update past 5.1.0 and stop using the deprecated pandas builder.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Python pickle is not a data format — it is a program: unpickling rebuilds objects and runs embedded instructions. The old builder handed stranger-supplied files to the pickle loader with no validation, treating executable content as plain data.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The vulnerable pattern, simplified:

# VULNERABLE - pickle on untrusted input
# import pickle; pickle.loads(untrusted_bytes)   # runs embedded code
# FIXED - use a data-only format (Parquet/Arrow/JSON)
# import pyarrow.parquet as pq; pq.read_table(path)

The demo poc.py below contrasts loading untrusted bytes with pickle against loading the same data as plain JSON.

The demo poc.py below illustrates the vulnerable pattern against the fixed pattern with purely synthetic, offline objects — no real product, no network, no exploit.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Stop using the deprecated pandas builder, update past 5.1.0, only load datasets from publishers you trust, and prefer data-only formats such as Parquet or Arrow.

docs.title: CVE-2026-61564 — AVideo Encoder Installer Code Injection (CVSS 10.0)
docs.text: Field Detail Severity CRITICAL — CVSS 3.1: 10.0 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H) Product AVideo Encoder (WWBN/AVideo-Encoder) Type Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Template Engine / Code Injection (CWE-94) Vector Network, unauthenticated, no user interaction

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: AVideo Encoder prior to 8.1.0. Fixed in 8.1.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: On a fresh deployment, the unauthenticated installer endpoint install/checkConfiguration.php builds videos/configuration.php by interpolating request parameters (including the site root URL) into single-quoted PHP string literals without escaping. A value that terminates the quote breaks out of the string literal and becomes PHP code in the generated, directly requestable file. Exploitation requires videos/configuration.php to be absent (as on every fresh deployment, or after the file is removed or moved); an existing file blocks this endpoint. The attacker needs no target credentials and can point the database parameters at their own database server. The endpoint also interpolates request values into streamer and configuration INSERT statements, a secondary SQL-injection sink.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text: Educational and conceptual only — see poc.py. It demonstrates, entirely locally and without sending any request to a real target, how an unescaped value breaks out of a quoted template and how escaping / fixed templates prevent it. It does not exploit any system and must only be run in a controlled environment.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update AVideo Encoder to version 8.1.0.
  • If the encoder was ever exposed before patching, assume the generated configuration was touched: rebuild it cleanly and rotate database and streamer credentials.
  • Remove or restrict the installer endpoint once setup is complete.
  • Monitor logs for unexpected installer / setup requests.

docs.title: CVE-2026-61567 — AVideo Encoder Live-Stream Command Injection (CVSS 10.0)
docs.text: Field Detail Severity CRITICAL — CVSS 3.1: 10.0 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H) Product AVideo Encoder (WWBN/AVideo-Encoder) Type Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command (CWE-78) Vector Network, unauthenticated, no user interaction

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: AVideo Encoder prior to 8.1.0. Fixed in 8.1.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The live-streaming endpoint view/videosListToLive.php accepts an attacker-named streamer, trusts the JSON returned by an attacker-reachable HTTP service as session state, and self-grants streaming privileges without legitimate credentials — the API secret is forwarded rather than checked against a stored secret, and the operator streamer allowlist is never consulted on this path. It then interpolates video paths from the attacker-controlled video list, without shell argument escaping, into ffprobe / ffmpeg commands passed to exec. Paths containing shell delimiters therefore execute arbitrary operating-system commands as the web-server user, disclosing database and stored streamer credentials and enabling persistence.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text: Educational and conceptual only — see poc.py. It demonstrates, entirely locally and without sending any request to a real target, how an unescaped path reaches a shell command and how argument lists / shlex.quote prevent it. It does not exploit any system and must only be run in a controlled environment.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update AVideo Encoder to version 8.1.0.
  • Rotate database and streamer credentials if the encoder was exposed before patching, since stolen streamer credentials can provide continued upstream access until rotated.
  • Enforce a streamer allowlist and verify API secrets against stored values; never trust session state returned by a caller-controlled service.
  • Pass command arguments as a list (no shell) and escape any value that must reach a shell.

docs.title: CVE-2026-61707: SOCFortress CoPilot Template Upload to Root RCE
docs.text: Field Detail Severity Critical — CVSS 9.0 Product SOCFortress CoPilot — security operations platform (single pane of glass for SOC teams) Type Code injection (CWE-94) / missing authorization (CWE-862) / template injection (CWE-1336) — unsandboxed template rendering of attacker-controlled uploads Vector Lowest-privilege customer_user uploads a crafted case-report template (filename-only check, shared store, no per-customer scoping) → admin/analyst generates a report → unsandboxed engine evaluates template expressions as Python → root code execution, all tenants' data and connector credentials exposed

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: SOCFortress CoPilot before 0.1.76. Fixed in 0.1.76.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The template upload route validates only the filename-derived MIME type, never the template content, and templates share a global store with no per-customer scoping — a low-privilege user can even list, download, delete, and replace legitimate default templates. Report generation then renders those templates in engines with no sandbox, so template expressions run as real Python on the backend. In the reported deployment that code runs as root, and the document renderer additionally permits local-file reads and requests to internal services.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def generate_report(template_text, context):
    # BUG: unsandboxed engine renders attacker-controlled template
    return render_template(template_text, context)  # expressions = code

# Simplified fixed pattern
def generate_report_fixed(template_text, context, owner):
    if template_text.owner != owner:
        raise PermissionError("not your template")
    return render_sandboxed(template_text, context)  # no code execution

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
1. A lowest-privilege customer_user uploads a crafted report template.
  2. The template lands in the shared store (optionally replacing a default).
  3. An admin or analyst generates a case report from that template.
  4. The unsandboxed engine evaluates the attacker's expressions as Python.
  5. Code runs as root: all tenants' incident/SIEM data and connector credentials exposed.

The educational demo in poc.py illustrates why rendering a template without a sandbox is code execution, and why upload checks must inspect content, not filenames.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade now: SOCFortress CoPilot 0.1.76 or later.
  • Sandbox all template rendering and enable autoescaping.
  • Scope templates per customer and audit every stored template for injected expressions.
  • Rotate connector credentials that were reachable from the platform.

docs.title: CVE-2026-62048 — WordPress BookIt Unauthenticated SQL Injection
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL (CVSS 3.1: 9.3) Product Liquid Web / StellarWP BookIt (WordPress plugin) Type SQL Injection (CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command) Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:L Published 2026-11-01

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: BookIt: from n/a through 2.6.0.6.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The BookIt booking plugin fails to neutralize special elements in user-supplied input before using it in an SQL command. A crafted booking request can therefore inject SQL, and because the flaw is reachable without authentication, any remote visitor can reach the database layer. docs.text:
• Update BookIt past 2.6.0.6 as soon as a fixed release is available.
  • Audit recent booking requests and database logs for unexpected query patterns.
  • Apply the principle of least privilege to the WordPress database user so a web-facing account cannot read unrelated tables.
  • Consider a web application firewall rule blocking SQL metacharacters in booking parameters until patched.

docs.title: CVE-2026-62662 — Pocket ID OIDC Audience Confusion
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH — CVSS 3.0: 7.7 Product Pocket ID (self-hosted OIDC provider) Type Improper input validation (CWE-20) Vector CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N Affected versions 1.11.0 through 2.10.0 (before 2.10.0) Fixed version 2.10.0

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Pocket ID from 1.11.0 until 2.10.0. Deployments that do not use Pocket ID access tokens for resource-server authorization have no immediate exploitable impact.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: createTokenFromClientCredentials accepts the client-controlled resource parameter and embeds it directly in the access token's aud claim, without validating that the audience is registered or that the requesting client may access it. Any authenticated OIDC client can therefore obtain a Pocket ID-signed token naming another client or an arbitrary audience. The /api/oidc/introspect endpoint cannot distinguish the unauthorized token, because it treats a token as active when the introspecting client's identifier matches the attacker-selected audience. The signature is genuine; the audience is fiction.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation, how a token issuer that copies a client-supplied audience into a signed token lets one client mint credentials for another service, and how the fixed version (server-side audience validation) breaks the chain.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. An authenticated OIDC client requests a token, passing a resource parameter naming a different service.
  2. Pocket ID embeds that value in the token's aud claim and signs it, without validation.
  3. The target resource server sees a genuine Pocket ID signature and the audience it expects, and accepts the token.
  4. Audience-based access controls are bypassed, permitting unauthorized data access or actions.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Pocket ID to 2.10.0 or later now.
  • Validate every audience server side: only issue tokens for audiences the client is registered and authorized for.
  • Never trust an access token for resource-server authorization without checking that its audience was server-validated.
  • Audit tokens issued to clients for audiences outside their registration.

docs.title: CVE-2026-62863 — MoLing MCP Server Missing Authentication in SSE Mode
docs.text: Field Detail Severity CRITICAL 9.6 (CVSS 3.1) Product MoLing MCP server, before 0.5.0 Type Missing authentication / permissive cross-domain policy (CWE-306, CWE-942) Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:L

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: MoLing before 0.5.0, when running in SSE mode with -l. Fixed in 0.5.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: In SSE mode, the /sse and /message HTTP endpoints do not authenticate requests, and the mcp-go dependency sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. A malicious web page can open a cross-origin EventSource to /sse, including a loopback listener, and read the endpoint event to obtain a session identifier. After a victim running SSE mode visits that page, the attacker can use the disclosed session identifier against /message to send unauthorized MCP tool calls. Depending on the configured tools, those calls can read or write local files, execute commands, or perform other actions. Binding only to loopback does not prevent this browser-mediated attack.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text: Educational only. The accompanying poc.py is a defensive checker, not an attack: run against your own MoLing instance, it simply reports whether the /sse endpoint answers without authentication and whether the response carries a wildcard cross-origin header. It does not steal a session, does not send tool calls, and does not execute anything on the target. The attack chain itself is described conceptually above: visit page, cross-origin stream, session disclosure, unauthorized tool calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update MoLing to 0.5.0 or later immediately.
  • Do not run SSE mode on a machine where you browse untrusted sites, and never expose it beyond loopback.
  • Treat any agent configured with file and command tools as fully privileged: restrict its tools, its network binding, and its origin policy.
  • Rotate any secrets that may have been exposed through a hijacked session.

docs.title: CVE-2026-63438: 2FAuth Reverse-Proxy Guard Lets Anyone Forge an Admin Identity
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL (9.8) CVSS vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Product 2FAuth Vulnerability type Improper Authentication (CWE-287)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: 2FAuth before 8.0.0, when AUTHENTICATION_GUARD=reverse-proxy-guard is enabled

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: When the reverse-proxy guard is enabled, 2FAuth reads the identity header (by default REMOTE_USER, or a custom header) without confirming that the request originated from a configured trusted proxy. A remote client that can reach the application directly can forge the selected identity header and authenticate as an existing user, including an administrator, gaining access to stored 2FA secrets and account or application management functions. On a fresh instance, an unknown identity is auto-created and the first created account is promoted to administrator, with the account email synchronized from a configured mail header. The sibling CVE-2026-63439 covers the same guard: the account auto-creation and admin promotion path.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo in poc.py models the safe pattern: the identity header is trusted only when the request comes from an allow-listed trusted proxy address; direct requests are rejected. It runs locally.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update 2FAuth to 8.0.0 immediately.
  • Block direct access to the application so only the trusted reverse proxy can reach it.
  • Allow-list trusted proxy addresses and verify the request origin before trusting any identity header.
  • Rotate every two-factor secret and review accounts for unknown or promoted users.

docs.title: CVE-2026-65119 — NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM loads untrusted tokenizer files, leading to code execution
docs.text: Educational writeup only. The proof of concept below is conceptual and demonstrates the flaw in a controlled lab. Do not use it against systems you do not own.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH 8.4 (CVSS v3.1) Product NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM (KvCacheAwareRouter tokenizer loading) Type Inclusion of functionality from an untrusted control sphere (CWE-829) Vector Local — no privileges required, no user interaction CWE CWE-829 (inclusion of functionality from untrusted control sphere) Fixed in NVIDIA October 2026 security update (bulletin 5883)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Versions covered by NVIDIA security bulletin 5883 (TensorRT-LLM, October 2026). A successful exploit can lead to code execution, information disclosure, data tampering, and denial of service.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The KvCacheAwareRouter loads tokenizer files without verifying that they come from a trusted source. Tokenizer files shape how text is split and understood, but in this loading path they are treated with the trust of code: a file from an untrusted place can carry functionality the server was never meant to run, and that functionality then runs inside the inference server with the server's own privileges. In AI serving, every model artifact is a potential doorway.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual, educational only)
docs.text:
See poc.py. It shows, against your own lab deployment only:

  1. How to test whether a tokenizer path outside a trusted allowlist is accepted for loading.
  2. The vulnerable pattern (any tokenizer path loaded, no source check) versus the fixed pattern (allowlisted, verified sources only, plus least-privilege execution).
  3. What a successful attack gains: code execution on the inference host, data and model tampering, and denial of service.

No working exploit is provided — only the allowlist check and the vulnerable-vs-fixed pattern.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Apply the NVIDIA October 2026 security update for TensorRT-LLM.
  • Load tokenizers only from trusted, verified sources.
  • Allowlist tokenizer load paths and verify artifact integrity.
  • Run inference with least privilege and sandbox model-artifact loading.
  • Audit model and tokenizer artifacts for tampering.

docs.title: CVE-2026-65145 — NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit missing authentication gives unauthenticated attackers full control
docs.text: Educational writeup only. The proof of concept below is conceptual and demonstrates the flaw in a controlled lab. Do not use it against systems you do not own.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL 10.0 (CVSS v3.1) Product NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit Type Missing authentication (CWE-306) Vector Network — unauthenticated, no user interaction, scope changed CWE CWE-306 (missing authentication for critical function) Fixed in NVIDIA October 2026 security update (bulletin 5912)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Versions covered by NVIDIA security bulletin 5912 (NeMo Agent Toolkit, October 2026). Any deployment that exposes the agent service to a network without authentication is reachable by a remote attacker; the impact includes code execution, privilege escalation, data tampering, denial of service, and information disclosure.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The agent service performs no authentication check before serving requests for critical functions. An attacker who can reach the service on the network is treated like any legitimate caller, so requests that drive agent actions, touch data, and use tools are accepted without a login, token, or other identity check. A service with the power to run code and reach data must never trust a caller it has not identified.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual, educational only)
docs.text:
See poc.py. It shows, against your own lab deployment only:

  1. How to test whether an agent endpoint answers without authentication (a harmless read-only probe of an endpoint that should require login).
  2. The vulnerable pattern (critical function served with no identity check) versus the fixed pattern (authentication required before any agent action, plus network allowlisting).
  3. What a successful attack gains: code execution, privilege escalation, data tampering, and denial of service.

No working exploit is provided — only the auth check and the vulnerable-vs-fixed pattern.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Apply the NVIDIA October 2026 security update for NeMo Agent Toolkit.
  • Require authentication on every agent endpoint, with no exceptions for internal-looking callers.
  • Never expose the agent service to untrusted networks; bind it to loopback or a private network and firewall it.
  • Run agents with least privilege and audit data, tools, and credentials the service could reach for abuse.

docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH (CVSS 3.1: 7.1) Product Nickboss WordPress File Upload (WordPress plugin) Type Cross-site Scripting (CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation) Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:L Published 2026-11-01

docs.title: OpenStack Manila: Public Shares Are Anyone's — Missing Ownership Checks
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.9 (v3.1) Product OpenStack Manila before 23.0.1 (shared filesystem service) Type Incorrect authorization (CWE-863) — ownership not re-verified on public shares Vector Any authenticated project member calls allow_access / deny_access / update_access / create_share_backup / soft_delete / restore / export-location metadata / access-rule listing on a foreign public share (UUID is public) → operation succeeds without ownership check

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: OpenStack Manila before 23.0.1. Fixed in 23.0.1.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The API controllers authorize the request against the caller's own project context, then load the target share — which may be a foreign public share — and never re-authorize against the share's actual owner. Eight operations trust the skipped check: allow_access grants data-plane access to someone else's share, create_share_backup exfiltrates data under the attacker's project, access-rule listing discloses IPs, usernames, and CephFS keys:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def allow_access(ctx, share_id, rule):
    authorize(ctx, ctx.project)          # checks YOUR project
    share = load_share(share_id)         # ...then loads ANY share
    share.add_rule(rule)                 # no ownership re-check!

# Simplified fixed pattern
def allow_access_fixed(ctx, share_id, rule):
    share = load_share(share_id)
    authorize(ctx, share.owner_project)  # check against the OBJECT's owner
    share.add_rule(rule)

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. Attacker, any project member, lists public shares and picks a victim's share UUID.
  2. They call create_share_backup on it — the backup lands under their own project, containing the victim's data.
  3. Or they call allow_access/deny_access/update_access to rewrite who can read the share, or list access rules to harvest CephFS keys and IPs.
  4. Cross-tenant confidentiality and integrity, broken by design.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: Authorize against the loaded object, after the load — never against a context you checked before fetching it. Offline, no server, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update now: OpenStack Manila to 23.0.1 or later.
  • Audit public shares for unexpected backups, access rules, and export-location metadata changes.
  • Rotate CephFS keys, credentials, and anything listed through access-rule disclosure.

docs.title: CVE-2026-73098-group — Nine Flaws in Apache Juneau through 9.2.0, Eight Rated 10.0
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL — CVSS 4.0: 10.0 (eight flaws), HIGH 8.7 (one flaw) Product Apache Juneau, through 9.2.0 Type Unsafe class loading (CWE-470), CSRF (CWE-352), Path traversal (CWE-22), XSS (CWE-79), Credential leak (CWE-522), Log info leak (CWE-532), Error info leak (CWE-209), HTTP response splitting (CWE-113), Resource exhaustion (CWE-770) Vector CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H (the 10.0 flaws) Affected versions Apache Juneau through 9.2.0 Fixed version Apache Juneau 9.2.1

docs.title: The batch
docs.text:
One disclosure, nine flaws, fixed in a single release (9.2.1). Eight of them score a perfect 10.0. They share one story: Juneau's defaults trust the network. Headline members:

  • CVE-2026-73098 (10.0) — Unsafe class loading (CWE-470). When Juneau parses a value into a property of type java.lang.Class, the default class swap loads the named class with initialization enabled, so input naming a class on the application classpath runs that class's static initializer — inside the server process.
  • CVE-2026-73099 (10.0) — CSRF (CWE-352). The REST server accepts a content query parameter that replaces the request body, enabled by default on every HTTP method including GET. A cross-site link delivers an attacker-chosen request body without a CORS preflight, defeating protections that rely on method or content type instead of an anti-CSRF token.
  • CVE-2026-121489 (10.0) — Path traversal (CWE-22). The microservice DirectoryResource does not keep request paths inside its configured root directory. When an application enables the resource's view, upload or delete settings (all off by default), a client can read, write or delete files outside the root, anywhere the server process can reach.
  • CVE-2026-96677 (10.0) — Cross-site scripting (CWE-79). HTML document serialization does not HTML-encode variable substitutions in the page chrome (header, nav, aside, footer). Applications whose chrome includes request-derived variables reflect them unencoded.
  • CVE-2026-73116 (10.0) — Credential leak (CWE-522). The Juneau RestClient followed HTTP redirects while keeping credential headers from the original request, so a server redirecting to a different host or port — or from HTTPS to HTTP — received Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization and X-API-Key headers.
  • CVE-2026-73100 (10.0) — Sensitive data in logs (CWE-532). The default REST server call logger records request headers for requests ending in a server error, without redacting them. Any client able to cause a server error gets its Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization and X-API-Key headers written in cleartext to the application log.
  • CVE-2026-73101 (10.0) — Sensitive data in error messages (CWE-209). The REST server sends the internal exception class and message to clients in a Thrown response header on every error response, and can include internal exception messages in the error body, even when stack-trace rendering is disabled.
  • CVE-2026-73117 (10.0) — HTTP response splitting (CWE-113). The REST server passed response header values and redirect targets to the servlet container unchecked. An application that sets a header or redirect target from request data lets a remote client inject header lines or redirect users to an arbitrary external site.
  • CVE-2026-73095 (8.7) — Resource exhaustion (CWE-770). The MessagePack parser, enabled by default on the REST server, sizes buffers from length values in the input. An unauthenticated client sends a few bytes that force a multi-gigabyte allocation and an OutOfMemoryError — denial of service. Related unbounded allocations in multipart uploads and request reader buffers are fixed at the same time.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Apache Juneau through 9.2.0. All nine flaws are fixed in 9.2.1.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Juneau's dangerous features ship switched on, and its parsers treat remote input as instructions. The class swap loads whatever class name the input carries, with initialization. The content parameter turns a GET link into an arbitrary-body request. The file resource joins a client-supplied path onto its root without checking the result stays inside. The call logger and error responses copy headers and exception details verbatim. Each flaw is a trust boundary the framework drew in the wrong place — and each one is remotely reachable with no login.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation with no network traffic, how a parser that loads a class by name runs that class's startup code, how a query parameter replaces a request body, and how a path escapes its root folder — and how the fixed versions (class allowlist, disabled content parameter, path containment check) block each one.

Conceptual attack chain (CVE-2026-73098):

  1. The attacker sends a normal request whose value names a class already on the server's classpath.
  2. Juneau parses the value into a Class property and loads the named class with initialization enabled.
  3. The class's static initializer runs immediately, inside the server process — no login, no upload, one request.

Conceptual attack chain (CVE-2026-73099):

  1. The attacker crafts a link to the Juneau service with a content query parameter holding an attacker-chosen body.
  2. A logged-in user clicks the link; the browser issues a GET.
  3. The server treats the parameter as the request body, executing the attacker's action with the victim's session — no preflight, no token.

Conceptual attack chain (CVE-2026-121489):

  1. The attacker requests a path containing ../ segments against an enabled DirectoryResource with view, upload or delete on.
  2. The path resolves outside the configured root directory.
  3. Files are read, written or deleted anywhere the server process can reach.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade to Apache Juneau 9.2.1 now — it fixes all nine flaws.
  • If you cannot upgrade today: set disableContentParam to true, keep the DirectoryResource view/upload/delete settings off, and disable or bound the MessagePack parser.
  • Rotate any credentials that may have reached application logs or error responses (Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization, X-API-Key).
  • If your application builds redirect targets from request data, switch from sendRedirect() to the new sendSafeRedirect(), and review any code that supplies its own HttpClient to the RestClient builder — it must disable automatic redirects or strip credential headers on cross-origin redirects itself.
  • Check server logs for odd class names, ../ path segments and unexpected content parameters.

docs.title: CVE-2026-76298 — Splunk Enterprise: Low-Privilege User Derives Sidecar DB Superuser Password
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.8 Product Splunk Enterprise below 10.4.4 and 10.2.8 (search head cluster members) Type Use of Hard-coded / Derived Credentials (CWE-321) — privileged password derived from a non-secret identifier Vector Low-privilege user (no admin/power role) → reads search job logs → extracts cluster identifier → derives PostgreSQL sidecar superuser password → runs OS commands as the Splunk service account

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• Splunk Enterprise below 10.4.4 and below 10.2.8.
  • Fixed in 10.4.4 and 10.2.8 (see Splunk advisory SVD-2026-1007).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The PostgreSQL sidecar service derives its privileged database password from the search head cluster identifier — but that identifier appears inside ordinary search job logs, which any user able to run searches can read. A secret built from public material isn't a secret:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def sidecar_password():
    cluster_id = read_cluster_id()          # also visible in job logs!
    return derive(cluster_id)               # deterministic -> recomputable

def attack():
    logs = run_search_and_read_job_logs()   # any low-priv user can do this
    cluster_id = extract_cluster_id(logs)
    password = derive(cluster_id)           # same math -> superuser password
    db_login("postgres_superuser", password)
    run_os_commands()                       # as the Splunk service account

# Simplified fixed pattern
def sidecar_password_fixed():
    return secrets.token_hex(32)            # random, stored securely,
                                           # never derived from public data

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The attack chain, conceptually:

  1. Low-privilege user (no admin/power role) runs an ordinary search.
  2. They open the search job logs and copy the cluster identifier.
  3. They apply the same derivation the sidecar uses → PostgreSQL superuser password.
  4. They authenticate to the sidecar database and escalate to arbitrary operating-system commands as the Splunk service account on cluster members.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a credential derived from a log-visible identifier (recomputable by anyone) versus a properly random stored secret — all synthetic, offline, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade now: Splunk Enterprise 10.4.4 or 10.2.8 per advisory SVD-2026-1007.
  • Rotate sidecar database credentials — anything derived the old way is burned.
  • Restrict search job log access and audit for unusual database logins or unexpected OS command execution on cluster members.

docs.title: CVE-2026-76466 — Cisco Expressway Series Remote Code Execution
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL 9.8 Product Cisco Expressway Series (Expressway-C and Expressway-E) Vulnerability type Use of Hard-coded Credentials / Missing Authentication (CWE-798) Vector Network — unauthenticated, remote attacker with network access to the device

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Cisco Expressway Series software prior to the patched October 2026 release published with Cisco advisory cisco-sa-vcs-static-cred-hr7EWZ8t (Expressway-C and Expressway-E). There are no workarounds — upgrade to a fixed release per Cisco's Fixed Releases table.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The database service feature relies on persistent cookies as proof of the caller's trust, and when TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering, client certificates are not validated at all. An attacker holding the cookies can connect to the database service and invoke specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands that execute arbitrary OS commands as root.

docs.title: Proof of concept (educational only)
docs.text:
EDUCATIONAL-ONLY: the code below is a conceptual illustration of the trust pattern, NOT a working exploit. It performs no network operations and cannot exploit any real system. Only test against systems you own in controlled environments.

See poc.py: a mock showing why a persistent, unbound cookie accepted as identity is equivalent to no authentication — and how the fixed pattern binds each session to a freshly validated credential.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade Expressway Core and Edge to the patched release Cisco published with this advisory. No workaround exists.
  • Rotate every secret, certificate, and credential stored on affected devices.
  • Restrict which networks can reach the database service; keep edge devices off the open internet.
  • Hunt logs for anonymous or unexpected RPC traffic against the database service.

docs.title: CVE-2026-76473 — Cisco Unified Communications Voice Hardening Batch (October 2026)
docs.text:
Cluster writeup. This page is framed around CVE-2026-76473, the lead identifier of Cisco's October 2026 voice-products hardening batch. The same internal review produced a family of CVEs; all are listed under References below and fixed by the same hardening releases.

Field Value Severity CRITICAL 9.8 Product Cisco Emergency Responder, Cisco Prime Collaboration Deployment, Cisco Unified Communications Manager (Unified CM), Unified CM IM & Presence Service, Unified CM Session Management Edition (SME), Cisco Unity Connection Vulnerability type Improper control of a resource through its lifetime / injection class (CWE-74); sibling identifiers cover improper authentication (CWE-287), cross-site scripting (CWE-79), and further hardening classes Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Versions 14.x through 15.x of the affected voice products, including Unified CM 14 through 14SU6 and 15 through 15SU4 / 15SU4a branches, IM & Presence 14 through 14SU6 and 15 through 15SU4, Unity Connection 14 through 14SU6 and 15 through 15SU4, Emergency Responder 14 through 14SU6 and 15 through 15SU4, and Prime Collaboration Deployment. See the Cisco advisory for the per-product, per-branch fixed releases.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: During a comprehensive internal security review, Cisco engineering found that several voice-product web interfaces and management APIs mishandled attacker-influenced input (the CWE-74 class grouped under CVE-2026-76473) and that authentication checks on session handling could be bypassed (the CWE-287 class grouped under CVE-2026-76474), alongside a stored scripting flaw in the web UI (CWE-79, CVE-2026-76475) and additional hardening issues. The common theme: trust boundaries between the network and privileged voice functions were not enforced consistently, so crafted requests could reach sensitive operations without proving identity.

docs.title: Proof of concept (educational only)
docs.text: poc.py contains a safe, self-contained simulation — it spins up a local mock web portal that mimics the pattern of the flaw (accepting a session token at face value) and a checker function that demonstrates, against the mock only, how a forged token would be accepted. It never touches a real Cisco system, never sends a real request to any network host, and cannot be repurposed into a working exploit. Run it with python3 poc.py to see the vulnerable pattern vs. the fixed pattern side by side.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade all six voice products to the October 2026 security hardening releases published with the Cisco advisory (match the fixed release to your 14.x / 15.x train).
  • There are no workarounds — upgrading is the only remediation.
  • Until patched, restrict the voice web consoles and management APIs to trusted admin networks only.
  • After upgrading, audit admin sessions for unexpected logins and rotate administrative credentials.

docs.text: The companion short video walks through this vulnerability cluster in six acts — the scenario, the flaw, the attack chain, the result, why it works, and the fix — with animated infographics. (YouTube Shorts link to be added after publication.)

docs.title: CVE-2026-76505 — Cisco IOS XR ASR 9000 Series IPv4 Unicast Packets DoS
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH 7.5 Product Cisco ASR 9000/9900 Series Aggregation Services Routers and ASR 9902/9903 Compact High-Performance Routers (Lightspeed/Lightspeed-Plus line cards), IOS XR 64-bit with IPv4 enabled Vulnerability type Improper Input Validation (CWE-20) in IPv4 packet processing Vector Network — unauthenticated, remote attacker sends crafted IPv4 packets

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Cisco IOS XR 64-bit releases listed in Cisco advisory cisco-sa-asr9k-tUyxcyXN running on affected ASR 9000/9900 (Lightspeed or Lightspeed-Plus line cards) and ASR 9902/9903 routers with IPv4 configured on any line card interface. Upgrade per Cisco's Fixed Software table. IPv6-only configurations are not affected.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Crafted IPv4 packets that are received on an affected line card interface and processed as for-us traffic are mishandled in the IPv4 packet-processing path, causing network processor (NP) errors. One error resets the line card; repeated errors can push the NP into a persistent shutdown state requiring an explicit line card reload. Transit IPv4 traffic does not trigger the issue and IPv6 traffic cannot trigger it.

docs.title: Proof of concept (educational only)
docs.text:
EDUCATIONAL-ONLY: the code below is a conceptual illustration of the input-validation pattern, NOT a working exploit. It parses a locally constructed byte string and performs no network operations. Only test against systems you own in controlled environments.

See poc.py: a toy IPv4 header parser showing the vulnerable pattern (trusting a length field from the packet without bounds checking) vs. the fixed pattern (validate every field before use).

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade to a fixed Cisco IOS XR 64-bit release per the advisory's Fixed Software section.
  • Apply control-plane policing (CoPP) to rate-limit for-us traffic destined to the router.
  • Monitor line cards for unexpected NP errors or resets.

docs.title: CVE-2026-76506 — Cisco UCS Central: Authenticated Remote Code Execution via Path Traversal
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH — CVSS 3.1: 7.6 Product Cisco UCS Central Software Type Path Traversal (CWE-22) leading to Remote Code Execution Affected versions Cisco UCS Central Software 2.1 before 2.1(2c); 2.0 and earlier Fixed version 2.1(2c) (2.0 and earlier: migrate to a fixed release)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Cisco UCS Central Software, regardless of device configuration. Fixed releases: 2.1(2c) for the 2.1 line; releases 2.0 and earlier must migrate to a fixed release. Cisco states there are no workarounds.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Insufficient validation of user-supplied input in an HTTP request to the web-based management interface. An authenticated, remote attacker sends a crafted HTTP request to an affected endpoint; the unvalidated input enables path traversal, arbitrary command execution, arbitrary file writes to the filesystem, and information disclosure on the affected device. Exploitation requires valid user credentials on the device.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation, how an unvalidated path input escapes its intended directory, and how the fixed version (resolve the path, then verify it stays inside the allowed base directory) breaks that chain.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. Attacker obtains valid credentials for the UCS Central web interface.
  2. Attacker sends a crafted HTTP request with a traversal sequence to a vulnerable endpoint.
  3. The unvalidated input escapes the intended location.
  4. The attacker writes arbitrary files and executes arbitrary commands on the management device, and reads sensitive information.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade Cisco UCS Central to 2.1(2c) (or migrate from 2.0 and earlier to a fixed release) immediately — there is no workaround.
  • Restrict access to the management interface to trusted networks only.
  • Audit accounts with access to the management interface and remove any that are unrecognized.
  • Monitor the management device for unexpected files and command execution.

docs.title: CVE-2026-76740 — HPE RMC: OS Command Injection on the Management Controller
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.2 Product HPE Compute Scale-up Server 3200/3250, HPE Superdome Flex, Superdome Flex 280 (RMC — remote management controller) Type OS Command Injection (CWE-78): management-console input interpolated unsanitized into shell commands Vector Network, low complexity, high privileges → an authenticated privileged user executes arbitrary commands on the RMC

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: • Firmware versions listed in HPE security bulletin hpesbhf05153 (update to the fixed firmware).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The RMC's management console takes operator input and interpolates it directly into shell commands with no neutralization. A single shell metacharacter (;, |, $(), backticks) breaks out of the intended command and executes arbitrary commands with the controller's privileges — the same controller that powers, resets, and firmware-flashes the entire rack.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def run_diagnostic(target):
    os.system(f"ping -c1 {target}")   # target = "x; id" -> breakout

# Simplified fixed pattern
def run_diagnostic(target):
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9.-]+", target):
        raise ValueError("rejected input")
    subprocess.run(["ping", "-c1", target], shell=False)

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. The attacker holds a privileged RMC account (PR:H — e.g. a compromised admin credential).
  2. In a management-console field they submit a value containing a shell metacharacter.
  3. The RMC builds a shell command from the raw input and executes it.
  4. Arbitrary commands run on the controller: read or rewrite firmware, power-cycle hosts, pivot into the management network.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: string-interpolated shell invocation versus allowlist validation with shell=False. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Apply the HPE firmware update from bulletin hpesbhf05153.
  • Isolate the management network: RMC/BMC interfaces on a dedicated VLAN, never internet-exposed.
  • Harden privileged accounts: strong unique credentials, MFA where supported, least privilege, rotate after any suspected compromise.
  • Monitor RMC audit logs for unusual command patterns.

docs.title: CVE-2026-77596-group: Kubeflow Pipelines Multi-User Authorization Bypasses
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL (9.6) / HIGH (7.2) CVSS vector CVE-2026-77596: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N CVSS vector CVE-2026-88984: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N Product Kubeflow Pipelines Vulnerability type Authorization Bypass (CWE-639, CWE-285)

docs.title: Covered CVEs
docs.text:
• CVE-2026-77596 (CRITICAL 9.6, CWE-639): pipeline upload authorization bypass via empty namespace.
  • CVE-2026-88984 (HIGH 7.2, CWE-285): shared/global pipeline modification and deletion without RBAC permission.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• CVE-2026-77596: Kubeflow Pipelines before 2.18.0 (fixed in 2.18.0)
  • CVE-2026-88984: Kubeflow Pipelines before 2.16.1 (fixed in 2.16.1)

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The multi-user API server's pipeline upload endpoints return without a SubjectAccessReview when the target namespace is empty while REQUIRE_NAMESPACE_FOR_PIPELINES defaults to false, so a low-privilege tenant can create shared pipelines or inject attacker-controlled versions into existing shared pipelines without the required write permission. If the API server is directly reachable without an authenticating proxy, an unauthenticated caller can exploit the same bypass. Separately, the API server treats the empty namespace used by shared or global pipelines as an authorization exception for modification and deletion operations, so an authenticated user can modify or delete shared pipeline definitions and versions without the required Kubernetes RBAC permissions. An enabled unpinned recurring run that follows the latest version then executes the injected specification in another tenant's namespace under that workload's service account.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo in poc.py models the safe pattern: an upload gate that requires a non-empty namespace AND a passing authorization check for every upload, modify, and delete operation, with no exception for shared or empty namespaces. It never contacts a real server.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade Kubeflow Pipelines to 2.18.0 (which includes the 2.16.1 shared-pipeline fix) immediately.
  • Put the API server behind an authenticating proxy; do not expose it directly.
  • Pin recurring runs to specific pipeline versions instead of following "latest".
  • Audit shared pipelines and their versions for unexpected changes.

docs.title: CVE-2026-77690 — Command Injection in ManageEngine Key Manager Plus
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH — CVSS 3.1: 8.8 Product ZohoCorp ManageEngine Key Manager Plus Type Command Injection (CWE-78) Vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Affected versions ManageEngine Key Manager Plus versions before 7151 Fixed version Build 7151

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: ManageEngine Key Manager Plus versions before build 7151. The attacker needs to be authenticated with certificate deployment privileges. A second flaw fixed in the same release lets low-privilege users export keys outside their scope.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: When configuring a deployment target, specially crafted input was not neutralized before it reached the system shell. The vault trusted deployment settings as data, but the shell read part of them as instructions — so a deployment configuration became a command execution primitive on the vault server itself, the machine that holds the company's SSH keys and certificates.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation, how deployment input that reaches a shell unescaped becomes command execution, and how the fixed version (no shell involved, or strict allowlisting of the target value) blocks it.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. Attacker holds a low-privilege account with certificate deployment rights on Key Manager Plus.
  2. The attacker configures a deployment target with crafted input.
  3. The crafted value reaches the system shell unescaped.
  4. The shell runs the attacker's commands on the vault server.
  5. Result: arbitrary command execution on the server that stores the company's keys and certificates.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Key Manager Plus to build 7151 or newer.
  • Restrict certificate deployment privileges to the smallest set of users who need them.
  • Audit existing deployment targets and export logs for unusual entries.
  • Rotate any keys or certificates that may have been exposed.

docs.text:

docs.title: CVE-2026-77876 — OS Command Injection in Control Web Panel (CWP)
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL — CVSS 9.8 Product Control Web Panel (CWP), versions before webpanel_version 1.16 Type OS Command Injection (CWE-78) Vector Network, low complexity, no user interaction (user panel context)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• Control Web Panel versions before webpanel_version 1.16.
  • Fixed in webpanel_version 1.16 and later.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The protected_directory module of the CWP user panel handles the acc=deletedp action by passing the user-supplied file POST parameter directly into a shell_exec call without escaping. Shell metacharacters in the value are therefore interpreted as commands, giving the attacker code execution in the user panel context on the hosting server.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text: See poc.py: a local simulation contrasting a handler that concatenates raw input into a shell command string with one that validates against an allowlist and never invokes a shell. It runs no shell commands and targets no real server.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Control Web Panel to 1.16 or later immediately.
  • Restrict access to the panel to trusted IPs where possible.
  • Audit panel logs for unusual deletedp requests.
  • Keep the hosting server fully patched.

docs.title: CVE-2026-78164 — Apache Camel: HTTP Header Template Injection Leaks Secrets
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.2 Product Apache Camel HTTP / Netty HTTP / Undertow / Vert.x HTTP producers Type Template Injection + Information Exposure (CWE-200) Vector Inbound message headers override the endpoint URI and are template-resolved

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The HTTP producer families let an inbound message override the endpoint URI via CamelHttpUri / CamelRestHttpUri headers, then passed that message-supplied string through property-placeholder resolution before use. Placeholder resolution is a template engine — attacker-controlled templates plus secret-valued properties equals information disclosure.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. Attacker sets CamelHttpUri on an inbound message.
  2. The producer resolves placeholders in the attacker string.
  3. Secret properties (passwords, tokens) expand into the URI.
  4. Secrets leak to attacker-influenced destinations / logs.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a vulnerable mock versus the fixed pattern. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Upgrade to Camel 4.18.5 or 4.22.1. Do not let message headers override endpoint URIs. Keep secrets out of placeholder-resolvable scopes.

docs.title: CVE-2026-78165 — Apache Camel: Spring Redis Deserializes Untrusted Bytes
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.8 Product Apache Camel camel-spring-redis Type Deserialization of Untrusted Data (CWE-502) Vector Attacker-controlled Redis payload bytes become live Java objects

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: RedisConfiguration.getSerializer lazily built a bare JdkSerializationRedisSerializer when no serializer was configured, and used it for every read. Spring's deserializer installs no ObjectInputFilter, so hostile bytes from Redis become hostile objects in the JVM — the classic deserialization RCE shape.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. Attacker gets malicious serialized bytes into Redis (or a MITM).
  2. The Camel Redis consumer reads them with the default deserializer.
  3. No allowlist filter: arbitrary classes instantiate.
  4. Remote code execution in the Camel process.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a vulnerable mock versus the fixed pattern. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Upgrade to Camel 4.18.5 or 4.22.1. Configure an explicit, safe serializer; never rely on JDK serialization defaults. Treat Redis as untrusted input: authenticate and isolate it.

docs.title: CVE-2026-79977 — Zephyr WireGuard: Unauthenticated Packet Overwrites VPN Peer Endpoint
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.2 (v3.1) Product Zephyr RTOS — WireGuard service (subsys/net/lib/wireguard/wg.c) Type Missing authentication for critical function (CWE-306) / origin validation error (CWE-346) Vector Attacker forges a UDP transport-data packet with a receiver index matching no session → handle_transport_data() cannot authenticate it (no key exists) → the handler schedules a new handshake AND memcpy()s the packet's source address into peer->endpoint → the device's VPN peer address now points at an attacker-chosen address → encrypted replies rerouted, link hijacked or broken

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Zephyr RTOS builds including the WireGuard service prior to the fix. Patched via commit cbaaf3e9 (advisory GHSA-w8h4-r8m3-rf5j).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The handler updated long-lived peer state from a message it knew it could not verify. Because the receiver index matched no session, no key existed to authenticate the packet - yet its source address was copied into the trusted endpoint table anyway. An unauthenticated datagram's source address is fully attacker-controlled. Mutable peer state must only move on verified input; the fix stops writing the endpoint before authentication succeeds.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The vulnerable pattern, simplified:

// VULNERABLE - endpoint rewritten from an unverifiable packet
void handle_transport_data(pkt) {
    peer = find_peer(pkt.receiver_index);   // NULL: no session, no key
    schedule_handshake(peer);
    memcpy(&peer->endpoint, pkt.src, sizeof(endpoint));  // <-- attacker address
}

// FIXED - never mutate peer state on unauthenticated input
void handle_transport_data(pkt) {
    peer = find_peer(pkt.receiver_index);
    if (!peer || !authenticate(pkt, peer->key))
        return;                             // drop, schedule nothing
    schedule_handshake(peer);               // endpoint only from verified pkts
}

The demo poc.py below models the endpoint-table write decision on synthetic records - no packets, no crypto, no device.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Apply the Zephyr WireGuard fix (commit cbaaf3e9) to all firmware builds. Firewall VPN ports so only known peers can reach the device, monitor for handshake anomalies, and keep fleet firmware on current releases.

docs.title: CVE-2026-79982 — Zephyr Bluetooth USB: Heap Overflow via Oversized HCI Packet (No Length Check)
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.8 (v3.1) Product Zephyr RTOS — new USB device stack (subsys/usb/device_next/class/bt_hci.c) Type Heap-based buffer overflow (CWE-787) — missing length check before copy Vector Attacker delivers a Bluetooth HCI event/ACL packet larger than the fixed USB pool slot (USBD_MAX_BULK_MPS, 64 bytes on full-speed-only builds) → bt_hci_tx_sync_in() allocates the tiny slot → net_buf_add_mem() copies the full packet with no length check → the copy overruns into adjacent pool memory → stack corruption, crash, or potential code execution on the embedded target

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Zephyr RTOS new USB device stack prior to the fix. Patched via commit 0419defd (advisory GHSA-w5px-w97v-c3hj).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The code assumed the incoming packet would fit the buffer. Pool slots were sized for the smallest USB transfer while Bluetooth packets are sized for the radio protocol, and nothing reconciled the two before the copy. Whenever the writer assumes and the reader never checks, overflow wins - the classic unchecked-copy bug, made worse by the memory-constrained embedded target where adjacent pool data may include control structures.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The vulnerable pattern, simplified:

// VULNERABLE - copy with no length check
buf = pool_alloc(64);                       // fixed tiny slot
net_buf_add_mem(buf, pkt->data, pkt->len);  // <-- pkt->len can be 200+

// FIXED - validate before copying
buf = pool_alloc(64);
if (pkt->len > buf_capacity(buf))
    return -EINVAL;                         // refuse oversized packet
net_buf_add_mem(buf, pkt->data, pkt->len);

The demo poc.py below models the copy decision on synthetic byte buffers - no USB, no Bluetooth, no device.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Apply the Zephyr USB transport fix (commit 0419defd). Audit every buffer copy in the USB stack for a length check, size pools to the largest packet the protocol allows, and fuzz USB transports with oversized inputs before shipping firmware.
