docs.title: CVE-2026-79983 — Apache Camel: FTP Consumer Path Traversal
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.4 Product Apache Camel camel-ftp Type Path Traversal (CWE-22) Vector Malicious server's file listing steers the consumer outside its directory

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The FTP remote-file consumer polls a directory on a remote server and builds each file's absolute remote path by concatenating the configured directory with the file name reported by the server. A rogue or compromised server returns ../-laden names, and the consumer happily walks outside its sandbox — reading or writing wherever the traversal points.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. Camel polls the FTP server's directory.
  2. The server's listing returns a filename like ../../secret.
  3. The consumer concatenates it unsanitized.
  4. Files outside the intended directory are read or overwritten.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a vulnerable mock versus the fixed pattern. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Upgrade to Camel 4.18.5 or 4.22.1. Only poll trusted servers; normalize every server-supplied filename. Run consumers with least-privilege filesystem access.

docs.text:

docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.2 Product Apache Camel camel-oauth Type Improper Authentication / Fail-Open (CWE-287) Vector Unauthenticated requests pass the OAuth guard when auth cannot complete

  2. The OAuth processor fails to establish a session.

  4. Protected endpoint serves the unauthenticated attacker.

docs.title: Mitigation

docs.title: CVE-2026-8168 — Uncontrolled recursion in Qt SVG parser/renderer (DoS)
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH (CVSS 4.0: 7.1) Product Qt SVG module (QtSvg) Type CWE-674 — Uncontrolled Recursion (stack exhaustion / stack overflow) Attack vector Network (attacker supplies a crafted SVG file; victim opens/renders it — UI:P)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• Qt 4.1.0 through Qt 6.8.8
  • Qt 6.9.0 through Qt 6.11.1
  • Status unknown before 4.1.0

Fixed in Qt 6.8.9, 6.11.2, and 6.12.0 or later, which render iteratively. Patch sets are also published by Qt for the dev, 6.11, and 6.8 branches (see References).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: When a Qt application loads an SVG file containing excessively deep element nesting, the Qt SVG module traverses the document tree recursively — while resolving paint servers, detecting cycles (detectCycles), rendering, and destroying the internal tree — without enforcing any recursion depth limit. Every nesting level consumes one C++ call frame, so a crafted document with thousands of nested elements exhausts the process call stack and the application segfaults. The fix replaces the recursive traversals with iterative loops and bounded depth handling.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
EDUCATIONAL ONLY — conceptual description, not a working exploit.

Attack chain:

  1. Attacker generates a tiny, valid SVG containing thousands of nested <g> elements (groups inside groups). Generation takes milliseconds; the file can be under 1 KB.
  2. The SVG reaches the victim through any channel: download, email attachment, icon asset, chat avatar.
  3. The Qt application parses and renders it. render(), paint-server resolution, and cleanup each recurse once per nesting level.
  4. Each level burns one stack frame. The finite call stack overflows → the process crashes (denial of service).

Vulnerable vs. fixed pattern (illustrative):

# VULNERABLE: unbounded recursion — nesting depth controls stack depth
def render(node):
    draw(node)
    for child in node.children:
        render(child)            # one stack frame per level

# FIXED: iterative traversal with a hard depth cap
def render(node, max_depth=100):
    stack = [(node, 0)]
    while stack:
        current, depth = stack.pop()
        if depth > max_depth:
            raise ValueError("SVG nesting too deep")
        draw(current)
        stack.extend((c, depth + 1) for c in current.children)

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Qt to 6.8.9, 6.11.2, or 6.12.0 or later (or apply the official qtsvg patch set for your branch).
  • Validate / sanitize SVG input: reject documents whose nesting depth exceeds a sane bound before parsing.
  • Enforce recursion depth limits anywhere your own code walks attacker-influenced document trees.
  • Restrict which SVG files users can load and prefer trusted sources for icons/assets.

docs.title: CVE-2026-82033 — DeepSeek Harness Missing Authentication Leads to Agent Command Execution
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH — CVSS 4.0: 8.6 Product DeepSeek Harness Type Missing authentication for critical function (CWE-306) Vector CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N Affected versions Before 0.1.2-alpha.2 Fixed version 0.1.2-alpha.2

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: DeepSeek Harness prior to 0.1.2-alpha.2, including the build at commit 3e24087.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The harness's web profile HTTP and WebSocket RPC control plane exposes session methods with no authentication at all. Any local process — including one running as a different operating-system user — can call unauthenticated session methods such as session.create and session.prompt. A prompt sent this way makes the victim's agent run its bash and filesystem tools, so commands execute as the victim user with the victim's configured model credentials. Live session traffic and logs are also exposed over the event stream, and the human tool-approval check can be bypassed by matching the approval identifiers broadcast over that same ungated stream.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational only — this demonstrates the pattern, not a working exploit. Do not test against systems you do not own.

See poc.py: it shows, in a safe local simulation, how a caller with no credentials can open a session and issue a prompt on an unauthenticated control plane, and how the fixed version (require an owner token for every session method, keep approval identifiers private) breaks the chain.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. The victim runs the harness; its control plane listens locally with no authentication.
  2. A rogue local process calls the session methods directly.
  3. It sends a prompt that makes the agent run shell commands and read files as the victim.
  4. It watches live session traffic over the open event stream and reuses broadcast approval identifiers to bypass human approval.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update DeepSeek Harness to 0.1.2-alpha.2 or later now.
  • Never run an unpatched harness on a shared or multi-user machine.
  • Review agent session logs for sessions you did not start, and rotate model credentials if anything looks off.

docs.title: CVE-2026-82814 — Duplicator: Unauthenticated Payload Planted in Site Content Detonates During Migration
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.8 (v3.1) Product Duplicator / Duplicator Pro — the WordPress backup and migration plugin Type Deserialization of untrusted data (CWE-502) — DUPX_UpdateEngine::unserializeTest() deserializes untrusted database content during migration; bundled gadget chains turn it into OS command execution (free) or config deletion leading to takeover (pro) Vector Unauthenticated attacker stores a serialized object in public site content → later, an administrator builds a package and runs a migration → the search-and-replace deserializes the planted object → gadget chain fires → OS command execution

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Duplicator (free) up to and including 1.5.17; Duplicator Pro up to and including 4.6.10.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The migration engine deserialized database content to perform search-and-replace, trusting bytes that any unauthenticated visitor could have planted earlier in public content. Because the plugin itself shipped usable gadget classes (a Requests POP chain in free, an IndexList destructor gadget in pro), the deserialization became a delayed remote control — the attacker only had to wait for an admin to migrate.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo contrasts migrate_vulnerable() (blind unserialize) with migrate_fixed() (schema-validated, gadget-free deserialization path).

The poc.py file next to this writeup demonstrates the vulnerable pattern versus the fixed pattern as a safe, offline logic demo — no network, no shell, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade now: Duplicator past 1.5.17, Duplicator Pro past 4.6.10.
  • Review recent migrations and scan the database for unknown serialized objects.
  • Restrict the installer directory's write permissions so gadget side effects cannot land.
  • Never unserialize data that untrusted users could have influenced.

docs.title: CVE-2026-83531 — Apache Camel: Dynamic Router Compiles Attacker Expressions
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.8 Product Apache Camel camel-dynamic-router Type Code / Expression Language Injection (CWE-94) Vector Remote participant sends a control message whose predicate is compiled as code

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The dynamic-router-control endpoint (introduced in 4.4.0) took the subscription predicate and the language name from inbound control messages and compiled them via DynamicRouterControlProducer. Attacker text went straight into an expression compiler running inside the application's JVM — data crossed the line into code.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. Attacker sends a control message naming a scripting language.
  2. The predicate carries a malicious expression.
  3. The router compiles and evaluates it with app permissions.
  4. Remote code execution on the integration server.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a vulnerable mock versus the fixed pattern. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Upgrade to Camel 4.18.5 or 4.22.1. Audit routes using the dynamic-router control endpoint for probing. Never compile or evaluate message-supplied expressions; allowlist languages.

docs.title: Azure Kubernetes Configuration Service: Missing Auth on a Critical Function
docs.text: Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test. | | | |---|---| | CVE | CVE-2026-83938 | | Severity | Critical — CVSS 10.0 (v3.1) | | Product | Azure Kubernetes Configuration Service | | Type | Missing authentication for critical function (CWE-306) | | Attack vector | Unauthenticated remote attacker calls a critical function that never verifies identity → privilege escalation over the network |

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Azure Kubernetes Configuration Service. Fixed by Microsoft service-side — authentication is now enforced; no customer patch to install.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
A critical configuration function accepted calls from the network without verifying who was calling. The service assumed only trusted callers could reach it — but anything on the network can. Reachability is not authorization:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def apply_cluster_config(request):
    return push_config(request.body)   # BUG: no identity check

# Simplified fixed pattern
def apply_cluster_config_fixed(request):
    identity = authenticate(request)   # verify at the boundary
    if not identity or not identity.can("cluster:admin"):
        return deny(request)
    return push_config(request.body)
Every critical function must verify identity at the boundary, no matter how internal the service feels.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
1. Attacker discovers the configuration service's network endpoint.
  2. Attacker crafts a request to the critical configuration function.
  3. The function performs no authentication check before acting.
  4. The request is honored as if it came from a trusted operator.
  5. Cluster configuration is changed — privilege escalation.

See poc.py — a safe, fully synthetic demo of the vulnerable vs. fixed pattern. network reachability is not authorization: the demo contrasts an unchecked critical function with one that authenticates at the boundary.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Nothing to install: Microsoft now enforces authentication service-side.
  • Review cluster configurations for changes made during the exposure window.
  • Rotate credentials that could have been touched.
  • Enable audit logging on configuration operations.

docs.title: CVE-2026-84243 — glibc gettext LANGUAGE traversal loads untrusted message catalogs
docs.text: Field Detail Severity HIGH 7.0 Product GNU C Library (glibc) version 2.0 and later Type CWE-22 (Path Traversal) Vector Local / environment

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: • glibc 2.0 and later (any program using the gettext family with a non-C locale)

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The gettext family reads the LANGUAGE environment variable directly and appends each colon-separated entry to the message catalog directory, without rejecting '/' or '..' entries. Unlike the earlier fix for CVE-2014-0475 (which covered locale names from setlocale/LANG/LC_*), LANGUAGE was never sanitized, so an attacker who can set the environment of a target program can point catalog loading at an arbitrary location. A crafted .mo file can then crash the program or, through mismatched format directives, cause undefined behaviour in the printf family.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Conceptually: a program looks up translations under a trusted catalog directory. With LANGUAGE set to a traversal value, the lookup escapes that directory and loads an attacker-placed catalog instead of a trusted one.

See poc.py in this folder for a safe, educational demonstration. It does not exploit the vulnerability.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Apply the glibc fix that rejects '/' and '..' entries in LANGUAGE.
  • Do not pass untrusted environment variables across trust boundaries (audit SSH AcceptEnv directives, especially LANGUAGE and LANG).
  • Restrict accounts that are limited to forced commands, and treat any such account as exposed if clients could set LANGUAGE.

docs.title: Pie Register Premium: An Upload Check Nobody Reads Lets Anyone Drop a Shell (RCE)
docs.text:
Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

Field Value CVE CVE-2026-84999 Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 Product Pie Register Premium for WordPress Type Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type (CWE-434) Vector An unauthenticated attacker submits a dangerous file (for example a PHP script) through the plugin's public registration-form upload. The upload handler runs file-type validation but never checks whether that validation reported an error before moving the file into place, and the AJAX handler has no nonce or capability check. The server returns the generated destination filename, giving the attacker the exact path needed to trigger the uploaded file.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Pie Register Premium in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.4.0. Update to the latest patched release past 3.8.4.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Two missing gates compound each other. First, the handler calls the file-type validation helpers but discards their result: an error from validation never stops the upload, so move_uploaded_file() runs regardless. Second, the AJAX endpoint performs no nonce check and no capability check, so the whole flow is reachable without an account. A validation that never blocks anything is not a control.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern (conceptual, not a working exploit)
def handle_upload(uploaded_file):
    result = check_file_type(uploaded_file)  # error is never inspected
    save_file(uploaded_file)                # runs even when the check failed
    return saved_filename(uploaded_file)    # exact path handed back

# Simplified fixed pattern
def handle_upload(uploaded_file):
    result = check_file_type(uploaded_file)
    if result.has_error():
        raise ValueError("Rejected file type")
    if not user_is_authenticated_and_authorized():
        raise PermissionError("Login and capability required")
    save_file(uploaded_file)

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational demonstration only, against a local test site you own:

  1. Set up a local WordPress install with a vulnerable Pie Register Premium version and a registration form with file upload enabled.
  2. Submit the form as an anonymous visitor with a harmless text file renamed to a script extension, and observe that the response returns a saved filename instead of a rejection.
  3. Confirm the fix on a patched install: the same submission is rejected, and no file is saved.
  4. On any real site you manage, search the uploads directory for unexpected script files and treat any hit as a compromise indicator.

No working exploit is published here.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Pie Register Premium to the latest patched release past 3.8.4.0.
  • If you cannot update yet, turn off file uploads in the plugin or remove the plugin.
  • Block script execution inside the uploads directory at the web-server level.
  • Scan the uploads directory for unexpected script files and investigate any hit as a possible compromise.
  • Require authentication and a valid nonce on every upload endpoint.

docs.title: CVE-2026-85250 — Apache Camel: XPath Component XXE Bypass
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.5 Product Apache Camel camel-xpath Type XML External Entity (CWE-611) Vector Attacker XML payload with a DOCTYPE declares external entities

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: With documentType set to InputSource, XPathBuilder handed the payload straight to javax.xml.xpath, which builds its own DocumentBuilder with JDK defaults — bypassing the hardening Camel applies to its default document type. A refused DOCTYPE on the default path was accepted here, and external entities were resolved.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. Attacker sends XML with a DOCTYPE declaring an external entity.
  2. The XPath component parses it with entity resolution on.
  3. Local files (file:///etc/passwd) expand into the document.
  4. File contents exfiltrated via the evaluated result / errors.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a vulnerable mock versus the fixed pattern. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Upgrade to Camel 4.18.5 or 4.22.1. Disable DOCTYPE declarations and external entities on every XML parser. Prefer the hardened default document type.

docs.text:

docs.title: CVE-2026-85251 — Apache Camel: Credentials Leak to Redirect Targets
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.5 Product Apache Camel camel-http Type Information Exposure (CWE-200) Vector Authorization credentials are re-sent to attacker-chosen redirect hosts

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: With followRedirects=true, two paths handed credentials to the redirect target — a host chosen by the remote server, not by the route. OAuth2ClientConfigurer registered its interceptor first in the chain, below the redirect executor, so the interceptor re-ran for every redirect and re-attached credentials to wherever the server pointed.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. Route calls a remote HTTP endpoint with credentials, following redirects.
  2. The server answers 302 to an attacker-controlled host.
  3. The credential interceptor re-attaches the Authorization header.
  4. Tokens/credentials land on the attacker's server.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a vulnerable mock versus the fixed pattern. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Upgrade to Camel 4.18.5 or 4.22.1. Strip Authorization on cross-host redirects; avoid following redirects blindly. Rotate credentials that traversed redirect-following routes.

docs.text:

docs.title: CVE-2026-85267 — Google Cloud Shell: Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking Steals Your Session
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.7 Product Google Cloud Shell prior to 2026-07-22 — the free in-browser Linux terminal tied to your Google account Type Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CWE-1385 / missing Origin validation) Vector Unauthenticated attacker page → cross-origin WebSocket handshake rides the victim's session cookies → live hijack + OAuth access token exfiltration

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• Google Cloud Shell prior to 2026-07-22.
  • Patched by Google on 2026-07-22; no customer action was needed.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The Cloud Shell WebSocket endpoint trusted the session cookie but never validated the Origin header during the handshake. Unlike normal HTTP pages, a completed WebSocket connection is not fenced by the same-origin policy, and browsers attach cookies automatically — so a handshake arriving from https://evil.com looked identical to one from Google's own page:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def websocket_handshake(request):
    if valid_session_cookie(request.cookies):   # cookies sent cross-site!
        return accept_websocket()               # Origin never inspected
    return reject()

# Simplified fixed pattern
def websocket_handshake_fixed(request):
    if request.headers.get("Origin") not in ALLOWLIST:
        return reject(403)                      # hostile pages turned away
    if not valid_csrf_token(request):
        return reject(403)
    return accept_websocket()

CSRF gives one blind request; CSWSH gives a full two-way conversation — commands in, data out.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The victim is logged into Cloud Shell (session cookie set).
  2. The victim opens a tab on the attacker's page — any page, no clicks needed beyond the visit.
  3. The page's JavaScript opens a WebSocket to Cloud Shell; the browser attaches the victim's cookies to the handshake.
  4. The server skips Origin validation and accepts — the attacker now has a live, authenticated channel and exfiltrates the OAuth access token.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a handshake model that accepts any Origin versus one with an explicit Origin allowlist plus a handshake token — all synthetic, offline, no network, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Nothing for users: Google fixed this server-side on 2026-07-22.
  • For developers shipping WebSocket endpoints: validate the Origin header against an explicit allowlist on every handshake, require a CSRF token in the handshake, and set SameSite on session cookies.

docs.title: CVE-2026-85295: Chartbrew Forged Sessions via Known Signing Secret
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL (9.8) CVSS vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Product Chartbrew Vulnerability type Use of Default Credentials (CWE-1394)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Chartbrew before 5.2.3

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Four authentication helpers accepted session tokens signed with the shared signing secret, including known, weak, or shipped-default values. The vulnerable surface is the session token fallback across the API and socket layer. A stock source or repository Docker Compose deployment retains a known, weak, or default signing secret, and an attacker submits a forged token decoding to a target user id. Knowing the symmetric secret lets the attacker create a token that the legacy verification fallback accepts as the target user without that user's password or second factor. A forged session impersonates the chosen user across the entire API and socket layer.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo in poc.py models the safe pattern: the app refuses to start with a known or default signing secret, and tokens are verified only against a strong, deployment-specific secret. It runs locally.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Chartbrew to 5.2.3 immediately.
  • Set a long, random, deployment-specific signing secret; never ship or reuse a default.
  • Rotate every active session after changing the secret.
  • Audit admin activity for logins you do not recognize.

docs.title: CVE-2026-86044: JupyterLab Desktop Link Lets an Attacker Site Steal the Server Token
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL (9.6) CVSS vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H Product JupyterLab Desktop Vulnerability type URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (CWE-601)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: JupyterLab Desktop before 4.6.2-1 (in a local managed session using JupyterLab before 4.4.8)

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: JupyterLab Desktop exposed the local server details to the renderer without confirming that the current page still had the local Jupyter server origin. In a local managed session using JupyterLab before 4.4.8, an attacker can place a crafted MathJax link in an untrusted notebook. If a victim opens the notebook and clicks the link, the existing renderer navigates to an attacker-controlled site while retaining access to the preload bridge. The site can call the server-info bridge to obtain the local server URL and authentication token, then use the Jupyter REST API to create and trust a notebook that executes arbitrary code as the victim. Users whose environment already uses JupyterLab 4.4.8 or later are unaffected because the corrected link handling breaks the first step of the chain.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo in poc.py models the safe pattern: the bridge returns server details only when the requesting page origin matches the local server origin. It runs locally.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update JupyterLab Desktop to 4.6.2-1 and JupyterLab to 4.4.8 or later.
  • Treat notebooks from untrusted sources as untrusted; do not click links inside them.
  • Review recent sessions for notebooks you did not create.

docs.title: CVE-2026-86055 — Part-DB: Password Reset Poisoning via Spoofed Host Header
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.7 (v4.0) Product Part-DB (open-source electronic-components inventory system) — password-reset link builder Type Weak password recovery / host header poisoning (CWE-640) Vector Unauthenticated attacker submits a forgot-password request for a KNOWN account (even the seeded admin) with a SPOOFED Host header → Part-DB builds the reset URL from the client-supplied Host → victim receives a link to the ATTACKER's domain embedding the GENUINE token → victim opens it (or their mail-security scanner dereferences it) → token leaks to the attacker → replayed on the real instance → new password set → full pre-auth admin account takeover

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Part-DB versions before 2.13.3. Fixed in 2.13.3.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Password-reset emails embed an absolute URL. Part-DB constructed that URL from the HTTP Host header of the incoming request — attacker-controlled — instead of a configured trusted base URL:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def build_reset_url(request):
    return f"https://{request.headers['Host']}/reset?token={token}"  # BUG

# Simplified fixed pattern
def build_reset_url_fixed(request, settings):
    if request.headers["Host"] not in settings.trusted_hosts:
        raise Reject("untrusted host")
    return f"https://{settings.base_url}/reset?token={token}"
The genuine token rides inside a link the attacker controls. Anything that trusts client-supplied headers to build security-sensitive URLs is vulnerable.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. Attacker sends a forgot-password request for a known account with Host: attacker.example in the headers.
  2. Part-DB emails the victim a reset link whose hostname is attacker.example — but whose token is genuine.
  3. The victim clicks the link (or their inbound mail-security scanner fetches it first).
  4. The attacker's server logs the request — leaking the valid token.
  5. The attacker replays the token against the real instance and sets a new password.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: security-sensitive URLs must be built from trusted configuration, not from client-supplied headers: the demo contrasts building a reset URL from the request Host with validating against an allowlist first. Offline, no server, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade now: Part-DB 2.13.3.
  • Validate the Host header against a trusted-host allowlist on every request — or build URLs from a configured base URL.
  • Invalidate password-reset tokens issued during the exposure window and rotate credentials.
  • Monitor for password-reset requests with unexpected Host headers.

docs.title: CVE-2026-8639: IBM Security Verify Directory Session Fixation
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH (8.8) CVSS vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Product IBM Security Verify Directory 10.0.0 through 10.0.4 and IBM Verify Directory 11.0.0 Vulnerability type Session Fixation (CWE-384)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: IBM Security Verify Directory 10.0.0 through 10.0.4 and IBM Verify Directory 11.0.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The directory server is vulnerable to session fixation: it does not reliably issue a fresh session identifier when a user authenticates. An attacker can establish a session first, trick a victim into logging in through that same session, and then hijack the now-authenticated session to gain unauthorized access to the directory management console.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo in poc.py models the safe login flow: the session identifier is regenerated (rotated) immediately after successful authentication, so any session id the attacker knew beforehand becomes useless. It runs locally.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update to the latest patched release from IBM (10.0.4.4 on the 10 line, 11.0.1.2 on the 11 line).
  • Invalidate all active sessions and force every user to log in again after patching.
  • Always rotate the session identifier on authentication and on privilege changes; never accept a pre-authentication session id after login.

docs.title: CVE-2026-86400 — Dell PowerProtect Data Domain: Unauthenticated Root Command Execution
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 Product Dell PowerProtect Data Domain — enterprise backup appliance (DD OS) Type Improper authentication (CWE-287) — authentication check can be bypassed remotely Vector Unauthenticated remote attacker reaches the appliance over the network → bypasses the authentication check → runs arbitrary commands with root privileges → full control of the backup system

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
DD OS Feature Release 7.7.1.0 through 8.8, LTS2024 7.13.1.0 through 7.13.1.80, LTS2025 8.3.1.0 through 8.3.1.40, LTS2026 8.6.1.0 through 8.6.1.20. Fixed in DD OS 8.9.0.0 or later, 7.13.1.90 or later, 8.3.1.50 or later, and 8.6.1.30 or later (Dell advisory DSA-2026-416). No active exploitation confirmed at publication.

DSA-2026-416 covers a cluster of related Data Domain flaws: CVE-2026-86397 (privileged account creation, 9.8), CVE-2026-86384 (hard-coded cryptographic key, 9.8) and CVE-2026-103780 (stack buffer overflow, 9.8) — all fixed by the same DD OS upgrade.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The appliance fails to verify who is calling before granting access. When an authentication check is missing on a privileged path, the system treats every remote request as trusted:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def handle_request(request):
    # BUG: no authentication check before privileged action
    return run_as_root(request.command)

# Simplified fixed pattern
def handle_request_fixed(request):
    if not request.is_authenticated():
        raise PermissionError("login required")
    return run_as_root(request.command)
Authentication must be verified before any privileged operation, never assumed from the fact that a request arrived.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
1. Attacker reaches the Data Domain appliance over the network — no account needed.
  2. A request hits a path whose authentication check is missing or bypassable.
  3. The appliance executes the supplied command with root privileges.
  4. The attacker creates privileged accounts, reads or wipes backups, and owns the system.

See poc.py for a safe, offline demo of an authentication gate that is never checked: the demo contrasts a privileged action executed blindly with the same action behind a verified login.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade now: DD OS 8.9.0.0 or later (or the patched LTS release for your branch: 7.13.1.90, 8.3.1.50, 8.6.1.30).
  • Restrict the appliance to trusted management networks — it must never be reachable from untrusted networks.
  • Audit admin accounts for any you did not create, and verify backups still restore.
  • Rotate credentials that may have been exposed on unpatched systems.

docs.title: CVE-2026-86471 (cluster CVE-2026-86471, CVE-2026-90800, CVE-2026-90797) — Apache CouchDB 3.5.3: Three Holes, One Upgrade
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.3 (v4.0; headliner); batch includes 8.1 and 7.7 Product Apache CouchDB — document database (JSON/HTTP API), widely used as a sync backend for mobile and web apps Type OS command injection via config (CWE-78), missing authorization (CWE-862), decompression bomb DoS (CWE-409) Vector Server admin → arbitrary shell commands as the couchdb OS user; any unauthenticated remote client → full read of system DBs or memory-exhaustion crash

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• Apache CouchDB 3.5.2 and earlier.
  • Fixed in CouchDB 3.5.3.

docs.title: The batch
docs.text: CVE CVSS Bug CVE-2026-86471 9.3 Unvalidated runtime configuration value → CouchDB server admin runs arbitrary shell commands as the couchdb OS user (CWE-78, E:A) CVE-2026-90800 8.1 Missing authorization checks in chttpd → any unauthenticated request reads the full contents of a prefixed _users/_replicator database (CWE-862) CVE-2026-90797 7.7 Unlimited gzip decompression routine in chttpd → any remote client triggers memory exhaustion, DoS (CWE-409)

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
A configuration value that can carry shell metacharacters flows into an OS command without validation; an authorization check is simply absent on a path variant (prefixed system databases); and a gzip reader expands input with no size cap. Three classic server-side failures in one release:

# Simplified vulnerable patterns
def apply_config_value(value):                       # CVE-2026-86471
    os.system(f"apply-setting {value}")              # shell metachars -> RCE

def read_system_db(db_name):                         # CVE-2026-90800
    if db_name.startswith(("_users", "_replicator")):
        return fetch_all(db_name)                    # no auth check on prefix variant

def gunzip(body):                                    # CVE-2026-90797
    return zlib.decompress(body, -15)                 # no size limit -> bomb

# Simplified fixed patterns
def apply_config_value_fixed(value):
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", value): raise ValueError()
    run(["apply-setting", value])                     # argument vector, no shell

def gunzip_fixed(body, max_bytes=10_000_000):
    d = zlib.decompressobj(-15)
    out = d.decompress(body, max_bytes)              # hard cap -> bomb defused

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. CVE-2026-86471: a CouchDB server admin sets a configuration value containing shell metacharacters; the server executes it, running attacker-chosen commands as the couchdb OS user.
  2. CVE-2026-90800: an unauthenticated client requests a prefixed _users or _replicator database path; the missing authorization check returns the entire database contents — user records, replication credentials.
  3. CVE-2026-90797: a remote client POSTs a tiny gzip payload that expands to gigabytes; the unbounded decompressor exhausts server memory and crashes the node.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the patterns safely: a decompression bomb guarded by an output-size cap on synthetic data, and config-value validation that rejects shell metacharacters — all synthetic, offline, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update now: Apache CouchDB to 3.5.3 or later immediately.
  • Audit any CouchDB server admin accounts and runtime config for unexpected values; block internet exposure of the database port and require authentication on every system database.

docs.title: CVE-2026-86596 — Remote Code Execution in s2Member for WordPress
docs.text: Field Value Severity CRITICAL — CVSS 9.8 Product s2Member plugin for WordPress, all versions up to and including 260927 Type Remote Code Execution (CWE-94) Vector Network, low complexity, low privileges required (custom-level access), no user interaction

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• All s2Member versions up to and including 260927.
  • Fixed in versions after 260927 — update immediately.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: s2Member's payment-notification handling sanitizes the attacker-controlled item_name value with strip_php_tags_deep(), which only removes literal <? sequences. The value is then embedded into an email template, and a later post-interpolation placeholder cleanup reassembles a valid <?php opener from the split pieces. The template is then executed as server-side code, so the attacker's payload runs on the WordPress host.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text: See poc.py: a local, side-effect-free illustration of a filter that strips a literal opener before embedding, followed by a cleanup step that accidentally reassembles it — contrasted with a fixed version that escapes values and never re-processes them as code.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update s2Member past version 260927 immediately.
  • Review PayPal notification logs for unusual item_name values.
  • Restrict who can hold custom-level accounts on the site.
  • Keep WordPress core, themes and plugins patched.

docs.title: Acronis Cyber Infrastructure: Missing Authorization Check Grants Anonymous Read and Write (CVE-2026-87095)
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.1 (v3.0) Product Acronis Cyber Infrastructure (ACI) before 6.0.1-112, 6.1.1-64, 6.2.1-71 (software-defined compute/storage/network for service providers) Type Incorrect authorization (CWE-863) — improper authorization checks Vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N — unauthenticated network request to the management API is treated as legitimate: sensitive information disclosed and infrastructure objects manipulated (C:H/I:H)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Acronis Cyber Infrastructure before build 6.0.1-112 (6.0 branch), before 6.1.1-64 (6.1 branch), before 6.2.1-71 (6.2 branch). Fixed in those builds.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The ACI management layer processes requests without checking who the caller is or what they are allowed to do. The authorization decision step is simply missing: instead of looking up the caller's privileges and denying unknown identities, the request flows straight into data reads and configuration changes. A plain network request — no password, no token, no user interaction — is treated as legitimate, so confidentiality and integrity of the whole cloud (backups, volumes, customer data, infrastructure objects) collapse at once.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def handle_api_request(request):
    # no identity lookup, no permission check — missing entirely
    return dispatch(request.action, request.payload)   # full access!

# Simplified fixed pattern
def handle_api_request_fixed(request):
    identity = authenticate(request)                  # who is calling?
    if not is_authorized(identity, request.action):   # allowed to do this?
        raise PermissionDenied("unauthorized")
    return dispatch(request.action, request.payload)

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. The attacker discovers a reachable ACI management endpoint (unauthenticated network access is all it takes).
  2. They send an ordinary API request — read storage objects, list backup manifests, then write to infrastructure objects. No credentials needed at any step.
  3. Because the authorization check is absent, reads disclose sensitive data (customer content, credentials, configuration) and writes silently alter volumes and service configuration.
  4. Anonymous access also means the activity can blend into unauthenticated log noise.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: authorization must happen per request, and internal reachability must never count as permission. Offline, no server, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update now: ACI to build 6.0.1-112, 6.1.1-64 or 6.2.1-71 (matching your branch).
  • Audit management API logs for anonymous/unexpected access and look for data access anomalies.
  • Isolate ACI management interfaces from the open network (allow-list trusted admin networks only).
  • Rotate credentials and keys that may have been exposed; verify volume and service configuration integrity.

docs.title: CVE-2026-87901 — phpBB Registration: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.3 (v3.1) Product phpBB — forum software (registration module) Type Cross-site scripting, reflected (CWE-79) — improper input sanitization Vector Attacker crafts a registration URL carrying a JavaScript payload → victim clicks the link → the registration module echoes the input back into the page unsanitized → the script executes in the victim's session context → session cookies stolen, account hijacked

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: phpBB (registration module). Update to the latest release containing the sanitization fix.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: User-controlled input was reflected into an HTML page without proper output encoding. The browser cannot distinguish the application's markup from attacker-supplied markup, so reflected input becomes executable script running with the victim's session privileges. Reflected XSS needs only a click - the payload never touches the database.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The vulnerable pattern, simplified:

// VULNERABLE - registration input echoed raw
$username = $_GET['username'];
echo "<p>Welcome, $username!</p>";   // <-- payload executes here

// FIXED - encode on output
echo "<p>Welcome, " . htmlspecialchars($username, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') . "!</p>";

The demo poc.py below contrasts raw echo vs encoded output on synthetic strings - no browser, no server, no real payloads.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Update phpBB to the latest release with the sanitization fix. Forum admins should audit the registration module (and other user-facing forms) for unsanitized echoes. Users: never register through links sent by strangers.

docs.title: CVE-2026-88900 — Apache Camel JGroups: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.8 Product Apache Camel camel-jgroups component (4.0.0 through 4.22.0) Type Deserialization of Untrusted Data (CWE-502) Vector A network-adjacent attacker joins the JGroups cluster and sends one crafted message — no login needed

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Apache Camel 4.0.0 through 4.22.0 (the camel-jgroups component). Fixed in 4.18.5, 4.22.1 and 4.23.0. Lines 4.14–4.17 and 4.19–4.21 are end of life — move to a supported release.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The JGroups consumer deserializes every incoming cluster message with a bare ObjectInputStream — no ObjectInputFilter allow-list. The default JGroups channel is unauthenticated UDP multicast, so anyone on the network can join the cluster and deliver an ObjectMessage. One crafted message triggers a Java deserialization gadget chain before Camel can inspect anything, giving remote code execution.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. Attacker joins the unauthenticated JGroups multicast channel on your network.
  2. Attacker sends one ObjectMessage carrying a serialized gadget chain.
  3. The consumer calls ObjectInputStream.readObject() with no filter.
  4. The gadget chain fires during deserialization — code runs with the app's privileges.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: an unfiltered "deserializer" that executes anything it is handed, versus a strict allow-list filter that rejects unknown classes. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Upgrade to Camel 4.18.5, 4.22.1 or 4.23.0 — these set a default ObjectInputFilter allow-list on the JGroups consumer. As defense in depth, set a JVM-wide serial filter with -Djdk.serialFilter (or jdk.serialFilter in java.security). Isolate the JGroups multicast traffic on a trusted network segment — the channel has no authentication of its own. Audit cluster membership and hunt for unexpected nodes.

docs.title: CVE-2026-88980-group: Kubeflow Pipelines Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH (8.6) / HIGH (8.6) CVSS vector CVE-2026-88980: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N CVSS vector CVE-2026-88981: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N Product Kubeflow Pipelines Vulnerability type Server-Side Request Forgery (CWE-918)

docs.title: Covered CVEs
docs.text:
• CVE-2026-88980 (HIGH 8.6, CWE-918): artifact fetch SSRF via caller-controlled HTTP(S) source, bucket, and key.
  • CVE-2026-88981 (HIGH 8.6, CWE-918): artifact download SSRF via caller-controlled S3/MinIO endpoints from workflow metadata.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Kubeflow Pipelines before 2.18.0 (fixed in 2.18.0).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The frontend artifact download path accepts caller-controlled destinations without requiring them to match operator-controlled storage configuration. The HTTP(S) artifact route accepts source=http or source=https with caller-controlled bucket and key values, and an all-digit decimal host is converted to an IPv4 address by the URL parser, so the default configuration lets an unauthenticated caller fetch internal HTTP resources and receive the response body. The S3/MinIO path accepts storage endpoints from workflow status metadata, so the shared interface pod can be made to connect to arbitrary reachable hosts and return response data, and requests may reveal an access-key identifier when signed with configured object-store credentials. Cloud credential disclosure depends on reachable metadata services and attached roles.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo in poc.py models the safe pattern: an artifact fetcher that only allows destinations matching the operator-configured storage allowlist, rejects decimal-IP hosts and metadata addresses, and refuses everything else. It never performs a real network request.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade Kubeflow Pipelines to 2.18.0 immediately.
  • Block access to cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. 169.254.169.254) from the frontend and UI pods.
  • Restrict artifact domains to operator-controlled storage via an explicit allowlist.
  • Audit logs for unusual artifact fetches and unexpected storage endpoints.

docs.title: CVE-2026-89079 — Theme My Login Unauthenticated Account Takeover
docs.text: Field Detail Severity Critical 9.8 (CVSS 3.1) Product "Theme My Login" plugin for WordPress, through 7.2.1 Type Missing identity validation → privilege escalation / account takeover Attack vector Network · no authentication required (multisite, certain configs)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Theme My Login through 7.2.1. Fixed in later releases.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The plugin's password-update routine never properly validates who is making the request:

function update_password($user, $new) {
    // missing: is the requester really $user?
    $user->set_password($new);   // done — for anyone who asks
}

Changing a password is one of the most sensitive actions possible, yet it is performed for an unauthenticated requester naming an arbitrary account.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
poc.py is an educational illustration of the missing check vs the fix. No real accounts, no network — pure logic demo.

python3 poc.py

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. Attacker (no account) POSTs a password change for admin.
  2. The plugin accepts it and swaps the password.
  3. Attacker logs in as administrator → full site compromise.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Theme My Login past 7.2.1 now.
  • Audit administrator accounts for unknown users.
  • Force a password reset for all users; enable two-factor authentication.

docs.title: CVE-2026-90910 — Apache Answer: Missing Authentication on the Reaction API
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 (CVSS 3.1) Product Apache Answer (Q&A platform) Type Missing Authentication for Critical Function (CWE-306) Vector Unauthenticated requests to the reaction API can read reaction metadata from restricted/private content, and add or remove reactions on it — content visibility controls were never enforced

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Apache Answer through 2.0.2. Fixed in 2.0.3.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The reaction API endpoints (likes and reactions on questions and answers) never called the content-visibility check that the rest of the platform enforces. Any unauthenticated user could list reaction metadata — including who reacted to what — on restricted or private content, and add or remove their own reactions to it. Reaction data is a window into what private questions exist and who is engaging with them.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. Attacker finds a target installation, no account needed.
  2. Requests the reaction endpoint for a question or answer ID.
  3. The API skips the visibility check and returns reaction metadata from private content.
  4. Attacker adds or removes reactions, manipulating engagement on content they cannot see.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a vulnerable mock versus the fixed pattern. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Upgrade to Apache Answer 2.0.3 immediately — every version through 2.0.2 is affected. Keep the instance off the public internet if it hosts private content. Audit reaction logs for anonymous adds/removes on restricted content.

docs.title: CVE-2026-91093 — HP One Agent: Privilege Escalation / Arbitrary Code Execution
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.5 (v4.0) Product HP One Agent — certain HP PC products Type Uncontrolled search path element (CWE-427) Vector Low-privileged local attacker plants a malicious library in a directory the agent searches before the legitimate location → when the privileged HP One Agent loads that library, attacker code runs with the agent's elevated privileges → full local privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution on the machine

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: HP One Agent on certain HP PC products. HP is releasing software updates to mitigate — see bulletin HPSBHF04150 for the affected product list and fixed versions.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The agent resolved a library or resource by searching a sequence of directories, and at least one of those directories was writable by a lower-privileged user and searched before the trusted location. This is the classic uncontrolled-search-path flaw: whoever controls the first directory searched controls what code the privileged process loads. Loaders must pin their dependencies to absolute, administrator-owned paths and never search user-writable directories first.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The vulnerable pattern, simplified:

# VULNERABLE - user-writable dir searched before the trusted one
SEARCH_PATH = ["/tmp/vendor/plugins", "/opt/vendor/lib"]

def load_library(name):
    for d in SEARCH_PATH:                      # attacker writes here first
        p = os.path.join(d, name)
        if os.path.exists(p):
            return dlopen(p)                   # privileged process loads it

# FIXED - pin to the administrator-owned absolute path
def load_library(name):
    return dlopen("/opt/vendor/lib/" + name)

The demo poc.py shows the search-order resolution with synthetic directories — no real libraries are loaded, nothing runs elevated.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Install the HP software update referenced in bulletin HPSBHF04150 as soon as it is available for your model. Until then, limit local accounts to trusted users, and monitor for unexpected files in directories the agent's components load from.

docs.title: CVE-2026-91403 — Oracle Java SE (JSSE): Unauthenticated Remote Compromise
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.1 Product Oracle Java SE (8u511, 11.0.33, 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5, 27.0.1), Oracle GraalVM for JDK (17.0.21, 21.0.13), Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition (21.3.20) Type JSSE (Java Secure Socket Extension / TLS) component flaw — remotely exploitable without authentication Vector Unauthenticated remote attacker → network access via multiple protocols → crafted data through APIs feeding JSSE → unauthorized creation, deletion, or modification of critical data

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• Oracle Java SE: 8u511, 8u511-perf, 11.0.33, 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5, 27.0.1
  • Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21, 21.0.13
  • Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20
  • Earlier unsupported releases are likely affected as well.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The vulnerability sits in JSSE, the component that implements TLS/SSL in the Java runtime. It is remotely exploitable without authentication over the network via multiple protocols. Oracle notes it can also be reached through APIs in the JSSE component — e.g. through a web service that supplies data to those APIs — and it applies to deployments (such as sandboxed Java Web Start / applet clients) that load untrusted code and rely on the Java sandbox for security. Successful attacks compromise the confidentiality and integrity of critical data:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def handle_network_input(data):
    jsse.process(data)          # unauthenticated, remote, low complexity
    # crafted input compromises the runtime ->
    # critical data: read, modified, deleted

# Simplified fixed pattern
def handle_network_input_fixed(data):
    apply_oracle_security_alert_patch()   # patched JSSE
    jsse.process(data)          # flaw addressed

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The attack chain, conceptually:

  1. Attacker has network access to a Java deployment — no credentials, no user interaction.
  2. Attacker sends crafted data over any affected protocol (or through a web service that feeds data into JSSE APIs).
  3. The JSSE component mishandles the input; the runtime is compromised.
  4. Attacker gains unauthorized creation, deletion, or modification access to critical data.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: an input pipeline where untrusted network data reaches a security component unvalidated versus one where the component is patched and input is handled safely — all synthetic, offline, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Apply the Security Alert patch now: follow Oracle's Patch Availability Document for CVE-2026-91403 for your Java SE / GraalVM version.
  • Upgrade unsupported releases: versions outside Premier/Extended Support are likely affected and untested — plan the upgrade.
  • Inventory Java deployments: JSSE is everywhere TLS is used; don't assume a service is safe because it sits behind a web tier.

docs.title: CVE-2026-92262 — MariaDB #mysql50# Table-Name Bypass
docs.text: Field Detail Severity Critical 9.9 (CVSS 3.1) Product MariaDB Server 10.6.1–10.6.27, 10.11.x–10.11.18, 11.4.x–11.4.12, 11.8.x–11.8.8, 12.3.x–12.3.2, 13.0.x–13.0.1 Type Filesystem encoding bypass → file read/write, crash, RCE Attack vector Network · low privileges (CREATE TABLE)

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
MariaDB encodes special table names so they map to harmless filenames on disk. But names starting with the legacy #mysql50# prefix skip that encoding entirely:

def encode_name(name):
    if name.startswith("#mysql50#"):
        return name          # legacy shortcut — no encoding!
    return safe_encode(name)

An attacker creates a table named #mysql50#../../<path> and the raw, unencoded name becomes a real filesystem path outside the data directory — readable and writable as the database user.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
poc.py is an educational illustration of the bypass vs the fix. It touches no database and writes no files.

python3 poc.py

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. Attacker (low DB privileges) runs CREATE TABLE \#mysql50#../../tmp/x` (...)`.
  2. The unencoded name escapes the data directory.
  3. Attacker reads/writes files as the mysql user: exfiltration, corruption, crashes — and potentially remote code execution.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update to a fixed release (10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3, or 13.0.2).
  • Restrict CREATE TABLE privileges (least privilege).
  • Audit existing schemas for table names starting with #mysql50#.

docs.title: TeamViewer: Your Remote Session Can Run Attacker Code
docs.text: Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test. | Field | Value | |---|---| | CVE | CVE-2026-92372 | | Severity | High — CVSS 8.8 (lead CVE of a TeamViewer batch) | | Product | TeamViewer Full Client and Host (Linux and macOS for the lead flaw; Windows also affected by sibling flaws) | | Type | Out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) in the screen-image decoder; batch siblings: CWE-190 integer overflow, CWE-367 TOCTOU, CWE-284/CWE-287/CWE-732 access-control and authentication flaws in installers, IPC, and update mechanisms | | Vector | During a remote-control session, crafted screen-image data reaches the viewer decoder, which writes past the destination image buffer. The same flaw can be triggered by persuading a user to open a specially crafted TeamViewer session recording (.tvs). Sibling flaws in the same batch let low-privilege local attackers climb to SYSTEM (Windows) or root (macOS) via installer staging, IPC impersonation, and update-mechanism tricks. |

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: TeamViewer Full Client for Linux and macOS prior to 15.83 (lead flaw); Full Client and Host prior to 15.82 (Windows installer/update siblings); Remote Management Monitoring prior to 26.10.1; Patch Management prior to 26.9.1. Update to the fixed versions above.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Screen data feels passive — just pixels. But decoding is code, and a decoder that trusts incoming sizes without verifying the destination hands the sender control of memory:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def decode_screen(data, buffer):
    buffer.write(data.pixels)  # BUG: destination bounds not checked

# Simplified fixed pattern
def decode_screen_fixed(data, buffer):
    if len(data.pixels) > buffer.capacity:
        return deny("malformed screen image")
    return buffer.write(data.pixels)
The session you trusted becomes the delivery channel, and the viewer becomes the target. The batch siblings show the same lesson in the installer and IPC layers: unguarded privileged helpers let a low-privilege local user reach SYSTEM or root.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational, conceptual demo only — it models the vulnerable pattern with synthetic, offline objects. It is not a working exploit and cannot be aimed at real systems.

  1. Attacker crafts screen-image data, or a rigged .tvs session recording.
  2. Victim connects to an attacker-controlled or compromised host, or opens the recording.
  3. The decoder writes past the image buffer, corrupting viewer memory.
  4. Code executes with the viewer's privileges. Separately, local batch flaws let low-privilege users escalate to SYSTEM/root via installers and IPC.

The demo in poc.py shows that incoming data sizes must be verified against the destination before any write: the demo contrasts an unchecked buffer write against a capacity-checked one.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update now: TeamViewer Full Client and Host to 15.83 or later (all platforms).
  • Update Remote Management Monitoring to 26.10.1 and Patch Management to 26.9.1.
  • Never open session recordings (.tvs) from untrusted senders.
  • Audit unattended machines first — they are the ones nobody checks.
  • Inventory all endpoints running TeamViewer, including servers and support workstations.

docs.title: CVE-2026-92698-group: FastNetMon Out-of-Bounds Reads (Packet Parser)
docs.text: Field Value Severity HIGH (8.2) CVSS vector CVE-2026-92698: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:H Product FastNetMon Vulnerability type Out-of-bounds Read (CWE-125)

docs.title: Covered CVEs
docs.text:
• CVE-2026-92693 (HIGH 8.2, CWE-125): IPv6 fragment header dereferenced without verifying the 8-byte Fragment header remains.
  • CVE-2026-92695 (HIGH 8.2, CWE-125): live pcap callback dereferences headers beyond captured bytes (caplen unchecked).
  • CVE-2026-92697 (HIGH 7.5, CWE-125): NetFlow v9 collector out-of-bounds read.
  • CVE-2026-92698 (HIGH 8.2, CWE-125): sFlow header_size trusted as captured length, defeating nested parser bounds checks.
  • CVE-2026-93424 (HIGH 7.5, CWE-125): sFlow template lookup out-of-bounds read.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: FastNetMon 1.2.9 and earlier. No fixed release is available as of this writing.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The shared packet parser trusts attacker-controlled length fields and dereferences headers without first verifying the bytes are actually present in the buffer. A crafted sFlow v5 RAW_PACKET_HEADER record can reach the parser with the Fragment bytes omitted; a short captured frame or an attacker-controlled IPv4 header length can make the live pcap callback read past the captured bytes; and an inflated header_size in a flow sample creates a false end pointer beyond the received buffer, defeating the nested parser's bounds checks. All five flaws share the same root cause: lengths treated as facts instead of claims. The result is an unauthenticated remote out-of-bounds read and, in most variants, process termination, with possible limited exposure of adjacent bytes through parsed flow fields.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The demo in poc.py models the safe pattern: a packet parser that compares every claimed length against the bytes actually remaining in the buffer before dereferencing any header, and drops the packet when the claim exceeds what was received. It never processes real network traffic.

See poc.py in this folder. Educational only: the demo illustrates the vulnerable pattern's safe counterpart and performs no exploitation. Only test in controlled environments against systems you own or are authorized to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Accept sFlow, NetFlow, and packet-capture data only from trusted senders; segment sensor interfaces away from untrusted networks.
  • Monitor the sensor process with automatic restarts and crash alerts, since there is no fixed release yet.
  • Apply the upstream fixes the moment a fixed release lands.
  • Restrict who can reach the FastNetMon management and collector ports.

docs.title: CVE-2026-92798 — User Registration & Membership: Arbitrary Shortcode Execution
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.1 Product WordPress plugin user-registration (User Registration & Membership) Type Code Injection via shortcode execution (CWE-94) Vector Low-privilege authenticated user → arbitrary shortcode execution

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: User Registration & Membership versions up to and including 5.2.8. Fixed in the release after 5.2.8.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
In UR_Smart_Tags::process(), the referrer_url branch takes attacker-influenced input and passes it into shortcode execution without sufficient sanitization. WordPress shortcodes are executable code, so any shortcode the attacker supplies runs inside the site with the plugin's privileges.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
$input = $_GET['referrer_url'];      // attacker-influenced
echo do_shortcode($input);           // executed unsanitized

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. A low-privilege user (e.g. a subscriber) crafts a registration request whose referrer_url value contains an arbitrary shortcode.
  2. The plugin's smart-tag processor reaches the referrer_url branch and feeds the value to the shortcode engine.
  3. The shortcode executes server-side — data reads, content injection, or a stepping stone toward privilege escalation.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock smart-tag processor that executes raw input versus a fixed one that sanitizes and allow-lists shortcode tags. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update User Registration & Membership past 5.2.8 immediately.
  • Audit recent subscriber registrations for suspicious activity.
  • Scan content for unknown or unexpected shortcodes.
  • Review server logs for crafted referrer_url values hitting the registration endpoints.

docs.title: CVE-2026-92885 — Qode Membership: Authentication Bypass via Facebook Login Typo
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 (v3.1) Product Qode Membership plugin for WordPress — member login/registration with social (Facebook) login Type Improper authentication (CWE-287) — Facebook OAuth token verification bypassed by a mistyped variable Vector Unauthenticated attacker takes a public login nonce from any page with the [qode_user_login] or [qode_user_register] shortcode, then sends a qode_membership_check_facebook_user request naming an existing login (e.g. an administrator). The token-verification guard tests an undefined variable, so its check always passes and no token is verified — WordPress then issues a session cookie for that account.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Qode Membership versions up to and including 2.0.6.2. Fixed in 2.0.6.3.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The Facebook login handler is supposed to verify the OAuth token before signing anyone in. A typographic error in the guard tests a variable name that does not exist, so the emptiness check always answers true and the verification branch becomes dead code:

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def login_from_facebook(request):
    if empty(check_social_useqoder):  # BUG: mistyped name, undefined
        return issue_session(request.login)  # token never verified

# Simplified fixed pattern
def login_from_facebook_fixed(request):
    if empty(check_social_user):       # real variable, actually tested
        return verify_facebook_token(request.token)  # proof required
    return issue_session(request.login)
A guard that tests the wrong name is no guard at all — and in this language, asking about an undefined variable quietly answers "empty", so the gate stood open while looking closed.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. Attacker visits any public page carrying the login or register shortcode and copies the public login nonce.
  2. Attacker sends a Facebook-login request naming an existing account login, such as an administrator's.
  3. The mistyped guard passes without any token verification.
  4. WordPress issues a session cookie for the named account — full account takeover.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a login guard must test a real, defined value: the demo contrasts checking a mistyped name (always passes) with checking the real variable (token actually verified). Offline, no server, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade now: Qode Membership 2.0.6.3 or newer.
  • Audit administrator logins for sessions you cannot explain.
  • Force password resets for administrator accounts.
  • Review member accounts for new administrators or unexpected changes.

docs.title: CVE-2026-93475 (cluster CVE-2026-93475, CVE-2026-92843, CVE-2026-92853) — Eclipse ThreadX NetX Secure: Three Pre-Auth Parser Bugs in IoT TLS
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.3 (v4.0; headliner); batch includes two 8.7s Product Eclipse ThreadX NetX Secure (NetX Duo) — TLS/X.509 stack of Azure RTOS, embedded in IoT and industrial devices Type Out-of-bounds write (CWE-787/1284), out-of-bounds reads (CWE-125), integer underflow (CWE-191) — all in certificate parsers Vector Pre-authentication remote attacker: a malicious TLS server (or network MITM) sends crafted certificates during the handshake → memory corruption on the device

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: • Eclipse ThreadX NetX Secure (netxduo) — affected versions per the GitHub security advisories; update to the patched release linked in each advisory.

docs.title: The batch
docs.text: CVE CVSS Bug CVE-2026-93475 9.3 X.509 parser accepts an RSA public key of any size, but signature verification decrypts into fixed-size buffers dimensioned for the 4096-bit default → out-of-bounds write past a file-scope static during chain verification (CWE-787/1284) CVE-2026-92843 8.7 Missing bounds check in the TLS 1.3 Certificate-message parser → malicious server triggers unsigned-integer underflow → heap out-of-bounds read, pre-authentication during the handshake (CWE-125) CVE-2026-92853 8.7 TLS 1.3 Certificate parser decrements the message length to skip a context byte without checking one exists → a zero-length Certificate message wraps the length to 0xFFFFFFFF, the bounds check becomes vacuous, and the parser reads past the packet buffer — a four-byte trigger (CWE-125/191)

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Embedded parsers trust message-declared lengths and do arithmetic before validating: a buffer sized for the default case meets an attacker-chosen larger case, and a length decrement happens before the existence check, so unsigned wraparound defeats the bounds test. Certificate parsing is the worst possible place for this — it runs before authentication, against a remote peer:

# Simplified vulnerable patterns
def verify_rsa_signature(modulus):                    # CVE-2026-93475
    buf = bytearray(512)                              # sized for 4096-bit default
    buf[:len(modulus)] = modulus                      # bigger key -> OOB write

def parse_cert_message(length):                       # CVE-2026-92843
    remaining = length - header_size                  # underflows if length < header
    return packet[0:remaining]                        # huge length -> OOB read

def parse_cert_v2(length):                            # CVE-2026-92853
    length = (length - 1) & 0xFFFFFFFF                # zero-length -> 0xFFFFFFFF
    if length <= packet_size:                         # check is now vacuous
        return packet[0:length]                       # reads past the buffer

# Simplified fixed patterns
def verify_rsa_signature_fixed(modulus):
    if len(modulus) > 512: raise ValueError()        # key size must fit the buffer

def parse_cert_fixed(length):
    if length < header_size: raise ValueError()      # validate BEFORE arithmetic
    remaining = length - header_size

def parse_cert_v2_fixed(length):
    if length == 0: raise ValueError()               # check existence first
    length -= 1

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. The attacker's malicious TLS server (or a network position) starts a handshake with a vulnerable ThreadX device.
  2. It sends a crafted X.509 chain with an oversized RSA modulus (CVE-2026-93475) — signature verification writes past a static buffer.
  3. Or it sends a TLS 1.3 Certificate message with a length smaller than the header (CVE-2026-92843) or a zero-length message (CVE-2026-92853) — unsigned arithmetic wraps and the parser reads heap memory it shouldn't.
  4. All three fire before authentication, remotely, against headless devices that rarely get patched.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: the unsigned-integer wraparound of length - 1 on a zero-length message, shown with pure Python integer arithmetic and a bounds-check model — synthetic, offline, no packets, no exploit.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update now: NetX Duo / NetX Secure to the patched release in the advisories; rebuild and redeploy device firmware.
  • Inventory IoT/OT devices running Azure RTOS TLS; segment device networks and treat unpatchable devices as untrusted endpoints.

docs.title: CVE-2026-93489 — ASUS Routers: Forged Access Tickets Without a Password
docs.text: Field Value Severity Under analysis — NVD has not published a CVSS score yet; unauthenticated admin operations Product ASUS router firmware — router modules shipping on models since 2018 Type Improper authentication (CWE-287) — forged access ticket accepted Vector Unauthenticated nearby user sends a crafted HTTP request → the router mints or accepts a forged access ticket → the attacker performs administrator operations with no password

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: ASUS router firmware before the October 2026 security update. See the ASUS Security Advisory 'Security Update for ASUS Router Firmware' for the fixed build per model.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: The ticket mechanism trusts a value the attacker can forge instead of verifying it against server-side session state. Authentication that can be minted client-side is not authentication.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The vulnerable pattern, simplified:

// VULNERABLE - ticket trusted without server-side verification
GET /admin.cgi?action=reboot&ticket=<attacker-forged-value>
// router: "ticket looks plausible" -> admin action runs

// FIXED - tickets are random, server-issued, and verified server-side
GET /admin.cgi?action=reboot
Cookie: session=<random 256-bit token bound to a server-side session>

Ticket-forging flaws are devastating on routers: the device is always on, always reachable on the LAN, and compromise means traffic interception.

Educational material only. Do not use against systems you do not own or have explicit permission to test.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text: Install the ASUS router firmware security update immediately (check the ASUS Security Advisory for your model's fixed build). After updating, review admin logs for unrecognized sessions and change the admin password.
